children.translated_text: <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> (Ornament of Mahāyāna Sūtras)
<s>Oṃ</s>
Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.
First chapter:

children.text: arthajño 'rthavibhāvanāṃ prakurute vācā padaiścāmalair duḥkhasyottaraṇāya duḥkhitajane kāruṇyatastanmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows the meaning sets forth the elucidation of meaning through speech and stainless words, out of compassion for suffering beings, for the crossing over of suffering, being absorbed in that.

children.text: dharmasyottamayānadeśitavidheḥ satveṣu tadgāmiṣu śliṣṭāmarthagatiṃ niruttaragataṃ pañcātmikāṃ darśayan // MSA_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Showing to beings who are headed toward it the well-connected course of meaning, the unsurpassed path of fivefold nature, in the method of the supreme vehicle taught as <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 1.1 //

children.text: ghaṭitamiva suvarṇaṃ vārijaṃ vā vibuddhaṃ sukṛtamiva subhojyaṃ bhujyamānaṃ kṣudhārtaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Like refined gold, or a lotus fully opened, like a fine meal being eaten by the hungry,

children.text: vidita iva sulekho ratnapeṭeva muktā vivṛta iha sa dharmaḥ prītimagryāṃ dadhāti // MSA_1.2 //
children.translated_text: like a well-known good letter, like a pearl in a jewel-casket — the <s>Dharma</s> thus disclosed here bestows the highest joy. // MSA 1.2 //

children.text: yathā bimbaṃ bhūṣāprakṛtiguṇavaddarpaṇagataṃ viśiṣṭaṃ prāmodyaṃ janayati nṛṇāṃ darśanavaśāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a reflection in a mirror, possessing the natural qualities of an ornament, produces extraordinary delight in people through the power of seeing,

children.text: tathā dharmaḥ sūktaprakṛtiguṇayukto 'pi satataṃ vibhaktārthastuṣṭiṃ janayati viśiṣṭāmiha satām // MSA_1.3 //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Dharma</s>, even though endowed with the natural qualities of well-spoken [words], constantly produces distinguished satisfaction here among the wise, its meaning having been distinguished. // MSA 1.3 //
Just as a medicine that is pungent when smelled but sweet in taste — likewise,

children.text: dharma[rmo] dvayavyavasthā[stho] vyañjanato 'rtho na ca[rthataśca] jñeyaḥ // MSA_1.4 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>, established in both [aspects], should be known by its expression as meaning, and by its meaning [as expression]. // MSA 1.4 //
Like a king, this <s>Dharma</s> is difficult to approach, being vast, deep, and profound.
But when approached, like [a king], it becomes the bestower of excellent qualities and wealth. // MSA 1.5 //
Just as a gem of fine quality and great value does not please those who are not connoisseurs,
so too this <s>Dharma</s> does not please the unwise; but conversely, it delights [the wise] likewise. // MSA 1.6 //
Because of non-elucidation at the beginning, because of equal application, because of being beyond the range [of ordinary minds], because of the accomplishment,
because of the [apparent] absence in existence, because of the contradictory, because of the rapid and the other. // MSA 1.7 //
The <s>Buddhas</s>, having direct vision and being protectors of the teaching,
whose knowledge is unobstructed and uncovered — indifference [toward beings] is not fitting for them. // MSA 1.8 //
Because of deficiency, because of contradiction, because of being not the means, and also because of non-instruction —
this is not the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle but is called the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>. // MSA 1.9 //
Because of the contradiction of intention, instruction, practice,

children.text: upastambhasya kālasya yat hīnaṃ hīnameva tat // MSA_1.10 //
children.translated_text: support, and time — what is inferior is indeed inferior. // MSA 1.10 //
From its own descent, from seeing its own discipline,
from its profundity and its vastness — the nature of <s>Dharma</s> is not contradicted. // MSA 1.11 //
Dependent, indeterminate, non-pervasive, conventional, and subject to weariness —

children.text: bālāśrayo matastarkastasyāto viṣayo na tat // MSA_1.12 //
children.translated_text: reasoning is considered to depend on the immature; therefore, that [<s>Dharma</s>] is not its domain. // MSA 1.12 //
From profundity and from vastness, ripening and non-conceptualization,

children.text: deśanā'to dvayasyāsmin sa copāyo niruttare // MSA_1.13 //
children.translated_text: and the teaching of both herein — that is the means in the unsurpassed [vehicle]. // MSA 1.13 //
That groundless fear arises in worldly beings, causing burning, because of producing a great mass of demerit over a long period.

children.text: agotro 'sanmitro 'kṛtamatirapūrvā'citaśubhasrasatyasmin dharme patati mahato 'rthādgata iha // MSA_1.14 //
children.translated_text: One without [spiritual] lineage, without true friends, of uncultivated mind, without prior accumulated merit — such a one falls away from this <s>Dharma</s> of great purpose, having departed [from it]. // MSA 1.14 //

Because of the absence of the other, because of the supreme profundity, because of following, because of the narration of diverse [matters], because of the connection with definitive statement of many aspects,

children.text: yathākhyānaṃ nārthādbhagavati ca bhāvātigahanāt na dharme 'smiṃsrāso bhavati viduṣāṃ yonivicayāt // MSA_1.15 //
children.translated_text: because of the statement as it is and not from [mere] meaning, and because of the extremely profound devotion to the Lord — in this <s>Dharma</s>, there is no fear for the wise, due to the investigation of its source. // MSA 1.15 //

children.text:
śrutaṃ niśrityādau prabhavati manaskāra iha yo
manaskārājñānaṃ prabhavati ca tatvārthaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: First, depending on what is heard, mental attention arises here; from mental attention, knowledge arises concerning the reality of the object of truth.

children.text: yadā pratyātmaṃ sā kathamasati tasminvyavasitiḥ // MSA_1.16 //
children.translated_text: when [the realization] is personal, how can there be conviction in its absence? // MSA 1.16 //
Then from that, the attainment of <s>Dharma</s> arises; and in that, the one who delights in wisdom —

children.text: ahaṃ na boddhā na gabhīraboddhā buddhau gabhīraṃ kimatarkagamyam /
children.translated_text: 'I am not an understander, nor an understander of the profound; what in <s>Buddha</s>-nature is profound and beyond reasoning?

children.text: kasmād gabhīrārthavidāṃ na mokṣa ityetaduttrāsapadaṃ na yuktam // MSA_1.17 //
children.translated_text: Why is there no liberation for those who know the profound meaning?' — this ground for alarm is not justified. // MSA 1.17 //

children.text: hīnādhimuktaḥ sunihīnadhātor hī naiḥ sahāyaiḥ parivāritasya /
children.translated_text: For one of inferior aspiration, of very inferior nature, surrounded by inferior companions —
if there is no faith in this <s>Dharma</s> taught with vastness and profundity — that is established [as natural]. // MSA 1.18 //

children.text: śrutānusāreṇa hi buddhimattaṃ labdhvā'śrute yaḥ prakarotyavajñām /
children.translated_text: For one who, having gained intelligence by following what is heard, shows contempt for what is not heard —

children.text: śrute vicitre sati cāprameye śiṣṭe kuto niścayameti mūḍhaḥ // MSA_1.19 //
children.translated_text: when what is heard is diverse and immeasurable and well-established, how can the fool arrive at certainty? // MSA 1.19 //
When meaning is imagined regarding what is not [truly] heard, one's own conviction suffers loss of intelligence,

children.text: svākhyātatāṃ ca kṣipati kṣatiṃ ca prāpnoti dharme pratighāvatīva[pratighātameva] // MSA_1.20 //
children.translated_text: and one casts away the well-expounded nature [of the teaching] and suffers damage in the <s>Dharma</s>, as if struck by hostility. // MSA 1.20 //
The defilement of the mind that is naturally defiled and of improper form —

children.text: prāgeva saṃdehagatasya dharme tasmādupekṣaiva varaṃ hyadoṣā // MSA_1.21 //
children.translated_text: all the more for one already in doubt regarding the <s>Dharma</s>; therefore, equanimity alone is better, being without fault. // MSA 1.21 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the first chapter on the establishment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
Second chapter:
Verse summarizing the distinctive features of going for refuge:

children.text: ratnāni yo hi śaraṇapragato 'tra yāne jñeyaḥ sa eva paramaḥ śaraṇa[ṇaṃ] gatānām /
children.translated_text: One who has gone for refuge to the [Three] Jewels in this vehicle is to be known as the supreme among those who have gone for refuge.
Through the fourfold distinction of meaning — characterized by all-pervasiveness, acceptance, attainment, and mastery. // MSA 2.1 //

children.text: yasmādādau duṣkara eṣa vyavasāyo duḥsādho 'sau naikasahasrairapi kalpaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since this resolve is difficult at first, since it is hard to accomplish even in many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: siddho yasmātsattvahitādhānamahārthas tasmādagre yāna ihāgraśaraṇārthaḥ // MSA_2.2 //
children.translated_text: since its accomplishment is of great purpose, being the basis of benefit for beings — therefore, the vehicle here is foremost, [worthy of] the highest refuge. // MSA 2.2 //

children.text: sarvān sattvāṃstārayituṃ yaḥ pratipanno yano jñāne sarvagate kauśalyayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who has set out to ferry across all beings, who is endowed with skill in all-pervading knowledge,

children.text: yo nirvāṇe saṃsaraṇe 'pyekaraso 'sau [saṃsṛtiśāntyekaraso 'sau] jñeyo dhīmāneṣa hi sarvatraga evam // MSA_2.3 //
children.translated_text: who is of one flavor in both <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s> — that wise one should be known as truly all-pervading. // MSA 2.3 //
Having gone to this refuge of great purpose, one attains an immeasurable increase of the multitude of qualities.

children.text: sphurati jagadidaṃ kṛpāśayena prathayati cāpratimaṃ mahā[rdhaṃ]dharmam // MSA_2.4 //
children.translated_text: With a compassionate mind, one illuminates this world and proclaims the incomparable, great <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 2.4 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the second chapter on going for refuge.
Third chapter:
Verse summarizing the distinctions of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage):
The supremacy of beings, the nature, the marks, the distinctions of <s>gotra</s>,
the disadvantages, the benefits, and the twofold analogy — [these are] fourfold. // MSA 3.1 //
From the distinction of dispositions (<s>dhātu</s>), aspirations (<s>adhimukti</s>), and practices,
and from the observation of distinction in results — the existence of <s>gotra</s> is ascertained. // MSA 3.2 //
In terms of supremacy, universality, great purpose, and inexhaustibility
of the wholesome — because of being its cause, the supremacy of <s>gotra</s> is established. // MSA 3.3 //

children.text: prakṛtyā paripuṣṭaṃ ca āśrayaścāśritaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: By nature and as nurtured, it is both the basis and what is based;
it should be known as both existent and non-existent, for the purpose of bringing forth [its] qualities. // MSA 3.4 //
Compassion, aspiration, patience, and initial practice,
right conduct, and [accumulation] of the wholesome — these are ascertained as the marks of the <s>gotra</s>. // MSA 3.5 //
The <s>gotra</s> is determinate and indeterminate, incorruptible and corruptible;
this distinction of <s>gotra</s> is, in brief, fourfold. // MSA 3.6 //
Habitual afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), bad companionship, poverty, and dependence on others —
these should be known, in brief, as the four disadvantages of <s>gotra</s>. // MSA 3.7 //
Quick departure from the lower realms, swift liberation therein,
slight experience of suffering, and stirring [others] with urgency toward the ripening of beings. // MSA 3.8 //
Like the lineage of gold, it should be known as the basis of immeasurable wholesomeness,
and as the foundation for the powers of knowledge, purity, concentration, and noble [qualities]. // MSA 3.9 //
Like the lineage of precious gems, it should be known — because of being the cause of great awakening,
because of its foundation in great knowledge, <s>samādhi</s>, noble [qualities], and the purpose of great beings. // MSA 3.10 //
Some are absolutely [fixed] in wrongdoing; some have eradicated their wholesome roots;
some possess wholesome [qualities] not leading to liberation; some are of inferior wholesomeness and without cause. // MSA 3.11 //

children.text: gāmbhīryaudāryavāde parahitakaraṇāyodite dīrghadharme ajñātvaivādhimuktirbhavati suvipulā saṃprapattikṣamā ca /
children.translated_text: In the teaching of the profound and vast, proclaimed for the benefit of others as the long-lasting <s>Dharma</s> — without even knowing, aspiration arises, vast and capable of realization;

children.text: saṃpattiścāvasāne dvayagataparamā yadbhavatyeva teṣāṃ tajjñeyaṃ bodhisattvaprakṛtiguṇavatastatprapuṣṭācca gotrāt // MSA_3.12 //
children.translated_text: and at the end, the supreme attainment of both [merit and wisdom] arises in them — this should be known as being from the <s>gotra</s> endowed with the natural qualities of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> and fully nurtured. // MSA 3.12 //
For the growth of the tree of awakening of vast and excellent qualities, and for the attainment of wealth, happiness, the cessation of suffering,
because of the fruitfulness of actions for one's own and others' benefit and happiness — this <s>gotra</s> is supreme [and well-rooted]. // MSA 3.13 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the third chapter on <s>gotra</s>.
Fourth chapter:
Verse on the characteristics of the generation of the mind [of awakening]:
Of great enthusiasm, great undertaking, for a great purpose, and of great arising —
the volition of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, for the purpose of both [self and others], is the arising of the mind [of awakening]. // MSA 4.1 //
That generation of the mind [of awakening] is [first] through aspiration; the next is through pure superior intention;
on the [Bodhisattva] stages, it is considered maturational, and likewise free from obstructions. // MSA 4.2 //
It is desired as rooted in compassion, always intending the benefit of beings,
aspiring toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and having as its object the search for the knowledge thereof. // MSA 4.3 //
It is [characterized by] higher aspiration, vehicle [commitment], foundation in moral restraint (<s>śīla</s> and <s>saṃvṛti</s>),
the arising [against] the adversary, resistance, and patient endurance. // MSA 4.4 //
Its benefit is the increase of the wholesome; for it consists of merit and knowledge.
It is always said to be the engagement in the <s>Pāramitās</s> and the way of going forth. // MSA 4.5 //
It culminates in the [Bodhisattva] stages, through the practice appropriate to each;
the determination of the mind-generation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood [thus]. // MSA 4.6 //
Through the power of a [spiritual] friend, the power of the cause, the power of the root, the power of hearing, and the practice of the wholesome —
the generation of the mind is said to be of unstable and stable arising, according to the declaration of others. // MSA 4.7 //
Having well attended upon the perfectly awakened ones, having well accumulated the accumulations of knowledge and merit,
from the arising of non-conceptual knowledge regarding phenomena — its supremacy [is established]. // MSA 4.8 //

children.text: dharmeṣu ca satveṣu ca tatkṛtyeṣūttame ca buddhatve /
children.translated_text: Regarding phenomena, beings, their activities, and the supreme <s>Buddhahood</s> —
from the equal-minded apprehension, its distinction as [generating] supreme joy [is established]. // MSA 4.9 //
The vastness of its birth, the enthusiasm therein, the purity of intention,

children.text: kauśalyaṃ pariśiṣṭe niryāṇaṃ caiva vijñeyam // MSA_4.10 //
children.translated_text: skill in what remains, and the going forth — these should be known. // MSA 4.10 //
Born from the seed of aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s>, from the supreme mother of the <s>Pāramitās</s>,

children.text: dhyānamaye sukhagarbhe karuṇā saṃvardhikā dhātrī // MSA_4.11 //
children.translated_text: in the blissful womb of meditative absorption (<s>dhyāna</s>), compassion is the nurse who nourishes. // MSA 4.11 //
Vastness should be known from the accomplishment of the ten great aspirational vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>);
enthusiasm should be understood from the unwearied [performance of] difficult and long-lasting deeds. // MSA 4.12 //
From the awakening close to [full] awakening, and from obtaining the knowledge of its means —
the purity of intention should be known; skill, however, pertains to other stages. // MSA 4.13 //
The going forth should be known through the mental attention of proper establishment;
from the knowledge of that conceptualization, and through the non-conceptualization of that very [thing]. // MSA 4.14 //
The [first] generation is like the earth; the next is like excellent gold;
like the bright new moon, and another like fire, [should be known] as increasing. // MSA 4.15 //
Again, another is like a great treasure; another is like a mine of jewels;
one should be known as like the ocean; another is like a diamond; and another like the moon. // MSA 4.16 //
Another should be known as like the king of medicines; another resembles a great friend;
another shines like a wish-fulfilling gem; another should be known as like the sun. // MSA 4.17 //
Another is like a sweet <s>Gandharva</s>-song; another should be known as like a king;
another is like a storehouse; and yet another is like a great highway. // MSA 4.18 //
One should be known as like a vehicle; and another like a spring — the arising of the mind.
Another resembles the sound of joy; and another is like the current of a great river. // MSA 4.19 //
And another is like a cloud — thus is the mind-generation of the children of the <s>Jinas</s>.

children.text: tasmāttathā guṇāḍhyaṃ cittaṃ muditaiḥ samutpādyam // MSA_4.20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, such a mind, rich in qualities, should be generated with joy. // MSA 4.20 //
From the mind [directed toward] the benefit of others, from the attainment of its means, from the great resolve, and from seeing the excellent truth of meaning —

children.text: mahārhacittodayavarjitā janāḥ śamaṃ gamiṣyanti vihāya tatsukham // MSA_4.21 //
children.translated_text: those who lack the arising of this precious mind will reach cessation, having abandoned that happiness. // MSA 4.21 //
From the simultaneous arising of the excellent mind of the wise one, the mind is well-restrained from infinite wrongdoing.

children.text: sukhena duḥkhena ca modate sadā śubhī kṛpāluśca vivardhana, dvayam // MSA_4.22 //
children.translated_text: The virtuous one, compassionate and ever-growing, always rejoices in both happiness and suffering. MSA 4.22
When, without regard for his own body and life, he undertakes the highest exertion for the sake of others,

children.text: paropaghātena tathāvidhaḥ kathaṃ sa duṣkṛte karmaṇi saṃpravatsyati // MSA_4.23 //
children.translated_text: how could such a one, through harming others, engage in sinful action? MSA 4.23
Seeing all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) as illusion-like, and births as mere festival-processions,

children.text: kleśācca duḥkhācca bibheti nāsau saṃpattikāle 'tha vipattikāle // MSA_4.24 //
children.translated_text: he fears neither <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) nor suffering, whether in times of prosperity or adversity. MSA 4.24

children.text: svakā guṇāḥ sattvahitācca modaḥ saṃcintyajanmarddhivikurvitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: His own virtues, delight in the welfare of beings, intentional birth, prosperity, and magical creation,
adornment, nourishment, the foremost stage, play and delight — these belong to those whose nature is perpetual compassion. MSA 4.25
For one compassionate in nature, striving for the welfare of others, even <s>Avīci</s> (the deepest hell) becomes pleasant,

children.text: kutaḥ punastrasyati tādṛśo bhavan parāśrayairduḥkhasamudbhavairbhave // MSA_4.26 //
children.translated_text: how much less would such a one be terrified of sufferings arising from dependence on others in [worldly] existence? MSA 4.26
For one endowed with great compassion, whose nature is that of a teacher, who is afflicted in mind by the sufferings of others,

children.text: parasya kṛtye samupasthite punaḥ paraiḥ samādāpanato 'tilajjanā // MSA_4.27 //
children.translated_text: when the task for another's [benefit] presents itself, there is intense shame at being prompted by others [to do it]. MSA 4.27
One who has placed upon his head the burden of supreme beings does not shine if he proceeds with faltering gait as a foremost being;
bound by the manifold bonds of self and others, he should exert himself a hundredfold. MSA 4.28
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fourth chapter on the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind).
Fifth chapter.
Verse on the characteristic of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>).
The practice of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) is held to consist of a great foundation, undertaking, fruition, and arising;
it is always characterized by great giving, great forbearance, and the accomplishment and performance of great purposes. MSA 5.1
Having attained in the next [life] a mind equal to one's own [in others], or even one more excellent and desirable than one's own [in others],

children.text: tathātmano 'nyārthaviśiṣṭasaṃjñinaḥ svakārthatā kā katamā parārthatā // MSA_5.2 //
children.translated_text: for one who considers himself as [existing for] another's purpose, what is self-interest and what is the interest of others? MSA 5.2

children.text: paratra loko na tathātinirdayaḥ pravartate tāpanakarmaṇāripau /
children.translated_text: In the other [world], people do not act so mercilessly in tormenting their enemy with painful deeds,

children.text: yathā parārthaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhatāpane kṛpātmakaḥ svātmani saṃpravartate // MSA_5.3 //
children.translated_text: as a compassionate one inflicts intense suffering-torment upon himself for the sake of others. MSA 5.3
For those established in inferior, middling, and superior <s>dharma</s>: excellent teaching, attracting, and causing entry;
discipline in [their specific] purpose, maturation in virtue, and likewise, instruction, establishment, understanding, and liberation. MSA 5.4
Likewise, the attainment of distinguished qualities, noble birth, prophecy, and consecration;

children.text: tathāgatajñānamanuttaraṃ padaṃ parārtha eṣa tryadhiko daśātmakaḥ // MSA_5.5 //
children.translated_text: the unsurpassed knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the supreme state — this [practice] for others' benefit is tenfold plus three. MSA 5.5
Teaching suited to the audience and not contrary, without arrogance, without conceit, discerning,

children.text: kṣamā ca dāntā ca sudūragā'kṣayā jinātmajānāṃ pratipattiruttamā // MSA_5.6 //
children.translated_text: patient, self-controlled, far-reaching, inexhaustible — such is the supreme practice of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. MSA 5.6

children.text: mahābhaye kāmijanaḥ pravartate cale viparyāsasukhe bhavapriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The pleasure-seeker engages in great danger; the lover of existence [delights] in unstable, perverted happiness;

children.text: pratisvamādhipraśame śamapriyaḥ sadā tu sarvādhiga[śa]me kṛpātmakaḥ // MSA_5.7 //
children.translated_text: the peace-lover [delights] in personal supreme pacification; but the compassionate one always [delights] in the pacification of all. MSA 5.7

children.text: jano vimūḍhaḥ svasukhārthamudyataḥ sadā tadaprāpya paraiti duḥkhatām /
children.translated_text: The deluded person, always striving for his own happiness, never attaining it, falls into suffering;

children.text: sadā tu dhīro hi parārthamudyato dvayārthamādhāya paraiti nirvṛtim // MSA_5.8 //
children.translated_text: but the wise one, always striving for others' welfare, fulfilling the purpose of both, attains supreme bliss. MSA 5.8

children.text: yathā yathā hyakṣavicitragocare pravartate cāragato jinātmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: As the son of the <s>Jina</s>, engaged in conduct, moves through the sphere of varied sense-objects,

children.text: tathā tathā yuktasamānatāpadairhitāya sattveṣvabhisaṃskaroti tat // MSA_5.9 //
children.translated_text: so too, through appropriate and equal steps, he fashions that [conduct] for the welfare of beings. MSA 5.9
The wise one never becomes angry at people whose minds are not self-governed but are under the sway of faults;

children.text: akāmakāreṇa hi viprapattayo jane bhavantīti kṛpāvivṛddhitaḥ // MSA_5.10 //
children.translated_text: for transgressions in people arise involuntarily — [he understands this] through the increase of compassion. MSA 5.10
This practice, overcoming all the courses of <s>bhava</s> (existence) and following supreme peace,
ever growing through multitudes of varied virtues, always embracing the world with a compassionate intention. MSA 5.11
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fifth chapter on practice.
Sixth chapter.
Verse on the analysis of the characteristic of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>).

children.text: na sanna cāsanna tathā na cānyathā na jāyate vyeti na cāvahīyate /
children.translated_text: It is neither existent nor non-existent, nor otherwise; it neither arises nor ceases, nor is it diminished,

children.text: na vardhate nāpi viśudhyate punarviśudhyate tatparamārthalakṣaṇam // MSA_6.1 //
children.translated_text: nor does it increase; nor is it purified; yet it is purified — that is the characteristic of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). MSA 6.1

children.text: na cātmadṛṣṭiḥ svayamātmalakṣaṇā na cāpi duḥsaṃsthitatā vilakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Neither is the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) itself the characteristic of the self, nor is the state of being ill-constituted its opposite characteristic;

children.text: dvayānna cānyad bhrama eṣata[tū]ditastataśca mokṣo bhramamātrasaṃkṣayaḥ // MSA_6.2 //
children.translated_text: nor is there anything other than these two — this error has arisen [from them]; and therefore liberation is merely the extinction of error. MSA 6.2

children.text: kathaṃ jano vibhramamātramāśritaḥ paraiti duḥkhaprakṛtiṃ na saṃtatām /
children.translated_text: How does a person, resorting to mere delusion, reach suffering that is continuous in nature?

children.text: avedako vedaka eva duḥkhito na duḥkhito dharmamayo na tanmayaḥ // MSA_6.3 //
children.translated_text: One who does not know, [yet] is a knower — is afflicted by suffering; one who is not afflicted, is constituted of <s>dharma</s>, not constituted of that [suffering]. MSA 6.3
How does a person, whose activity is evident, take recourse to what is caused by another, in what arises from dependent origination?
What kind of darkness is this, such that not seeing, one perceives what is neither existent nor non-existent? MSA 6.4

children.text: ta cāntaraṃ kiṃcana vidyate 'nayoḥ sadarthavṛttyā śamajanmanoriha /
children.translated_text: There is no [real] interval between these two — peace and arising — here, since they function with a single meaning;

children.text: tathāpi janmakṣayato vidhīyate śamasya lābhaḥ śubhakarmakāriṇām // MSA_6.5 //
children.translated_text: yet, through the destruction of birth, the attainment of peace is accomplished for those who perform virtuous deeds. MSA 6.5

children.text: saṃbhṛtya saṃbhāramanantapāraṃ jñānasya puṇyasya ca bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having accumulated an infinite and boundless provision of knowledge and merit, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,
through well-determined contemplation of <s>dharmas</s>, goes beyond mere verbal elaboration to the understanding of meaning. MSA 6.6

children.text: arthānsa vijñāya ca jalpamātrān saṃtiṣṭhate tannibhacittamātre /
children.translated_text: Having understood those meanings as mere verbal elaboration, he abides in the mere [transformation of] mind resembling that;
and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) becomes directly perceived — therefore, freed from the characteristic of duality. MSA 6.7

children.text: nāstīti cittātparametya buddhyā cittasya nāstitvamupaiti tasmāt /
children.translated_text: Having transcended mind with the understanding 'it does not exist,' [he realizes] the non-existence of mind itself; therefore,
having realized the non-existence of both, the wise one abides in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, free from [both] its course and its destruction. MSA 6.8
Through the power of the non-conceptual knowledge of the wise one, constantly accompanied [by him] in all directions,

children.text: tadāśrayo gahvaradoṣasaṃcayo mahagadeneva viṣaṃ nirasyate // MSA_6.9 //
children.translated_text: the accumulation of deep-seated faults, which is [the mind's] basis, is expelled like poison by a great remedy. MSA 6.9
Established in the well-ordered good <s>dharma</s> proclaimed by the <s>Muni</s>, having applied his intellect to the root <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
having understood mindfulness and course as mere conceptual construction, the courageous one quickly crosses to the far shore of the ocean of virtues. MSA 6.10
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixth chapter on reality (<s>tattva</s>).
Seventh chapter.
Verse on the analysis of the characteristic of spiritual power (<s>prabhāva</s>).
Regarding birth, speech, mind, virtue and non-virtue, their basis, essence, and the domain beyond [ordinary perception],

children.text: jñānaṃ hi sarvatragasaprabhedeṣvavyāhataṃ dhīragataḥ prabhāvaḥ // MSA_7.1 //
children.translated_text: knowledge that is unobstructed in all-pervading [matters] with their divisions — that is the power of the courageous one's attainment. MSA 7.1
Having attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) in its utmost purity, through the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge,
through mental activity according to the [appropriate] arrangement, he attains the supreme accomplishment of spiritual power. MSA 7.2
By means of noble, divine, incomparable, and sublime <s>Brāhma</s> abodes (<s>vihāras</s>), he always dwells nobly;

children.text: buddhāṃśca sattvāṃśca sa dikṣu gatvā saṃmānayatyānayate viśuddhim // MSA_7.3 //
children.translated_text: and going to the <s>Buddhas</s> and beings in all directions, he honors them and brings about purification. MSA 7.3
He sees all world-realms with their beings, with their evolutions and destructions, as illusion-like;

children.text: saṃdarśayatyeva ca tānyatheṣṭaṃ vaśī vicitrairapi sa prakāraiḥ // MSA_7.4 //
children.translated_text: and he displays them as he wishes, that master, through various modes as well. MSA 7.4
Through the emission of rays, he transforms beings in the lower realms who are intensely suffering into heaven-dwellers;
shaking the <s>Māras</s> and their hosts, with their magnificent flying palaces agitated, he terrifies the assembled <s>Māras</s>. MSA 7.5
He displays immeasurable sport of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) amidst the foremost assembly;
and through supreme emanations with [appropriate] actions and births, he remains for the welfare of beings at all times. MSA 7.6
Through mastery of knowledge, he attains the purification of the [Buddha-]field, for displaying it according to his wish;
and in [realms] where the name of <s>Buddha</s> does not exist, by causing [beings] to hear the name of <s>Buddha</s>, he transfers them to another realm. MSA 7.7

children.text: śakto bhavatyeva ca satvapāke saṃjātapakṣaḥ śakuniryathaiva /
children.translated_text: And he becomes capable of maturing beings, just like a bird whose wings have grown;

children.text: buddhātpraśaṃsāṃ labhate 'timātrām ādeyavākyo bhavati prajānām // MSA_7.8 //
children.translated_text: he receives immense praise from the <s>Buddha</s> and becomes one whose words are to be heeded by living beings. MSA 7.8

children.text: ṣaḍdhāpyabhijñā trividhā ca vidyā aṣṭau vimokṣā 'bhibhuvastathā'ṣṭau /
children.translated_text: The sixfold <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and the threefold <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) and likewise the eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery),

children.text: daśāpi kṛtsnāyatanānyameyāḥ samādhayo dhīragataḥ prabhāvaḥ // MSA_7.9 //
children.translated_text: and the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality-bases) and immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> — that is the power of the courageous one's attainment. MSA 7.9

children.text: sa hi paramavaśitvalabdhabuddhirjagadavaśaṃ svavaśe vidhāya nityam /
children.translated_text: For he, having attained the intellect of supreme mastery, ever bringing the uncontrolled world under his own control,
delighting solely in performing benefit for others, moves through [worldly] existences like a lion, the truly courageous one. MSA 7.10
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the seventh chapter on spiritual power.
Eighth chapter.
Compilation of verses on the maturation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: rūciḥ prasādaḥ praśamo 'nukampanā kṣamātha medhā prabalatvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Inclination, faith, tranquility, compassion,

children.text: ahāryatāṅgaiḥ samupetatā bhṛśaṃ jinātmaje tatparipākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.1 //
children.translated_text: patience, intelligence, and great strength, together with being endowed with the [necessary] factors and being unshakeable — these are the characteristics of maturation in the son of the <s>Jina</s>. MSA 8.1
Good friendship and the triad [of hearing, reflecting, meditating], intense vigor, the gathering of the highest and supreme <s>dharma</s>,
compassionate great embrace of the true <s>dharma</s> — this is held to be the characteristic of proper maturation. MSA 8.2
Knowledge of qualities, quick attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, experience of fruits, and non-violation of the mind,

children.text: jinātmaje śāstari saṃprapattaye mataṃ hi samyakparipākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.3 //
children.translated_text: in the son of the <s>Jina</s>, for the purpose of devotion to the Teacher — this is held to be the characteristic of proper maturation. MSA 8.3
Good moral conduct, avoidance of afflicted thoughts, freedom from obstacles, and delight in virtue,

children.text: jīnātmaje kleśavinodanāyatan mataṃ hi samyakparipākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.4 //
children.translated_text: in the son of the <s>Jina</s>, for the purpose of dispelling <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — this is held to be the characteristic of proper maturation. MSA 8.4

children.text: kṛpā prakṛtyā paraduḥkhadarśanaṃ nihīnacittasya ca saṃpravarjanam /
children.translated_text: Compassion by nature, seeing the suffering of others, abandoning those of base minds,
attaining distinction, and being foremost among beings in the world — these are the characteristics of maturation for compassion toward others. MSA 8.5
Fortitude by nature, meditative cultivation with analytical reflection, constant forbearance of intense suffering, cold, and the like,
progress toward distinction and delight in virtue — this is held to be the characteristic of maturation for patience (<s>kṣamā</s>). MSA 8.6
Purity of karmic fruition, non-loss of what has been heard and the like, penetration into well-spoken and ill-spoken [teachings],

children.text: smṛtermahābuddhayudaye ca yogyatā sumedhatāyāḥ paripākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.7 //
children.translated_text: fitness for mindfulness and the arising of great intelligence — these are the characteristics of maturation for good intelligence (<s>medhā</s>). MSA 8.7
Nourishment of the twofold realm (<s>dhātu</s>) through the two [accumulations of] virtue, supreme fitness for the arising of fruit in the basis,
fulfillment of aspirations, and being foremost among beings in the world — these are the characteristics of maturation for attaining strength (<s>bala</s>). MSA 8.8
Disposition for good <s>dharma</s>, investigation and analysis, attainment of distinction, refutation of opposing positions,

children.text: punaḥ sadā māranirantarāyatā ahāryatāyāḥ paripākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.9 //
children.translated_text: and perpetual freedom from the obstacles [posed by] <s>Māra</s> — these are the characteristics of maturation for being unshakeable (<s>ahāryatā</s>). MSA 8.9
Accumulation of virtue, fitness for effort regarding the basis, delight in supreme virtue through detachment,

children.text: jinātmaje hyaṅgasamanvaye punarmataṃ hi samyakparipākalakṣaṇam // MSA_8.10 //
children.translated_text: in the son of the <s>Jina</s>, for the purpose of being endowed with the [necessary] factors — this is held to be the characteristic of proper maturation. MSA 8.10
Thus, enriched by these nine categories, having attained fitness for the maturation of others,
with a nature constantly nourished by virtuous <s>dharma</s>, he always becomes the foremost kinsman of the world. MSA 8.11

children.text: vraṇe 'pi bhojye paripāka iṣyate yathaiva tatsrāvaṇabhogayogyatā /
children.translated_text: Just as in a wound or in food, maturation is desired — namely, the fitness for draining and for consumption,
so too in this basis, the pacification of both sides, and likewise the state of being fit for enjoyment and of the well-pacified side. MSA 8.12
Ripening (<s>vipācana</s>) is stated, and likewise maturing (<s>paripācana</s>), thorough cooking (<s>prapācana</s>), and also not-cooking (<s>anupācana</s>),

children.text: supācanā[cā]pyadhipācanā matā nipācanotpācananā ca dehiṣu // MSA_8.13 //
children.translated_text: good-cooking (<s>supācana</s>), over-cooking (<s>adhipācana</s>), down-cooking (<s>nipācana</s>), and up-cooking (<s>utpācana</s>) — these [apply] to embodied beings. MSA 8.13
Just as the son of the <s>Jina</s>, established here with a benevolent intention, matures the entire world,

children.text: tathā na mātā na pitā na bandhavaḥ suteṣu bandhuṣvapi suvyavasthitāḥ // MSA_8.14 //
children.translated_text: so neither mother, nor father, nor kinsmen are so well-established toward their children and relatives. MSA 8.14

children.text: tathājano nātmani vatsalo mataḥ kuto 'pi susnigdhaparāśraye jane /
children.translated_text: Indeed, an ordinary person is not so considered to be affectionate toward himself — how much less toward another person, however dear;

children.text: yathā kṛpātmā parasatvavatsalo hite sukhe caiva niyojanātmataḥ // MSA_8.15 //
children.translated_text: as is a compassionate one who is devoted to other beings, by nature inclined to engage them in welfare and happiness. MSA 8.15

children.text: na bodhisattvasya śarīrabhogayoḥ pareṣvadeyaṃ punarasti sarvathā /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, there is nothing whatsoever in body or enjoyments that is not to be given to others;

children.text: anugraheṇa dvividhena pācayan paraṃ samairdānaguṇairna tṛpyate // MSA_8.16 //
children.translated_text: maturing others through twofold grace, he is never satiated with equal qualities of giving. MSA 8.16
Always by nature non-harmful himself, delighting [in virtue], heedful, establishing others therein;

children.text: paraṃparānugrahakṛt dvidhā pare vipākaniṣyandaguṇena pācakaḥ // MSA_8.17 //
children.translated_text: one who creates benefit for others in succession, ripening them in two ways — through the qualities of fruition and natural outflow. // MSA_8.17 //
Wise in having a beneficent attitude toward those who harm him, forgiving even harsh transgressions,
through skillful mental attitudes and forbearance of harm, he leads those who harm him to virtue. // MSA_8.18 //

children.text: punaḥ sa yatnaṃ paramaṃ samāśrito na khidyate kalpasahasrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Again, having resorted to the supreme effort, the son of the <s>Jinas</s> is not wearied even by billions of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: jinātmajaḥ sa[ttva]gaṇaṃ prapācayan paraikacittasya śubhasya kāraṇāt // MSA_8.19 //
children.translated_text: ripening the multitude of beings, for the sake of even a single virtuous thought in another. // MSA_8.19 //
Having attained supreme mastery over the mind, he attracts others here to the teaching;

children.text: nihatya sarvāmavamānakāmatāṃ śubhena saṃvardhayate ca taṃ punaḥ // MSA_8.20 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed all desire for contempt, he further cultivates that [being] through virtue. // MSA_8.20 //

children.text: sa tatvabhāvārthanaye suniścitaḥ karoti satvānsuvinīta saṃśayān /
children.translated_text: He, well-established in the method of reality, meaning, and doctrine, removes the doubts of beings while being well-disciplined;

children.text: tataśca te tajjinaśāsanādarād vivardhayante svaparaṃ guṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ // MSA_8.21 //
children.translated_text: and they, through their respect for the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>, develop themselves and others through excellent qualities. // MSA_8.21 //

children.text: iti sugatigatau śubhatraye vā jagadakhilaṃ kṛpayā sa bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, whether in [leading beings to] a good rebirth or the three excellences, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, out of compassion for the entire world,
disciplines [beings] through minor, supreme, middle, and [other] modes, proceeding with an attitude equal toward [all] the world. // MSA_8.22 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eighth chapter on ripening (<s>paripāka</s>).
The ninth chapter.
On omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), two verses; the third is an exposition of those very [two].
Through immeasurable hundreds of difficult deeds, through immeasurable accumulations of merit,
through an immeasurable period of time, through the destruction of immeasurable obscurations — // MSA_9.1 //
the attainment of omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), stainless of all obscurations,
revealed like a jewel-casket — this is called <s>Buddhahood</s>. // MSA_9.2 //

children.text: kṛtvā duṣkaramadbhutaṃ śramaśataiḥ saṃcityasarvaśubhaṃ kālenottamakalpayānamahatā sarvāvṛtīnāṃ kṣayāt /
children.translated_text: Having performed wondrous difficult deeds through hundreds of efforts, having accumulated all virtue, through an immeasurably great supreme <s>kalpa</s>-vehicle of time, through the destruction of all coverings,

children.text: sūkṣmasyāvaraṇasya bhūmiṣu gatasyotpāṭanād buddhatā ratnānāmiva sā prabhāvamahatāṃ peṭā samuddhāti[ṭi?]tā // MSA_9.3 //
children.translated_text: through the uprooting of the subtle obscuration that has gone through the stages — <s>Buddhahood</s>, like a jewel-casket of those great in power, stands revealed. // MSA_9.3 //

children.text: sarvadharmāśca buddhatvaṃ dharmo naiva na kaścana /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddhahood</s>, yet no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever [is Buddhahood];

children.text: śukladharmamayaṃ tacca na ca taistannirūpyate // MSA_9.4 //
children.translated_text: it is constituted of white (pure) <s>dharmas</s>, yet it is not defined by them. // MSA_9.4 //
Because it is the cause of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, it is compared to a jewel-mine;
because it is the cause of virtue, it is considered comparable to a cloud. // MSA_9.5 //

children.text: buddhatvaṃ sarvadharmaḥ samuditamatha vā sarvadharmavyapetaṃ prodbhūterdharmaratnapratatasumahato dharmaratnākarābham /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> is all <s>dharmas</s> assembled, or else devoid of all <s>dharmas</s>; because of the production of the vast, great jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, it resembles a jewel-mine of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: bhūtānāṃ śuklasasyaprasavasumahato hetuto meghabhūtaṃ dānāddharmāmbuvarṣapratatasuvihitasyākṣayasya prajāsu // MSA_9.6 //
children.translated_text: because it is the cause of the vast production of the pure harvest of beings, it is like a cloud — well-established in the inexhaustible rain of <s>Dharma</s>-water of giving and so forth upon creatures. // MSA_9.6 //
For <s>Buddhahood</s> is always protection from all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>),
from all evil conduct, and from birth and death. // MSA_9.7 //
From all calamities, from bad destinies, from wrong means,
from the belief in a self-entity (<s>satkāya</s>), and from the <s>Hīnayāna</s> — therefore it is the supreme refuge. // MSA_9.8 //
That incomparable refuge, the supreme <s>Buddhahood</s>, is desired — protection in birth, death, all afflictions, and evils;
the removal of all fears for those beset by various fears — the means for the removal of manifold extended sufferings. // MSA_9.9 //

children.text: bauddhairdharmairyacca susaṃpūrṇaśarīraṃ yatsaddharme vetti sa sattvānpravinetum /
children.translated_text: Whose body is perfectly complete with the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, who in the true <s>Dharma</s> knows [how] to lead beings,

children.text: yātaṃ pāraṃ yatkṛpayā sarvajagatsu tad buddhatvaṃ śreṣṭhamihatyaṃ[heṣṭaṃ] śaraṇānām // MSA_9.10 //
children.translated_text: who has gone to the far shore out of compassion for all worlds — that <s>Buddhahood</s> is the supreme of refuges here. // MSA_9.10 //
For all time, for all beings, <s>Buddhahood</s> is the great refuge,
considered as the turning away from all calamities and the well-being [of beings]. // MSA_9.11 //

children.text: kleśajñeyavṛtīnāṃ satatamanugataṃ bījamutkṛṣṭakālaṃ yasminnastaṃ prayātaṃ bhavati suvipulaiḥ sarvahāniprakāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: In whom the seed that continuously accompanies the obscurations of affliction and the knowable, [accumulated] over a supreme [length of] time, has been destroyed through all the varieties of complete abandonment —

children.text: buddhatvaṃ śukladharmapravaraguṇayutā ā[cā]śrayasyānyathāptis tatprāptirnirvikalpādviṣayasumahato jñānamārgātsuśuddhāt // MSA_9.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) endowed with the foremost qualities of pure <s>dharmas</s>; its attainment is from the supremely pure, non-conceptual path of knowledge that has a vast object. // MSA_9.12 //
And abiding in that, the <s>Tathāgata</s> gazes upon the world as if standing on the king of great mountains;

children.text: śamābhirāmaṃ karūṇāyate janamaghā[bhavā]bhirāme 'nyajane tu kā kathā // MSA_9.13 //
children.translated_text: he has compassion for the people delighting in tranquility — what need to speak of [his compassion for] other people delighting in evil [and existence]? // MSA_9.13 //
Activity, arising, non-activity, the basis, cessation, covering, and then the two from the two;

children.text: samāviśiṣṭā api sarvagātmikā tathāgatānāṃ parivṛttiriṣyate // MSA_9.14 //
children.translated_text: though equally distinguished, the revolution (<s>parivṛtti</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is held to be all-pervading in nature. // MSA_9.14 //

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ sarvagataṃ sadāmataṃ tathaiva tatsarvagataṃ sadāmatam /
children.translated_text: Just as space is always considered all-pervading, so too that [<s>Buddhahood</s>] is always considered all-pervading;

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ rūpagaṇeṣu sarvagaṃ tathaiva tatsatvagaṇeṣu sarvagam // MSA_9.15 //
children.translated_text: just as space pervades all form-aggregates, so too that pervades all being-aggregates. // MSA_9.15 //
Just as when a water-vessel is broken, the reflection of the moon is not seen,

children.text: tatha duṣṭeṣu sattveṣu buddhabimbaṃ na dṛśyate // MSA_9.16 //
children.translated_text: so in corrupted beings, the image of the <s>Buddha</s> is not seen. // MSA_9.16 //
Just as fire blazes in one place and is extinguished in another,
so too should the appearance and disappearance among <s>Buddhas</s> be understood. // MSA_9.17 //
Just as from unstruck drums there would be the arising of sound,

children.text: tathā jiṇe vinābhogaṃ deśanāyāḥ samudbhavaḥ // MSA_9.18 //
children.translated_text: so in the <s>Jina</s>, without deliberate effort, is the arising of teaching. // MSA_9.18 //
Just as from a gem, without effort, there is the display of its natural radiance,
so too among <s>Buddhas</s>, without effort, is the display of their activity. // MSA_9.19 //
Just as in space, uninterrupted activities are seen in the world,
so too in the undefiled element (<s>anāsrava dhātu</s>), the activities of the <s>Jinas</s> are uninterrupted. // MSA_9.20 //
Just as in space, there is always decline and rise of activities,
so too in the undefiled element, there is the arising and passing away of <s>Buddha</s>-activity. // MSA_9.21 //
Though undifferentiated with respect to before and after, stainless of all obscurations,

children.text: naśuddhā nāpi cāśuddhā tathatā buddhatā matā // MSA_9.22 //
children.translated_text: neither pure nor impure — <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>) is considered <s>Buddhahood</s>. // MSA_9.22 //
In the purified <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), through <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), from the attainment of the path,
the <s>Buddhas</s>, having attained the pure self, have reached the great selfhood of the self. // MSA_9.23 //

children.text: na bhāvo nāpi cābhāvo buddhatvaṃ tena kathyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> is spoken of as neither existence nor non-existence;
therefore, regarding the question of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s [post-mortem] state, the method of the undeclared is held. // MSA_9.24 //
Just as in the case of burning and cooling of metal, and in the case of seeing [and removal] of darkness,

children.text: cittajñāne tathā bauddhe bhāvābhāvo na śasyate // MSA_9.25 //
children.translated_text: so in the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge of mind, neither existence nor non-existence is praised. // MSA_9.25 //

children.text: buddhānāmamale dhātau naikatā bahutā na ca /
children.translated_text: In the stainless element of the <s>Buddhas</s>, there is neither oneness nor multiplicity,
because of bodilessness like space, [yet] in accordance with former bodies. // MSA_9.26 //
In the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the powers and the like, <s>Bodhi</s> is compared to a jewel-mine;
in the wholesome harvests of the world, it is considered comparable to a great cloud. // MSA_9.27 //
Because of being perfectly complete in merit and knowledge, it is considered comparable to the full moon;
because of making the light of knowledge, it is considered comparable to the great sun. // MSA_9.28 //
Just as immeasurable rays, mixed together in the orb of the sun,
always function as one [entity] and illuminate the world —
so too in the undefiled element, the immeasurability of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
mixed as one in [their] activities, makes the light of knowledge. // MSA_9.30 //
Just as from the essence of one ray, all rays emanate
from the sun — so too should the emanation of knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> be understood. // MSA_9.31 //
Just as in the functioning of the sun's rays there is no sense of 'mine,'

children.text: tathaiva buddhajñānānāṃ vṛttau nāsti mamāyitam // MSA_9.32 //
children.translated_text: so too in the functioning of the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge there is no sense of 'mine.' // MSA_9.32 //
Just as the world is illumined by rays released simultaneously from the sun,

children.text: sakṛt jñeyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ buddhajñānaiḥ prabhāsyate // MSA_9.33 //
children.translated_text: so too all the knowable is illumined simultaneously by the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // MSA_9.33 //
Just as clouds and the like are considered the obscuration of the sun's rays,
so too the corruption of beings is the obscuration of the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge. // MSA_9.34 //
Just as due to dust on cloth there is absence of dye-coloration,
so due to non-penetration in liberation, there is absence of knowledge-coloration. // MSA_9.35 //
The profundity in the stainless element, in the marks, abodes, and activities
of the <s>Buddhas</s> is declared — as the coloring of space with colors. // MSA_9.36 //
Though <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>) is undifferentiated for all, it has come to purity;
therefore <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood, and therefore all embodied beings contain that embryo (<s>tathāgatagarbha</s>). // MSA_9.37 //
The sovereignty of <s>Śrāvakas</s> is surpassed by that of worldly [<s>Buddhas</s>];
the [sovereignty] of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> is surpassed by that of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. // MSA_9.38 //
It does not attain even a fraction of the sovereignty of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>;
[that of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>] does not attain even a fraction of the sovereignty of a <s>Tathāgata</s>. // MSA_9.39 //
Immeasurable and inconceivable is the sovereignty of the <s>Buddhas</s> considered to be —

children.text: yasya yatra yathā yāvatkāle yasminpravartate // MSA_9.40 //
children.translated_text: regarding whom, where, how, how much, and at what time it operates. // MSA_9.40 //
In the revolution of the five sense-faculties, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the operation of all purposes for all, with the arising of twelve hundred qualities. // MSA_9.41 //
In the revolution of the mind too, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the knowledge that accompanies sovereignty — non-conceptual and supremely pure. // MSA_9.42 //
In the revolution of meaningful apprehension, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the purification of the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field, displaying enjoyments at will. // MSA_9.43 //
In the revolution of conceptualization, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the non-obstruction of all knowledge-activities at all times always. // MSA_9.44 //
In the revolution of the basis (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained —
the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s> in the stainless state. // MSA_9.45 //
In the revolution of sexual union, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the blissful abode of a <s>Buddha</s> — the vision of a consort without defilement. // MSA_9.46 //
In the revolution of the notion of space, supreme sovereignty is attained,
in the fulfillment of intended purposes and in the manifestation of movement and form. // MSA_9.47 //
Thus, through immeasurable revolution, immeasurable sovereignty is held [to arise],
through the performance of inconceivable activities of the <s>Buddhas</s> in [their] stainless basis. // MSA_9.48 //

children.text: śubhe vṛddho loko vrajati suviśuddhau paramatāṃ śubhe cānārabdhvā vrajati śubhavṛddhau paramatām /
children.translated_text: The world, increased in virtue, goes to supreme purification; and without having begun virtue, goes to supreme increase of virtue;

children.text: vrajatyevaṃ loko diśi diśi jinānāṃ sukathitair apakvaḥ pakvo vā [na]ca punaraśeṣaṃ dhruvamiha // MSA_9.49 //
children.translated_text: thus the world proceeds in every direction through the well-spoken [teachings] of the <s>Jinas</s> — whether unripe or ripe, yet not entirely [at once], certainly, here. // MSA_9.49 //

children.text: tathā kṛtvā caryāṃ [kṛcchrāvāpyāṃ] paramaguṇayogādbhutavartī mahābodhiṃ nityāṃ dhruvamaśaraṇānāṃ ca śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the [difficult-to-attain] conduct, possessing wondrous supreme qualities, the brave ones attain the eternal great <s>Bodhi</s>, the certain refuge for the refugeless,

children.text: labhante yaddhīrā [diśi diśi] gasadā [sadā]sarvasamayaṃ tadāścaryaṃ loke suvidhacaraṇānnādbhutamapi // MSA_9.50 //
children.translated_text: always, at all times, [in every direction] — this is wonderful in the world, yet from the well-conducted practice, it is not [truly] wonderful. // MSA_9.50 //

children.text: kvaciddharmāñcakaṃ [dharmyaṃ cakraṃ] bahumukhaśatairdarśayati yaḥ kvacijjanmāntardhiṃ kvacidapi vicitrāṃ janacarīm /
children.translated_text: Somewhere he displays the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> with hundreds of faces; somewhere birth and disappearance; somewhere also varied conduct among people;

children.text: kvacitkṛtsnāṃ bodhiṃ kvacidapi ca nirvāṇamasakṛt na ca sthānāttasmādvicalati sa sarvaṃ ca kurute // MSA_9.51 //
children.translated_text: somewhere complete <s>Bodhi</s>, and somewhere also <s>Nirvāṇa</s> repeatedly — yet he does not stir from that state, and does everything. // MSA_9.51 //

children.text: na buddhānāmevaṃ bhavati mamapakvo 'yamiti cāprapācyo 'yaṃ dehī api ca adhunāpācyata iti /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> do not have [the thought]: 'This one is ripened by me,' or 'this being is unripenable,' or 'this one is being ripened now';

children.text: vinā saṃskāraṃ tu prapacamupayātyeva janatā śubhairdharmairnityaṃ diśi diśiḥ samantāttrayamukham // MSA_9.52 //
children.translated_text: yet without [deliberate] construction, the people attain ripening through excellent <s>dharmas</s>, always, in every direction, in all three ways. // MSA_9.52 //

children.text: yathāyatnaṃ bhānuḥ pratataviṣadairaṃśavisaraiḥ prapāka[kaṃ] sasyānāṃ diśi [diśi] samantātprakurūte /
children.translated_text: Just as the sun, without effort, with extensive clear rays spreading, effects the ripening of crops in every direction all around,

children.text: tathā dharmārko 'pi praśamavidhidharmāṃśuvisaraiḥ prapākaṃ sasyānāṃ diśi diśi samantātprakurūte // MSA_9.53 //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Dharma</s>-sun, with rays of <s>dharmas</s> of the method of pacification spreading, effects the ripening of [the] crops in every direction all around. // MSA_9.53 //

children.text: yathaikasmāddīpādbhavati sumahāndīpanicayo 'prameyo 'saṃkhyeyo na ca sa punareti vyayamataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as from one lamp arises a great multitude of lamps, immeasurable and countless, and it does not undergo diminishment thereby,

children.text: tathaikasmād buddhād [pākā]bhavati sumahān paripāka[pāka]nicayo 'prameyo 'saṃkhyeyo na ca punareti[punarupaiti] vyayamataḥ // MSA_9.54 //
children.translated_text: so too from one <s>Buddha</s> arises a great multitude of ripenings, immeasurable and countless, and he does not undergo diminishment thereby. // MSA_9.54 //

children.text: yathā toyaistṛptiṃ vrajati na mahāsāgara iva na vṛddhiṃ vā yāti pratataviṣadāmbu praviśanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the great ocean is not satiated by waters, nor increases when vast clear waters enter it,

children.text: tathā bauddhau dhātuḥ satatasamitaiḥ śuddhiviśanair natṛptiṃ vṛddhiṃ vā vrajati paramāścaryamiha tat // MSA_9.55 //
children.translated_text: so the <s>Buddha</s>-element (<s>dhātu</s>) is neither satiated nor increased by the constant entry of purifications — this is the supreme wonder here. // MSA 9.55 //
It has the characteristic of purification of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s> through the removal of the duality [of subject and object],
and the characteristic of inexhaustibility and mastery over reality, knowledge, and its objects. // MSA 9.56 //

It has the characteristic of purification of the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> from the two obscurations — of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions) and <s>jñeya</s> (the knowable) — and the characteristic of inexhaustibility and mastery over reality, the knowledge of its objects.

The cultivation of the knowledge of <s>tathatā</s> in all respects is the accomplishment; the placing of all beings in the twofold [goal] and inexhaustibility in every way is the fruit. // MSA 9.57 //
It functions through the activity, means, and practice of magical creation of body, speech, and mind,
and is endowed with immeasurable [qualities] through the two doors of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention). // MSA 9.58 //
It functions differently through the <s>svabhāva</s> (essential), <s>dharma</s>, <s>saṃbhoga</s> (enjoyment), and <s>nirmāṇa</s> (emanation) [bodies],
and this purified <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is proclaimed as belonging to the <s>Buddhas</s>. // MSA 9.59 //
The <s>svābhāvika</s> (essential body), the <s>sāṃbhogya</s> (enjoyment body), and the other, the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation body) —

children.text: kāyabhedā hi buddhānāṃ prathamastu dvayāśrayaḥ // MSA_9.60 //
children.translated_text: these are the divisions of the bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s>; the first is the basis of the [other] two. // MSA 9.60 //
The enjoyment body is differentiated in all realms by retinues,
by fields, names, bodies, <s>dharma</s>-enjoyment, and activities. // MSA 9.61 //

children.text: samaḥ sūkṣmaśca tacchiṣṭaḥ[cchliṣṭaḥ] kāyaḥ svābhāviko mataḥ /
children.translated_text: The essential body is regarded as equal, subtle, and adherent to that [enjoyment body],
being the cause of the glory of the enjoyment [body], showing enjoyment as desired. // MSA 9.62 //
The immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-emanation is regarded as the emanation body,
and the complete fulfillment of the purpose of both [self and others] is established in every aspect. // MSA 9.63 //
Through displays of craft, birth, great awakening, and perpetual <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
this emanation body of the <s>Buddha</s> is a great skillful means for liberation. // MSA 9.64 //
The collection of the <s>Buddhas</s>' bodies should be known through these three bodies,
which, with their basis, serve the purposes of self and others — shown through these three bodies. // MSA 9.65 //
They are regarded as equal in basis, intention, and action;
and their eternality in these [three bodies] is through nature, non-degeneration, and continuity. // MSA 9.66 //
The <s>ādarśajñāna</s> (mirror-like wisdom) is immovable; the three [other] wisdoms depend on it —
in equality, discriminating examination, and the accomplishment of activities. // MSA 9.67 //
The <s>ādarśajñāna</s> is without self-attachment, unlimited, ever-accompanying,

children.text: sarvajñeyeṣvasaṃmūḍhaṃ na ca teṣvāmukhaṃ sadā // MSA_9.68 //
children.translated_text: unconfused regarding all knowables, and never turned away from them. // MSA 9.68 //
Because it is the cause of all wisdoms, it is like the form of a great mirror,
and it is the <s>saṃbhoga</s>-Buddhahood, because of the arising of the reflection of wisdom [in it]. // MSA 9.69 //
The <s>samatājñāna</s> (wisdom of equality) regarding beings is considered immaculate through the purification of cultivation,
and is regarded as the wisdom of equality, pervaded by non-abiding [<s>nirvāṇa</s>]. // MSA 9.70 //
It is considered as ever-accompanying through great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>),
and it shows the image of the <s>Buddha</s> to beings according to their faith (<s>adhimokṣa</s>). // MSA 9.71 //
The <s>pratyavekṣaṇajñāna</s> (discriminating wisdom) is always unobstructed regarding knowables,
and it is like a treasury of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> and <s>samādhis</s>. // MSA 9.72 //
In the circle of the assembly, it displays all glories,
cuts through all doubts, and pours forth the great <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 9.73 //
The <s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s> (wisdom of accomplishing activities), through emanations in all realms,
accomplishes the welfare of all beings through varied, immeasurable, and inconceivable [means]. // MSA 9.74 //
Through the varieties of accomplishing activities, through numbers and fields, always,

children.text: acintyaṃ buddhanirmāṇaṃ vijñeyaṃ tacca sarvathā // MSA_9.75 //
children.translated_text: the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-emanation should be known in every way. // MSA 9.75 //
From retention, from an equal mind, from the correct illumination of the <s>Dharma</s>,
and from the accomplishment of activities — the four wisdoms arise. // MSA 9.76 //
Due to the difference of lineage (<s>gotra</s>), non-futility, completeness, and beginninglessness,
there is neither a single <s>Buddha</s>-hood nor [mere] multiplicity, due to non-difference in the immaculate basis. // MSA 9.77 //
That which is non-existent is itself the supreme existent;
and the complete non-apprehension is regarded as the supreme apprehension. // MSA 9.78 //
The supreme cultivation is the effort; for those who do not see the cultivation,

children.text: pratilambhaḥ paraśceṣṭaḥ pratilambhaṃ ca paśyatām // MSA_9.79 //
children.translated_text: the supreme attainment is the effort — for those who [truly] see the attainment. // MSA 9.79 //
For those who see [something] — the weighty, the long cause, the effort of oneself —
for those proud <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is far off. // MSA 9.80 //
For those who see — all this as stated is mere conceptual construction;
for the non-conceptualizing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is attained. // MSA 9.81 //
Rivers with different beds and different waters, with little water, producing separate effects and purposes,
providing sustenance for aquatic creatures — they exist without having entered the ocean. // MSA 9.82 //
But having entered the ocean, all become of one bed, of one great water,
mixed, of one purpose, and of great sustenance for aquatic creatures always. // MSA 9.83 //
The wise ones with different beds and different minds, with little understanding, performing separate individual tasks,
providing small benefit to beings — they exist without having entered <s>Buddhahood</s>. // MSA 9.84 //
But having entered <s>Buddhahood</s>, all become of one bed, of one great understanding,

children.text: miśrekakāryāśca mahopabhogyāḥ sadā mahāsatvagaṇasya te hi // MSA_9.85 //
children.translated_text: mixed, of one purpose, and of great sustenance for the host of great beings always. // MSA 9.85 //
Thus, through the practice of pure <s>dharmas</s> and because of the <s>Buddha</s>-stage being the cause of benefit and happiness,
because of its production of auspiciousness, supreme happiness, and inexhaustibility, one of auspicious mind deserves to attain the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening). // MSA 9.86 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the ninth chapter on awakening (<s>bodhi</s>).
The tenth chapter.
Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: ādiḥ siddhiḥ śaraṇaṃ gotraṃ citte tathaiva cotpādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beginning, accomplishment, refuge, lineage, and likewise the arising in the mind,
purpose of self and others, the meaning of reality, power, maturation, and awakening. // MSA 10.1 //

children.text: jātā jātā grāhikā grāhyabhūtā mitrādāttā svātmato bhrāntikā ca /
children.translated_text: Born, born, apprehending, being the apprehended, received from a spiritual friend, from oneself, erroneous,

children.text: abhrāntānyā āmukhā naiva cānyā ghoṣācārā caiṣikā cekṣikā ca // MSA_10.2 //
children.translated_text: and another that is non-erroneous, face-to-face, and not otherwise, proceeding from sound, of the nature of a signal, and visual. // MSA 10.2 //
Susceptible to loss, mixed, unmixed with adversaries, inferior, excellent, covered, uncovered,

children.text: yuktā'yuktā saṃbhṛtā'saṃbhṛtā ca gāḍhaṃ viṣṭā dūragā cādhimuktiḥ // MSA_10.3 //
children.translated_text: connected, disconnected, gathered, ungathered, deeply entered, and far-reaching — [such is] <s>adhimukti</s> (aspiration). // MSA 10.3 //
Inattentiveness, abundance [of sloth], laziness, disturbance in practice,
bad companions, weakness in virtue, and improper mental activity, // MSA 10.4 //
heedlessness, little learning, and contentment with mere hearing and thinking,
pride in mere tranquility, and likewise lack of familiarity — these are known // MSA 10.5 //
as non-alarm, and also alarm, obscuration, and also disconnection,
and non-gathering — these are the obstacles to <s>adhimukti</s> (aspiration). // MSA 10.6 //
Great merit, freedom from remorse, joy, great happiness,

children.text: avipraṇāśaḥ sthairyaṃ ca viśeṣagamanaṃ tathā // MSA_10.7 //
children.translated_text: non-loss, stability, and likewise the attainment of distinction, // MSA 10.7 //
and then the comprehension of <s>dharma</s>, and the supreme attainment of one's own and others' welfare,
and swift supernormal knowledge — these are the benefits of <s>adhimukti</s>. // MSA 10.8 //
For the passionate, it is like a dog; for those in <s>samādhi</s>, like a tortoise;

children.text: bhṛtyopamā svārthināṃ sā rājaprakhyā parārthinām // MSA_10.9 //
children.translated_text: for the self-interested, like a servant; for the altruistic, like a king. // MSA 10.9 //

children.text: tathā kāmisthātṛsvaparajanakṛtyārthamudite viśeṣo vijñeyaḥ satatamadhimuktayā vividhayā /
children.translated_text: Thus, the distinction should be always known through the various [forms of] aspiration, arising for the purpose of the passionate, the stable, the self-interested, and the altruistic. Knowing the supremacy of this in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as prescribed here, the wise one should intensely choose it through those very [aspirations] always. // MSA 10.10 //

children.text: mahāyāne tasya vidhivadiha matvā paramatāṃ bhṛśaṃ tasmin dhīraḥ satatamiha tābheva vṛṇuyāt // MSA_10.10 //
children.translated_text: [Continuation of the above verse.]
Human beings attain awakening at every moment;

children.text: aprameyā yataḥ sattvā layaṃ nāto 'dhivāsayet // MSA_10.11 //
children.translated_text: since beings are immeasurable, one should therefore not be discouraged. // MSA 10.11 //

children.text: yathā puṇyaṃ prasavate pareṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dadat /
children.translated_text: Just as one who gives food to others generates merit,

children.text: na tu svayaṃ sa bhuñjānastathā puṇyamahodayaḥ // MSA_10.12 //
children.translated_text: but not the one who eats himself — so the arising of great merit [is for the altruistic]. // MSA 10.12 //
From the <s>Dharma</s> taught in the <s>sūtras</s>, taught for the benefit of others, [merit] is obtained,
but from the <s>Dharma</s> taught for one's own benefit, it is not obtained. // MSA 10.13 //

children.text: iti vipulagatau mahogha[mahārya]dharme janiya[parijanayan?] sadā matiṃmānmahādhimuktim /
children.translated_text: Thus, constantly generating the mind of great aspiration toward the vast and noble <s>Dharma</s>,
one progresses to the abundant and constant increase of merit and attains supreme greatness through incomparable virtues. // MSA 10.14 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the tenth chapter on <s>adhimukti</s> (aspiration).
The eleventh chapter.
In the chapter on the investigation of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>), four verses on the investigation of the object of support (<s>ālambana</s>):
The three <s>piṭakas</s> (baskets), or two in summary, are valued for nine reasons:
through habituation, awakening, pacification, penetration — they liberate from that. // MSA 11.1 //
The <s>sūtras</s>, <s>abhidharma</s>, and <s>vinaya</s> are regarded as having four kinds of meaning in brief;
from the knowledge of these, the wise one attains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). // MSA 11.2 //
The <s>sūtra</s> is [defined] by its basis, characteristic, <s>dharma</s>, meaning, and indication;
and the <s>abhidharma</s> by facing [the truth], and by frequency, and by the mode of transcendence. // MSA 11.3 //
The <s>vinaya</s> character [is defined] by offense, arising, recovery, and emergence;
by the individual, by designation, and by analysis and determination. // MSA 11.4 //
The object of support (<s>ālambana</s>) is considered to be the <s>dharma</s>, internal and external;
the attainment of both is through the meaning of both and through the non-apprehension of both.
Through mental discourse, through the retention of the meaning stated correctly,

children.text: arthakhyānasya jalpācca nāmni sthānācca cetasaḥ // MSA_11.6 //
children.translated_text: through the discourse of meaning-expression, and through the mind's resting on the name, // MSA 11.6 //
the attainment of the <s>dharma</s> object of support arises through three kinds of knowledge — hearing and the like;
and the threefold attainment of the object of support, as previously stated, depends on these. // MSA 11.7 //
Pertaining to the three realms, accomplishing the purpose, with a constricted basis — the other [type];
establishing aspiration, producing intense desire — another [type]. // MSA 11.8 //
With inferior and complete basis, twofold — with discourse and without discourse,
conjoined with knowledge, and having the nature of the essential practice of <s>yoga</s>. // MSA 11.9 //
And that has a combined object of support and a differentiated object of support;

children.text: pañcadhā saptadhā caiva parijñā pañcadhā 'sya ca // MSA_11.10 //
children.translated_text: it is fivefold and sevenfold, and its full comprehension is fivefold. // MSA 11.10 //
The four and thirty-seven aspects belong to cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>);
it has the nature of the twofold path, has two benefits, and is receptive. // MSA 11.11 //
Preparatory, under one's control, limited, and of vast nature —

children.text: yogināṃ hi manaskāra eṣa sarvātmako mataḥ // MSA_11.12 //
children.translated_text: this mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) of the <s>yogins</s> is considered to be all-encompassing. // MSA 11.12 //

children.text: tatvaṃ yatsatataṃ dvayena rahitaṃ, bhrānteśca saṃniśrayaḥ śakyaṃ naiva ca sarvathābhilapituṃ yañcāprapañcātmakam /
children.translated_text: That reality which is always devoid of duality, the basis of error, impossible to express in any way, and of the nature of non-elaboration —

children.text: jñeyaṃ heyamatho viśodhyamamalaṃ yacca prakṛtyā matam yasyākāśasuvarṇavārisadṛśī kleśādviśuddhirmatā // MSA_11.13 //
children.translated_text: that which is the knowable, the abandonable, the purifiable, and considered immaculate by nature, whose purification from <s>kleśas</s> is likened to space, gold, and water. // MSA 11.13 //

children.text: na khalu jagati tasmādvidyate kiṃcidanyajjagadapi tadaśeṣaṃ tatra saṃmūḍhabuddhi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is nothing else in the world apart from that; and the entire world, confused in understanding regarding it,
how has this manner of worldly delusion arisen — attached to the non-existent, having entirely abandoned the existent? // MSA 11.14 //
Just as there is illusion (<s>māyā</s>), so is <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptual construction) described;
just as there are things created by illusion, so is the error of duality described. // MSA 11.15 //
Just as there is the nature of that [illusion] in something that is not that — so is <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality) accepted;
and just as there is the apprehension of that [illusory appearance] — so is <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth). // MSA 11.16 //
Just as, in the absence of that [illusion], the manifestation of its cause is obtained,
so, in the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), the [manifestation] of unreal conceptual construction is obtained. // MSA 11.17 //
Just as, regarding that cause [of illusion], the world, undeluded, would act freely,
so too, in the transformation [of the basis], the ascetic (<s>yati</s>), undeluded, acts freely. // MSA 11.18 //
The form of that [illusion] exists there, but the nature of that [illusion] does not exist;
therefore, both existence and non-existence are predicated of illusion and the like. // MSA 11.19 //

children.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca /
children.translated_text: In that [illusion], a being is not a non-being, nor is a non-being a being;
and the non-distinction of being and non-being is predicated of illusion and the like. // MSA 11.20 //
Thus, the appearance of duality exists therein, yet its [inherent] reality is not found;
therefore, existence and non-existence are both predicated of form and the like. // MSA 11.21 //

children.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca /
children.translated_text: Neither is [their] being there an [absolute] non-being, nor is [their] non-being [absolute] being;
and the non-differentiation of being and non-being is predicated of form and the like. // MSA 11.22 //
This is accepted for the purpose of negating superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>),
and also for the purpose of negating the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (lesser vehicle) in favor of the [one] vehicle. // MSA 11.23 //
The cause of delusion and the delusion itself are held to be material perception (<s>rūpavijñapti</s>);
and the immaterial perception, from the non-existence [of its object], would exist — but not the other [i.e., the material object]. // MSA 11.24 //
Two [things] are cited as [analogous to] the delusion of grasping the form of a magical elephant:

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate // MSA_11.25 //
children.translated_text: just as the two [i.e., elephant and its form] do not exist therein, yet the two are indeed perceived. // MSA 11.25 //
Two [things] are cited as [analogous to] the delusion of grasping a reflection and a chain [of images]:

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate // MSA_11.26 //
children.translated_text: just as the two do not exist therein, yet the two are indeed perceived. // MSA 11.26 //
Thus from [their] being, thus from [their] non-being, and from the non-differentiation of being and non-being,

children.text: sadasanto 'tha māyābhā ye dharmā bhrāntilakṣaṇāḥ // MSA_11.27 //
children.translated_text: those <s>dharmas</s> that are characterized by delusion are existent-and-non-existent, like an illusion. // MSA 11.27 //
Thus from non-being, thus from non-being, and thus from non-being, they are without defining marks;

children.text: māyopamāśca nirdiṣṭā ye dharmāḥ prātipakṣikāḥ // MSA_11.28 //
children.translated_text: and those <s>dharmas</s> that serve as antidotes are declared to be like an illusion. // MSA 11.28 //
Just as a magical king is defeated by another magical king,

children.text: ye sarvadharmān paśyanti nirmārāste jinātmajāḥ // MSA_11.29 //
children.translated_text: those children of the <s>Jina</s> (Buddha) who see all <s>dharmas</s> [as illusory] are free from <s>Māra</s>. // MSA 11.29 //
Resembling illusion, dream, mirage, and reflection — arising, hearing, bubbles, and water; knowable, moon-in-water, reflection, and magical creation again —

children.text: ṣaṭ ṣaṭ dvau ca punaśca ṣaṭ dvayamatā ekaikaśaśca trayaḥ saṃskārāḥ khalu tatra tatra kathitā buddhairvibuddhottamaiḥ // MSA_11.30 //
children.translated_text: six, six, and two, then again six and two, and three for each one — the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are indeed declared in each case by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme among the awakened. // MSA 11.30 //

children.text: abhūtakalpo na bhūto nābhūto 'kalpa eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhūtakalpa</s> (false imagination) is neither existent nor non-existent, and is indeed beyond conceptualization;

children.text: na kalpo nāpi cākalpaḥ sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ nirucyate // MSA_11.31 //
children.translated_text: it is neither conceptual nor non-conceptual — all that is to be known is thus explained. // MSA 11.31 //
From their own element (<s>dhātu</s>), appearing as duality, accompanied by ignorance and afflictive (<s>kleśa</s>) tendencies,
conceptualizations arise, devoid of the substance of duality. // MSA 11.32 //
The attainment of a particular object [of meditation] is through the connection with abiding in one's own element;

children.text: ta eva hyadvayābhāsā vartante carmakāṇḍavat // MSA_11.33 //
children.translated_text: for those very [conceptualizations], appearing as non-dual, function like [the smoothing of] a hide with a scraper. // MSA 11.33 //
The mind, shining forth as duality, is held to appear as desire (<s>rāga</s>) and the like; likewise,

children.text: śraddhādyābhāsaṃ na tadanyo dharmaḥ kliṣṭakuśalo 'sti // MSA_11.34 //
children.translated_text: appearing as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the like — there is no other <s>dharma</s> that is afflicted or wholesome [apart from mind]. // MSA 11.34 //
Just as there is no [entity with] the characteristic of duality apart from the appearance of duality,

children.text: iti cittaṃ citrābhāsaṃ citrākāraṃ pravartate // MSA_11.35 //
children.translated_text: so the mind operates with variegated appearances, having variegated forms. // MSA 11.35 //

children.text: lakṣyaṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ caiva lakṣaṇā ca prabhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: The characterized (<s>lakṣya</s>), the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and the characterization (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — in their divisions —
have been illuminated by the perfectly awakened ones for the benefit of sentient beings. // MSA 11.36 //
The mind that possesses views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) — therein, the states and their transformations —
