this is the characterized, in brief; it is immeasurable in its divisions. // MSA 11.37 //
The <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) is the cause of the designation of the meaning of ordinary speech;
and from that too, the manifestation of the object is the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>). // MSA 11.38 //

children.text: yathā nāmārthamarthasya nāmnaḥ prakhyānatā ca yā /
children.translated_text: The manifestation of meaning from name, and of name from meaning —
the cause of unreal imagination is indeed the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>). // MSA 11.39 //
Threefold-threefold appearance, characterized as the grasped and the grasper —
false imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is indeed the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). // MSA 11.40 //
The non-being of being and the equality of being and non-being,
unquiescent-yet-quiescent and beyond conceptualization — this is the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). // MSA 11.41 //
Taking as object the <s>dharma</s> of [resultant] flow (<s>niṣyanda</s>), proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>),

children.text: cittasya dhātau sthānaṃ ca sadasattārthapaśyanā // MSA_11.42 //
children.translated_text: abiding of the mind in [its own] element, and the seeing of existence and non-existence as [mere] objects — // MSA 11.42 //
the attainment of equality therein — the <s>Ārya</s> (noble) lineage (<s>gotra</s>) is indeed pure;
equal, distinguished, neither deficient nor excessive — this is considered the characterization. // MSA 11.43 //
The revolution (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) from the appearance of word-objects, bodies [and the like] — the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>)
element (<s>dhātu</s>) — [arises] from the revolution of the seed; and that is the universal basis (<s>sarvatragāśraya</s>). // MSA 11.44 //
Mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) is fourfold: in the functioning [of mind], in the apprehension by mind,

children.text: vikalpasyāvikalpe hi kṣetre jñāne 'tha karmaṇi // MSA_11.45 //
children.translated_text: and [in the cessation] of conceptualization in the non-conceptual — namely, in the field, in knowledge, and in action. // MSA 11.45 //
In the three stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) beginning with the immovable (<s>acalā</s>), that mastery is fourfold:
two in one [stage], and one each in the other [stages] — thus is mastery understood. // MSA 11.46 //

children.text: viditvā nairātmyaṃ dvividhamiha dhīmānbhavagataṃ samaṃ tacca jñātvā praviśati sa tatvaṃ grahaṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having understood the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) here, the wise one, having gone through the stages of existence, knowing that [selflessness] as equal, enters that reality through [correct] apprehension;

children.text: tatastatra sthānānmanasa iha na khyāti tadapi tadakhyānaṃ muktiḥ parama upalambhasya vigamaḥ // MSA_11.47 //
children.translated_text: then, from abiding therein, the mind no longer manifests here; and that very non-manifestation is liberation — the supreme cessation of apprehension. // MSA 11.47 //
In the support [of meditation], from the accumulation [of merit], when the basis is established, seeing mere name alone,

children.text: paśyati hi nāmamātraṃ tatpaśyaṃstacca naiva paśyati bhūyaḥ // MSA_11.48 //
children.translated_text: one sees mere name alone; and seeing that, one no longer sees even that. // MSA 11.48 //
This mind, perpetually corrupted, is bound by the view of self;
but its cessation is understood [to come] from the establishment of the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>). // MSA 11.49 //
From the non-existence of [things] by themselves, through their own nature, and from the non-establishment in [inherent] nature,
and from the non-existence of [the grasped] like [the absence of] the grasped — essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) is accepted. // MSA 11.50 //
[Established through essencelessness, with progressively higher foundations,
non-arising and non-cessation, primordial peace, and complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>.] // MSA 11.51 //
First regarding reality, otherness, own-characteristic, and then non-otherwise-ness,
in defilement and then in distinction — patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding non-arising is declared as the <s>dharma</s>. // MSA 11.52 //
Because of the equality of <s>dharma</s>, selflessness, and liberation, and from the difference of lineage (<s>gotra</s>),
and from the attainment of two dispositions, and from [the Buddha's] magical creation until the final [stage] — there is one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>). // MSA 11.53 //
For the purpose of attracting some, and for restraining others,
the one vehicle has been taught by the perfectly awakened ones, though provisionally, for the undetermined. // MSA 11.54 //
The undetermined <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) is of two kinds: from the vehicle of seen and unseen purpose;
the one of seen purpose is free from desire, while the one not yet free from desire is of gentle [disposition]. // MSA 11.55 //
Both of them, having attained the noble path, through maturation in the [various] states of existence,
are endowed with an inconceivable transformative rebirth. // MSA 11.56 //
One, through the power of [prior] vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), takes birth;
one, through the connection of non-returning (<s>anāgāmitā</s>), accomplishes [the goal] through magical creations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>). // MSA 11.57 //
And because of their delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, both are considered to be of slow progress,
due to the repeated functioning of their own mind [in that direction]. // MSA 11.58 //
Having not accomplished the goal, born in the unawakened [state], striving for meditation,
seeking magical creation — relying on that, one attains supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). // MSA 11.59 //

children.text: vidyāsthāne pañcavidhe yogamakṛtvā sarvajñatvaṃ naiti kathaṃcitparamāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without practicing in the five fields of knowledge, the supreme noble one cannot in any way attain omniscience;

children.text: ityanyeṣāṃ nigrahaṇānugrahaṇāya svājñārthaṃ vā tatra karotyeva sa yogam // MSA_11.60 //
children.translated_text: therefore, for the sake of defeating and assisting others, or for one's own knowledge, one indeed practices in those [fields]. // MSA 11.60 //
The satisfaction at finding the cause, its support, and the recollection of that;
the desire for a common result, and conviction in accordance with awakening. // MSA 11.61 //
Delight through fourfold power, and determination regarding hardship;
with regard to the opponent and the antidote — fourfold understanding. // MSA 11.62 //

children.text: prasādaḥ saṃpratīkṣā ca dānacchandaḥ paratra ca /
children.translated_text: Clarity, expectation, the aspiration to give, and for others [as well];
armoring [oneself], aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), rejoicing, and mental engagement. // MSA 11.63 //
Constant eagerness upon obtaining the capacity, sixfold in giving and the other [<s>pāramitās</s>];
in ripening, in worship, in service, and in compassion. // MSA 11.64 //

children.text: akṛte kukṛte lajjā kaukṛtyaṃ viṣaye ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: Shame at what is not done and what is badly done; remorse regarding sense-objects, delight;
perceiving hardship as an enemy; and the thought of arranging and cultivating [virtue]. // MSA 11.65 //
Giving and the other [<s>pāramitās</s>] are the refuge for awakening, not <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like;

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca pratisaṃvedanād [?]dvayoḥ // MSA_11.66 //
children.translated_text: [this is known] from the experience of both faults and virtues. // MSA 11.66 //
Recollecting the accumulation [of merit] and delight therein, and seeing its great purpose;
aspiration in yoga, in the non-conceptual, in maintaining that, and in gaining conviction. // MSA 11.67 //
Seeing the capacity for overcoming the sevenfold false grasping;

children.text: āścaryaṃ cāpyanāścaryaṃ saṃjñā caiva caturvidhā // MSA_11.68 //
children.translated_text: and the wonderful, the non-wonderful, and the fourfold perception. // MSA 11.68 //
Equanimity toward all sentient beings, and the great-souled vision;
counteracting others' virtues [by emulation], and the threefold unceasing aspiration. // MSA 11.69 //
From practicing what was taught by the <s>Buddha</s>, [and] from the intention of those in lower stages;
through [seeing] its decrease and increase in sentient beings — absence of joy [at others' loss] and rejoicing [at their gain]. // MSA 11.70 //
In comparison [with others], in meditation that has become [a practice] — there is no distaste;
no attachment, mental engagement, aspiration for [receiving] a prediction [of <s>Buddhahood</s>] and certainty. // MSA 11.71 //
For the future — seeing [the path], conduct, intention, and equanimous vision;
and through conduct regarding the highest <s>dharmas</s> — the determination of oneself as supreme. // MSA 11.72 //
These wholesome mental engagements, concordant with the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),

children.text: sarvadā bodhisattvānāṃ dhātupuṣṭau bhavanti hi // MSA_11.73 //
children.translated_text: belong to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> at all times, in the nourishment of the [Buddha-]element (<s>dhātu</s>). // MSA 11.73 //
From nourishment, through [superior] aspiration, a great quest is accepted by the steadfast ones;

children.text: savivāsā hyavivāsā tathaiva vaibhutvikī teṣām // MSA_11.74 //
children.translated_text: with attachment and without attachment, and also universal — such is their [quest]. // MSA 11.74 //
Without [a gross] body, with a light body, and with a fully complete body — [such are the states] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;
with great and subtle pride, and through magical creation — this quest is approved. // MSA 11.75 //
In the form and formless [realms], the <s>dharma</s>, its characteristics and causes, and likewise in well-being;
in sovereignty, through superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and in the inexhaustibility of those — [such is the quest] of the steadfast ones. // MSA 11.76 //
The conceptualizations of non-existence, existence, superimposition, denial, oneness, multiplicity, and non-distinction;
and the conceptualizations of [taking] names and objects as ultimately real — [all these] are to be abandoned by the children of the <s>Jina</s>. // MSA 11.77 //
Thus, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] of good understanding, having transcended this, with fierce effort, ever intent upon the quest for the true nature of <s>dharmas</s> as duality,

children.text: pratiśaraṇamataḥ sadā prajānāṃ bhavati guṇaiḥ sa samudravatprapūrṇaḥ // MSA_11.78 //
children.translated_text: becomes always a refuge for beings, filled with virtues like an ocean. // MSA 11.78 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eleventh chapter on the quest for <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>).
The twelfth chapter:
A verse on the prohibition of miserliness in teaching the <s>dharma</s>:

children.text: prāṇānbhogāṃśca dhīrāḥ pramuditamanasaḥ kṛcchralabdhānasārān satvebhyo duḥkhitebhyaḥ satatamavasṛjantyuccadānaprakāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: The steadfast, with joyful minds, constantly distribute to suffering sentient beings their lives and enjoyments — hard-won and worthless — through exalted forms of giving;

children.text: prāgevodāradharmaṃ hitakaramasakṛtsarvathaiva prajānāṃ kṛcchre naivopalabdhaṃ bhṛśamavasṛjatāṃ vṛddhigaṃ cāvyayaṃ ca // MSA_12.1 //
children.translated_text: how much more so the noble <s>dharma</s> that benefits beings in every way — not found in difficulty at all by those who abundantly distribute what is ever-increasing and imperishable! // MSA 12.1 //

children.text: dharmo naiva ca deśito bhagavatā pratyātmayavedyo yata ākṛṣṭā janatā ca yukta[yukti]vihitairdharmaiḥ svarkī dharmatāṃ /
children.translated_text: No <s>dharma</s> was taught by the Blessed One, since it is to be personally realized; yet beings have been drawn by <s>dharmas</s> established through reasoning toward the nature of <s>dharma</s> itself;

children.text: svaśāntyāsyapuṭe viśuddhivipule sādhāraṇe 'thākṣaye lāleneva kṛpātmabhistvajagaraprakhyaiḥ samāpāditā // MSA_12.2 //
children.translated_text: in the pure and vast, common and inexhaustible [dharma-]mouth of peace, they have been brought [to maturity] — as if by saliva — by those whose nature is compassion, resembling great serpents. // MSA 12.2 //

children.text: tasmānnaiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā bhāvanā yogināṃ tasmānnaiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā deśanā saugatī /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of yogins is not purposeless; therefore, the teaching of the followers of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) is not purposeless.

children.text: dṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ śrutamātrakādyadi bhavet syādbhāvanāpārthikā aśrutvā yadi bhāvanāmanuviśet syāddeśanāpārthikā // MSA_12.3 //
children.translated_text: If the goal were seen from mere hearing, meditation would be purposeless; if one entered meditation without hearing, teaching would be purposeless. // MSA 12.3 //
From scripture (<s>āgama</s>), from realization (<s>adhigama</s>), from pervasiveness, and from the supremacy of the teaching —
[teaching proceeds] from the mouth, from form, from everywhere, from space, and also through vocalization... // MSA 12.4 //
Clear, doubt-removing, acceptable, reality-revealing, and twofold —
this should be known as the accomplished teaching of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // MSA 12.5 //

children.text: madhurā madavyapetā na ca khinnā deśanāgrasatvānāṃ /
children.translated_text: Sweet, free from intoxication, and untired is the teaching of the supreme beings;
clear, variegated, well-connected, progressive, free from material enticement, and all-pervading. // MSA 12.6 //

children.text: adīnā madhurā sūktā pratītā viṣadā tathā [vāgjinātmaje] /
children.translated_text: Undaunted, sweet, well-spoken, comprehensible, clear — [such is the speech of the children of the <s>Jina</s>];
appropriate, unbiased, measured, and inexhaustible likewise.
From the topic (<s>uddeśa</s>), from the exposition (<s>nirdeśa</s>), likewise from conformity with the vehicle, from gentleness,
from dependent [arising], from appropriateness, from [leading to] liberation, and from agreeableness — // MSA 12.8 //
this perfection of expression (<s>vyañjanasaṃpat</s>) should be known in every way as [the quality] of the supreme beings;
having sixty aspects, it is inconceivable — the voice of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas) is indeed infinite. // MSA 12.9 //
Through speech, with well-joined words, through instruction, analysis, and the resolution of doubts,
[the teaching] follows the mode of elaboration, applied to those of extracted, detailed, and [comprehensive] knowledge. // MSA 12.10 //

children.text: śuddhā trimaṇḍalena hiteyaṃ deśanā hi buddhānāṃ /
children.translated_text: Pure by the three spheres [of giver, gift, and recipient], this teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> is beneficial.
It should be known as free from eight faults. // MSA 12.11 //
Laziness, lack of understanding, failure to provide opportunity, lack of guidance,
failure to resolve doubt, and failure to strengthen its removal. // MSA 12.12 //

children.text: khedo 'tha matsaritvaṃ doṣā hyete matā kathāyāṃ hi /
children.translated_text: Weariness and miserliness — these are considered the faults in discourse.
Because of their absence, the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> is unsurpassed. // MSA 12.13 //
This <s>Dharma</s> is excellent, because of being the cause of devotion, satisfaction, and understanding,
of twofold meaning, easy to grasp, and like the holy life of fourfold excellence. // MSA 12.14 //
Exclusively through a practice unshared with others, fulfilling the elimination of afflictions in the three realms,
pure by nature and pure from defilements — that is considered the holy life of fourfold excellence. // MSA 12.15 //
The hidden intention (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of introduction, and the hidden intention regarding characteristics,
the hidden intention of the antidote, and the hidden intention regarding transformation. // MSA 12.16 //
Regarding <s>Śrāvakas</s>, regarding essential natures, regarding the discipline of faults,
and regarding the profundity of expression — this hidden intention is fourfold. // MSA 12.17 //
Those who find essence in the essenceless, who are well-established in what is inverted,

children.text: kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭā labhante bodhimuktamāṃ // MSA_12.17* //
children.translated_text: and who are well-afflicted by defilements — they attain the supreme awakening. // MSA 12.17* //
|| Thus ||
Equality, [then] in another meaning, and likewise in another time,
and in the disposition of the person — the intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>) is fourfold. // MSA 12.18 //
Disrespect toward the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Dharma</s>, laziness, contentment with a mere trifle,

children.text: rāge māne caritaṃ kaukṛtaṃ cāniyatabhedaḥ // MSA_12.19 //
children.translated_text: conduct rooted in passion and pride, and remorse — [these are] the distinctions of the indeterminate [lineage]. // MSA 12.19 //
The obstruction of beings, its antidote being discourse on the supreme vehicle —
the elimination of all faults of obstacles for them arises therefrom. // MSA 12.20 //
One who applies himself to retaining even two verses, whether by text or by meaning,

children.text: sa hi daśavidhamanuśaṃsaṃ labhate satvottamo dhīmān // MSA_12.21 //
children.translated_text: that supreme being, the wise one, obtains tenfold benefit. // MSA 12.21 //

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ ca dhātupuṣṭiṃ prāmodyaṃ cottamaṃ maraṇakāle /
children.translated_text: Complete nourishment of the [spiritual] element, and supreme joy at the time of death,

children.text: janma ca yathābhikāmaṃ jātismaratāṃ ca sarvatra // MSA_12.22 //
children.translated_text: birth according to one's wish, and the remembrance of [past] births everywhere. // MSA 12.22 //
Meeting with <s>Buddhas</s>, hearing the supreme vehicle from them,

children.text: adhimuktiṃ saha buddhyā dvayamukhatāmāśubodhiṃ ca // MSA_12.23 //
children.translated_text: aspiration together with understanding, the twofold entrance, and swift awakening. // MSA 12.23 //
Thus, going well, unwearied, compassionate, of renowned fame, endowed with knowledge of proper method,

children.text: bhavati sukathiko hi bodhisattvastapati jane kathitairyathaiva sūryaḥ // MSA_12.24 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes an excellent teacher, shining upon people through his discourses, just as the sun. // MSA 12.24 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the twelfth chapter on teaching.
Thirteenth chapter:
Six verses in the section on the distinction of practice:
Having understood selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) as twofold — of person and of phenomena —
the wise one should abandon the falseness of both through the threefold [method]. // MSA 13.1 //
The knower of meaning understands the seed-like nature of all phenomena;
for the abandonment of complacency with [mere] learning, he is therefore called a knower of <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 13.2 //
Through the knowledge of an ordinary person, having penetrated both [kinds of selflessness],
upon the completion of that knowledge, one proceeds in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 13.3 //
Then one obtains supramundane, unsurpassed knowledge,
on the first stage, equal with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of that nature. // MSA 13.4 //
Having accomplished the complete destruction of afflictions to be abandoned through seeing,
one applies oneself to meditation for the abandonment of the obscurations to the knowable. // MSA 13.5 //
Through the non-conceptual knowledge that accompanies [right] determination,
one thus practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> on the remaining stages. // MSA 13.6 //
Easy to obtain, self-established, of excellent stage, with good companions,

children.text: suyogo guṇavān deśo yatra dhīmān prapadyate // MSA_13.7 //
children.translated_text: well-practiced, and endowed with virtues — [such is] the place where the wise one practices. // MSA 13.7 //
Learned, one who has seen the truth, eloquent, compassionate,

children.text: akhinno bodhisattvaśca jñeyaḥ satpurūṣo mahān // MSA_13.8 //
children.translated_text: unwearied — such a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be known as a great, true person. // MSA 13.8 //
Of proper support, well-sustained, well-cultivated and well-taught,
of excellent practice leading to the going forth — [such is] the proper exertion of the self. // MSA 13.9 //
The cause of delight, of the arising of the favorable moment, and of health,
as well as of <s>samādhi</s> and investigation — the prior accumulation of merit [is important]. // MSA 13.10 //
Since no <s>dharma</s> exists that is separate from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
therefore passion and the like are considered by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the escape for them. // MSA 13.11 //
Since no <s>dharma</s> exists that is separate from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
therefore, in the exposition of affliction, that is considered by the wise as the hidden intention. // MSA 13.12 //
Since one thoroughly penetrates those very passions and the like,
one is liberated from them — therefore, the escape from them comes from that. // MSA 13.13 //

children.text: na khalu jinasutānāṃ bādhakaṃ duḥkhamugraṃ narakabhavanavāsaiḥ satvahetoḥ kathaṃcit /
children.translated_text: Indeed, fierce suffering through dwelling in the hells is not an obstruction for the children of the <s>Jinas</s>, who [endure it] for the sake of beings.

children.text: śamabhavaguṇadoṣapreritā hīnayāne vividhaśubhavikalpā bādhakā dhīmatāṃ tu // MSA_13.14 //
children.translated_text: But in the inferior vehicle, diverse wholesome conceptualizations, impelled by the virtues and faults of cessation and existence, are obstructions for the wise. // MSA 13.14 //

children.text: na khalu narakavāso dhīmatāṃ sarvakālaṃ vimalavipulabodherantarāyaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Indeed, dwelling in hell does not at all times create an obstacle for the wise to stainless, vast awakening.
But in the other vehicle, the conceptualization focused on one's own benefit and supreme calm, even in the abode of supreme bliss, creates an obstacle. // MSA 13.15 //
The apprehension of the non-existence of phenomena, and the purity of non-affliction —
this should be known as similar to illusion and the like, and likewise similar to space. // MSA 13.16 //

children.text: yathaiva citre vidhivadvicitrite natonnataṃ nāsti ca dṛśyate 'tha ca /
children.translated_text: Just as in a painting, properly made with variety, there is no height or depth, yet it appears so,

children.text: abhūtakalpe 'pi tathaiva sarvathā dvayaṃ sadā nāsti ca dṛśyate 'the ca // MSA_13.17 //
children.translated_text: so too in false imagination, in every way, duality never exists, yet it appears. // MSA 13.17 //

children.text: yathaiva toye luti[ṭi]te prasādite na jāyate sā punaracchatānyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as when water that was turbid becomes clear, that clarity does not arise from elsewhere;

children.text: malāpakarṣastu sa tatra kevalaḥ svacittaśuddhau vidhireṣa eva hi // MSA_13.18 //
children.translated_text: it is merely the removal of impurity there — this indeed is the method for the purification of one's own mind. // MSA 13.18 //

children.text: mataṃ ca cittaṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ sadā tadāgantukadoṣadūṣitaṃ /
children.translated_text: And it is held that the mind is luminous by nature, [though] always defiled by adventitious defilements.

children.text: na dharmatācittamṛte 'nyacetasaḥ prabhāsvaratvaṃ prakṛtau vidhīyate // MSA_13.19 //
children.translated_text: Apart from the <s>dharmatā</s>-mind, no luminosity of nature is established for another mind. // MSA 13.19 //
The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s love for beings, deeply immersed, is great —
like [love] for an only child; therefore, it is considered as always beneficial. // MSA 13.20 //
Because of acting beneficially toward beings, he does not incur transgression born of passion.

children.text: dveṣo virudyate tvasya sarvasatveṣu satpathā[sarvathā] // MSA_13.21 //
children.translated_text: But aversion is opposed to his [attitude] toward all beings in every way. // MSA 13.21 //
Just as a dove, exceedingly tender toward her offspring, remains embracing them by nature,

children.text: tathāvidhāyaṃ pratigho virudhyate suteṣu tadvatsakṛpe 'pi dehiṣu // MSA_13.22 //
children.translated_text: so aversion of this kind is opposed [in him] — compassionate toward embodied beings as toward [his own] children. // MSA 13.22 //

children.text: maitrī yataḥ pratighacittamato viruddhaṃ śāntiryato vyasanacittamato viruddhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Since loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) — the mind of hostility is therefore opposed; since peace — the mind of misfortune is therefore opposed;

children.text: artho yato nikṛticittamato viruddhaṃ lhādo yataḥ pratibhayaṃ na[ca] tato viruddhaṃ // MSA_13.23 //
children.translated_text: since purpose — the mind of deceit is therefore opposed; since joy — fear is therefore opposed. // MSA 13.23 //
Just as a sick person regards good medicine — so one regards <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: āture ca yathā vaidyaḥ satveṣu pratipadyate // MSA_13.24 //
children.translated_text: and just as a physician regards the sick — so one regards beings. // MSA 13.24 //
Just as [one regards] an unfinished servant — so one regards oneself;

children.text: vaṇigyathā punaḥ puṇye kāmeṣu pratipadyate // MSA_13.25 //
children.translated_text: just as a merchant regards profit — so one regards merit in [the midst of] desires. // MSA 13.25 //
Just as a washerman regards a garment for work — so one regards action;

children.text: pitā yathā sute bāle satvāheṭhe prapadyate // MSA_13.26 //
children.translated_text: just as a father regards a young child — so one regards helpless beings. // MSA 13.26 //
Just as one seeking fire regards the lower fire-stick — so one regards perseverance;
just as one who is trustworthy [regards] an unfinished [task] — so one regards the higher mind. // MSA 13.27 //
Just as a magician [regards] what is to be known — so one regards [the knowable] with wisdom.

children.text: pratipattiryathā yasmin bodhisattvasya sā matā // MSA_13.28 //
children.translated_text: Such is the practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as it is considered. // MSA 13.28 //
Thus, always noble, endowed with effort, well-applied in ripening and purifying both [beings and buddha-fields],

children.text: paramavimalanirvikalpabuddhyā vrajati sa siddhimanuttamāṃ krameṇa // MSA_13.29 //
children.translated_text: with supremely stainless, non-conceptual understanding, one gradually proceeds to the unsurpassed attainment. // MSA 13.29 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the thirteenth chapter on practice.
Fourteenth chapter:
Fifty-one verses in the section on instruction and guidance:
Having emerged from incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, developing aspiration,
filled with wholesome qualities, like an ocean with waters. // MSA 14.1 //
Thus, the child of the <s>Jinas</s>, having accumulated the provisions, in the initial purification,
well-discerning and with a pliant mind, applies oneself to meditation. // MSA 14.2 //
Then, in the stream of <s>Dharma</s>, one receives instruction from the <s>Buddhas</s>,
vast, for the purpose of entering into the fullness of tranquility-knowledge. // MSA 14.3 //
Then, in the <s>Dharma</s> of sūtras and the like, which reveals the meaning of non-duality,
the practitioner should first bind the mind to what is called sūtra and the like. // MSA 14.4 //
Then one should examine the divisions of words in succession;
and one should investigate their meanings, personally and thoroughly. // MSA 14.5 //
Having ascertained those meanings, one should again collect [them] in the <s>Dharma</s>;
then one should encourage oneself for the realization of those meanings. // MSA 14.6 //
One should seek and examine through continuous mental discourse,
and should investigate through mental attentions that are free from discourse and of one flavor. // MSA 14.7 //
The path of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) should be known as the collected [<s>Dharma</s>];
the path of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) should be known as the investigation of those meanings. // MSA 14.8 //
The path of their union (<s>yuganaddha</s>) should be known as their collection again.
One should seize the sunken mind and calm the agitated [mind]. // MSA 14.9 //
One should maintain equanimity toward the [mind that has] attained calm; and again, regarding that object,
continuously, and with respect, one should apply [the mind] to everything. // MSA 14.10 //
Having bound the mind to the object, one should not let its flow be scattered;
having quickly noticed distraction, one should again bring [the mind] back to it. // MSA 14.11 //
The wise one should progressively gather the mind inwardly, again and again;
then one should tame the mind for <s>samādhi</s>, through seeing its virtues. // MSA 14.12 //
One should calm displeasure therein, through seeing the faults of distraction;
likewise, one should calm covetousness, ill-will, and the like when they have arisen. // MSA 14.13 //
Then, [having attained] the effortful [state], and the spontaneous flow in the mind,
the practitioner obtains the effortless [state] again through practice of that. // MSA 14.14 //

children.text: tataḥ sa tanukāṃ labdhvā praśrabdhiṃ kāyacetasoḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained subtle tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of body and mind,

children.text: vijñeyaḥ samanaskāraḥ punastān [stāṃ] sa vivardhayan // MSA_14.15 //
children.translated_text: one should be known as having [full] mental attention; and further, by increasing that — // MSA 14.15 //
through the far-reaching [quality] of growth, one attains the stabilized absorption;
purifying that, for the purpose of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), one reaches supreme pliancy. // MSA 14.16 //
Through the accomplishment of superknowledges in <s>dhyāna</s>, one goes to world-systems,
for the worship of immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> and for hearing [the <s>Dharma</s>]. // MSA 14.17 //
Having attended upon immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> through immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>,
one attains supreme pliancy of mind from that attendance. // MSA 14.18 //

children.text: tato 'nuśaṃsān labhate pañca śuddhaiḥ sa pūrvagān /
children.translated_text: Then, through the prior pure [attainments], one obtains the five benefits,

children.text: viśuddhibhājanatvaṃ ca tato yāni niruttaraṃ // MSA_14.19 //
children.translated_text: and the capacity for the unsurpassed purification. // MSA 14.19 //
The body melts from all its coarseness at every moment,

children.text: āpūryate ca praśrabdhyā kāyacittaṃ samantataḥ // MSA_14.20 //
children.translated_text: and is filled completely with the tranquility of body and mind. // MSA 14.20 //
One knows the unlimited appearance of all phenomena everywhere;
one perceives the signs, uncreated, in [the state of] purification. // MSA 14.21 //

children.text: prapūrau ca viśuddhau ca dharmakāyasya sarvathā /
children.translated_text: For the fulfillment and purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> in every way,
the wise one constantly gathers the causes thus. // MSA 14.22 //
Then, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being thus, composed in <s>samādhi</s> —
One does not perceive any objects apart from mental fabrication. // MSA_14.23 //
For the increase of the light of <s>Dharma</s>, one exerts firm <s>vīrya</s> (vigor),
And through the increase of the light of <s>Dharma</s>, one abides in <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). // MSA_14.24 //
Then one perceives the appearance of all objects within the mind,
At that time, the distraction toward the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>) is eliminated for that one. // MSA_14.25 //
Then only the distraction toward the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>) remains for that one,

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiṃ ca spṛśatyāśu tadā punaḥ // MSA_14.26 //
children.translated_text: And then again one quickly touches the <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> (immediate concentration). // MSA_14.26 //
Whereupon the distraction toward the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>) diminishes, immediately thereafter
These stages beginning with <s>ūṣmagata</s> (warmth) and so forth are to be known in their proper sequence. // MSA_14.27 //
Free from the grasping of duality, supramundane, unsurpassed,

children.text: nirvikalpaṃ malāpetaṃ jñānaṃ sa labhate punaḥ // MSA_14.28 //
children.translated_text: Non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) and free from defilement — one then obtains such <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). // MSA_14.28 //
This transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) is regarded as the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage),

children.text: ameyaiścāsya sā kalpaiḥ suviśuddhiṃ nigacchati // MSA_14.29 //
children.translated_text: And through immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), it reaches complete purification. // MSA_14.29 //
Having then realized the sameness of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality),
One attains an equal mind toward all beings, always seeing the self as equal. // MSA_14.30 //
Regarding selflessness, the meaning of suffering, duty, and the absence of counteraction,
That one is of equal mind toward beings, just as other <s>Jinātmaja</s>s (sons of the Conqueror). // MSA_14.31 //
The formations of self in the three realms, arising from <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination),
One sees with thoroughly purified <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) whose object is non-duality. // MSA_14.32 //
And the existence of the absence of that, which is free from views that are to be abandoned —

children.text: labdhvā darśanamārgo hi tadā tena nirūcyate // MSA_14.33 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained this, the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing) is then declared by that. // MSA_14.33 //
Having known the emptiness of non-existence, and likewise the emptiness of existence,

children.text: prakṛtyā śūnyatāṃ jñātvā śūnyajña iti kathyate // MSA_14.34 //
children.translated_text: Having known the emptiness of intrinsic nature — one is called a knower of emptiness. // MSA_14.34 //
The state of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>) is to be known as the cessation of conceptualizations,
And <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination) is that of the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). // MSA_14.35 //

children.text: tena darśanamārgeṇa saha lābhaḥ sadā mataḥ /
children.translated_text: Through that <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing), a <s>Jinātmaja</s> (son of the Conqueror) is considered
To always obtain all the various factors of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). // MSA_14.36 //
Having understood that the world is mere formations (<s>saṃskāramātra</s>), selfless, merely the growth of suffering,

children.text: vihāya yānarthamayātmadṛṣṭiḥ mahātmadṛṣṭiṃ śrayate mahārthāṃ // MSA_14.37 //
children.translated_text: Abandoning the self-view that pursues vehicle-goals, one resorts to the great self-view that has great purpose. // MSA_14.37 //
One who without self-view has self-view, and without suffering is greatly afflicted,

children.text: sarvārthakartā na ca kārakāṅkṣī yathātmanaḥ svātmahitāni kṛtvā // MSA_14.38 //
children.translated_text: Who accomplishes all purposes yet does not seek an agent — as if performing benefits for oneself by oneself. // MSA_14.38 //

children.text: yo muktacittaḥ parayā vimuktyā baddhaśca gāḍhāyatabandhanena /
children.translated_text: One whose mind is liberated by the supreme liberation, yet is bound by the firm and extensive bonds,

children.text: duḥkhasya paryantamapaśyamānaḥ prayujyate caiva karoti caiva // MSA_14.39 //
children.translated_text: Not seeing an end to suffering, yet engages and acts. // MSA_14.39 //
The world is unable to bear even its own suffering — how much less the accumulated suffering of others?

children.text: janmaikamālokayate[gataṃ] tvacinto viparyayāttasya tu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_14.40 //
children.translated_text: One looks upon even a single birth as inconceivable — but the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does the opposite of that. // MSA_14.40 //

children.text: yatprema yā vatsalatā prayogaḥ satveṣvakhedaśca jinātmajānāṃ /
children.translated_text: The love, the tenderness, the effort, and the tirelessness toward beings of the <s>Jinātmaja</s>s (sons of the Conqueror) —

children.text: āścaryametatparamaṃ bhaveṣu na caiva satvātmasamānabhāvāt // MSA_14.41 //
children.translated_text: This is the supreme wonder in all existences, and it is not so because of the sameness of beings and self. // MSA_14.41 //
Then on the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of cultivation), on the remaining <s>bhūmi</s>s (stages),
One engages in the cultivation of twofold <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). // MSA_14.42 //
That non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) <s>jñāna</s> purifies the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>s,
And the other, which is knowledge of how things are established, ripens beings. // MSA_14.43 //
The culmination of cultivation comes from the completion of two incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
Having reached the final cultivation, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is consecrated (<s>abhiṣikta</s>). // MSA_14.44 //
Having attained the <s>vajropama-samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration), indestructible by conceptualization,
The ultimate transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), stainless from all obstructions, // MSA_14.45 //
One obtains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), the unsurpassed state,
Wherein one abides and acts for the benefit of all beings. // MSA_14.46 //

children.text: kathaṃ tathā durlabhadarśane munau bhavenmahārthaṃ na hi nityadarśanaṃ /
children.translated_text: How could seeing of the <s>Muni</s> (sage), so rare to encounter, be of great purpose if it were constant?
For one whose mind is always greatly nourished by waves of faith born from incomparable hearing. // MSA_14.47 //

children.text: a[pra]codyamānaḥ satataṃ ca saṃmukhaṃ tathāgatairdharmasu[mu]khe vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unprompted and always face-to-face, established at the gateway of the <s>Dharma</s> by the <s>Tathāgata</s>s,

children.text: nigṛhya keśeṣviva doṣagahvarāt nikṛṣya bodhau sa balānniveśyate // MSA_14.48 //
children.translated_text: As if seized by the hair from the pit of faults, one is forcibly dragged out and established in <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). // MSA_14.48 //
That one, having overcome the entire world through thoroughly purified visions and aeon-spanning awakenings in every way,

children.text: mahāndhakāraṃ vidhamayya bhāsate jaganmahāditya ivātyudārataḥ // MSA_14.49 //
children.translated_text: Dispelling the great darkness, shines forth like the great sun of the world, with supreme magnificence. // MSA_14.49 //

children.text: buddhāḥ samyakpraśaṃsāṃ vidadhati satataṃ svārthasamyakprayukte, nindāmīrṣyāprayukte sthitivicayapare cāntarāyānukūlān /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>s constantly bestow proper praise upon one who is rightly engaged in one's own purpose, and censure one engaged in envy; the <s>Jina</s>s show to the foremost being all kinds of <s>dharma</s>s that are favorable to the removal of obstacles and that are concerned with stability and investigation, in the proper manner,

children.text: dharmān sarvaprakārānvidhivadiha jinā darśayantyagrasatve, yān varjyāsevya yoge bhavati vipulatā saugate śāsane 'smim // MSA_14.50 //
children.translated_text: Which, when practiced in yoga and avoiding what should be avoided, bring about vastness in this teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>. // MSA_14.50 //

children.text: iti satataśubhācayaprapūrṇaḥ suvipulametya sa cetasaḥ samādhiṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus that foremost being, filled with the continuous accumulation of merit, having attained a vast <s>samādhi</s> of the mind,
Always receiving the great exhortation of the <s>Muni</s>, reaches the far shore of the ocean of virtues. // MSA_14.51 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fourteenth chapter on exhortation and instruction.
Fifteenth chapter.
<s>Uddāna</s> (summary verses):
In the section on action accompanied by skillful means, four verses:
Abundant faith, seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, teaching,
Proper practice, and exhortation and instruction. // MSA_15.1 //
Just as the earth is the foundation everywhere for forests, bodies, mountains, and rivers,

children.text: tathaiva dānādiśubhasya sarvato budheṣu karma trividhaṃ nirucyate // MSA_15.2 //
children.translated_text: So likewise threefold action toward the wise is declared as the basis for all merit beginning with <s>dāna</s> (generosity). // MSA_15.2 //
For the <s>Jinātmaja</s>s (sons of the Conqueror), who are devoted to extremely difficult actions of various forms, extending over many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: na kāyavāk cittamayasya karmaṇo jinātmajānāṃ bhavatīha saṃnatiḥ // MSA_15.3 //
children.translated_text: There is no weariness of action consisting of body, speech, and mind. // MSA_15.3 //
Just as one who seeks one's own welfare would protect one's own body from poison, weapons, and great fire, and from enemies,
So a <s>Jinātmaja</s> (son of the Conqueror) would guard against the twofold action of the inferior vehicle, the threefold action. // MSA_15.4 //

children.text: na karmiṇaḥ karma na karmaṇaḥ kriyāṃ sadāvikalpaḥ samudīkṣate tridhā /
children.translated_text: One who is always non-conceptual does not perceive the agent of action, the action of the agent, or the act in three ways,

children.text: tato 'sya tatkarma viśuddhipāragaṃ bhavatyanantaṃ tadupāyasaṃgrahāt // MSA_15.5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore that action of one's reaches the shore of purity, becoming infinite through the collection of skillful means. // MSA_15.5 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fifteenth chapter on action accompanied by skillful means.
Sixteenth chapter.
Summary verse on the classification of <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections):
In the section on enumeration and classification, six verses:
Their number, characteristics, sequence, etymology, practice, and qualities,

children.text: prabhedanaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ vipakṣo jñeyo guṇo 'nyonyaviniścayaśca // MSA_16.1 //
children.translated_text: Their classification, summary, opposition, quality, and mutual determination are to be known. // MSA_16.1 //
Wealth, embodiment, excellence, service, undertaking, excellence, higher attainment,
Not being under the power of <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions), and never being deluded in one's duties. // MSA_16.2 //
One who is well-engaged in the purposes of beings accomplishes through renunciation, non-harm, and forbearance,
And through the ground of abiding, liberation with cause, one pursues one's own purpose in every way. // MSA_16.3 //
Through non-obstruction, non-affliction, endurance of affliction, tirelessness in action,

children.text: āvarjanaiḥ sulapitaiḥ parārtha ātmārtha etasmāt // MSA_16.4 //
children.translated_text: Attraction, and well-spoken words — the purpose of others comes from the purpose of self. // MSA_16.4 //
Intense non-delight in sense pleasures, reverence toward the two, tirelessness,
And non-conceptual yoga — all this is the supreme vehicle. // MSA_16.5 //
One path for non-attachment to objects, another for attainment, distraction, and restraint,
Another for not abandoning beings, their increase, and the purification of obstructions. // MSA_16.6 //

children.text: śikṣātrayamadhikṛtya ca ṣaṣṭ pāramitā jinaiḥ samākhyātāḥ /
children.translated_text: The six <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections) are taught by the <s>Jina</s>s with reference to the three trainings (<s>śikṣātraya</s>),
The first three in two ways, and one from the last two in each of the three. // MSA_16.7 //

children.text: dānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nivikalpena /
children.translated_text: <s>Dāna</s> (generosity), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.8 //

children.text: śīlaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena /
children.translated_text: <s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.9 //
<s>Kṣānti</s> (patience), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.10 //

children.text: vīryaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nivikalpena /
children.translated_text: <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.11 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.12 //

children.text: prajñā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena /
children.translated_text: <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), free from its opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
Fulfilling all wishes and ripening beings — threefold. // MSA_16.13 //
The teaching is in that order, based on the prior being the support of the subsequent and their arising,
From the standpoint of the inferior and the superior, and from the coarse and the subtle. // MSA_16.14 //
The explanation is from the removal of poverty, the attainment of coolness, the destruction of anger,
And from the excellence of yoga, mental concentration, and knowledge of the ultimate meaning. // MSA_16.15 //
With reference to the substratum of cultivation, mental attention, disposition,

children.text: upāyaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ ca sarvāsāmeva kathyate // MSA_16.16 //
children.translated_text: Skillful means, and sovereignty — it is stated for all of them. // MSA_16.16 //
The giving of objects, intention as the established root,
The excellence of wealth and embodiment, fulfilling the benefit of both. // MSA_16.17 //
That which is accompanied by non-miserliness, free from the fear of visible benefit,
Having thus fully understood <s>dāna</s> (generosity), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.18 //
Having six limbs, ending in tranquility, bestowing a good rebirth,
A foundation for peace and fearlessness, endowed with the accumulation of merit, // MSA_16.19 //
Obtained through conventional and ultimate reality (<s>dharmatā</s>), it is found among those who are restrained —
Having thus fully understood <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.20 //
Forbearance, patient endurance, and knowledge — from compassion and reliance on the <s>Dharma</s>,
Five benefits are declared, and it serves the purpose of both. // MSA_16.21 //
Endowed with the strength of austerity, it is regarded as threefold among those,
Having thus fully understood <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.22 //

children.text: dvayorarthaṃ sa kurūte ātmanaśca parasya ca /
children.translated_text: One serves the purpose of both, of oneself and of the other,

children.text: yaḥ paraṃ kupitaṃ jñātvā svayaṃ tatropaśāmyati // MSA_16.22* //
children.translated_text: Who, having known the other to be angered, oneself becomes pacified therein. // MSA_16.22* //
|| Thus ||
Zeal in the wholesome, rightly established in faith and aspiration,
For the increase of qualities such as <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and others, it is the antidote to afflictions. // MSA_16.23 //
Endowed with qualities such as non-greed and others, it is sevenfold among those,
Having thus fully understood <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.24 //
Stability of mind internally, established in <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>vīrya</s> (vigor),
For the attainment of happiness, it governs the abode of <s>abhijñā</s> (supernormal knowledge). // MSA_16.25 //

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ pramukhaṃ teṣu vidyate trividhaśca saḥ /
children.translated_text: It is foremost among <s>dharma</s>s, and it is threefold among those,
Having thus fully understood <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.26 //
Right investigation of what is to be known, established in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),
For complete liberation from affliction, teaching the livelihood of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). // MSA_16.27 //
It is the highest among <s>dharma</s>s, and it is threefold among those,
Having thus fully understood <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the wise one should undertake it. // MSA_16.28 //
All wholesome <s>dharma</s>s should be known as scattered, concentrated, and both,

children.text: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ pāramitābhyāṃ parigṛhītāḥ // MSA_16.29 //
children.translated_text: Comprised by two, two, and two <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections) respectively. // MSA_16.29 //

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca dānaṃ /
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached — the <s>dāna</s> (generosity) is indeed not attached,

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām // MSA_16.30 //
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached — that of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. // MSA_16.30 //

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca śīlaṃ /
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached — the <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) is indeed not attached,

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisatvānām // MSA_16.31 //
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached — that of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>s. // MSA_16.31 //

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā sattikā na kṣāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — the patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached;

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā bodhisattvānām // MSA_16.32 //
children.translated_text: neither attached, nor attached, nor attached. MSA 16.32

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva ca na vīryaṃ /
children.translated_text: Neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — the vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is indeed not attached;

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām // MSA_16.33 //
children.translated_text: neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — [the vigor] of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. MSA 16.33

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca dhyānaṃ /
children.translated_text: Neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is indeed not attached;

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām // MSA_16.34 //
children.translated_text: neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — [the meditation] of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. MSA 16.34

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā saktikā na ca prajñā /
children.translated_text: Neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is not attached;

children.text: na ca saktā na ca sakta na ca saktā bodhisattvānām // MSA_16.35 //
children.translated_text: neither attached, nor attached, nor attached — [the wisdom] of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. MSA 16.35

children.text: tyaktaṃ buddhasutaiḥ svajīvitamapi prāpyārthinaṃ sarvadā kāruṇyātparato na ca pratikṛtirneṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prārthitaṃ /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> always give up even their own life when they encounter a supplicant, out of compassion; and no reciprocation is sought, nor is any fruit desired;

children.text: dānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā dānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'jñayaṃ sthāpitam // MSA_16.36 //
children.translated_text: and through that very giving, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s> (awakening); and that giving, embraced by knowledge, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.36

children.text: āttaṃ buddhasutairyamodyamamayaṃ śīlatrayaṃ sarvadā svargo nābhimataḥ sametya ca punaḥ saktirna tatrāhitā /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> always undertake the threefold morality (<s>śīla</s>), which consists of disciplined effort; heaven is not desired, and having attained it, no attachment is placed there;

children.text: śīlenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā śīlaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam // MSA_16.37 //
children.translated_text: and through that very morality, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s>; and that morality, embraced by knowledge, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.37

children.text: kṣāntaṃ buddhasutaiḥ suduṣkaramatho sarvāpakāraṃ nṛṇāṃ na svargārthamasa[śa]ktimato na ca bhayānnaivopakārekṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> endure all offenses of people, [which are] extremely difficult [to bear]; not for the sake of heaven, not out of incapacity, not out of fear, and not with a view to reciprocal benefit;

children.text: kṣāntyānuttarayā ca sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā kṣāntirjñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayā sthāpitā // MSA_16.38 //
children.translated_text: and through that unsurpassed patience, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s>; and that patience, embraced by knowledge, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.38

children.text: vīryaṃ buddhasutaiḥ kṛtaṃ nirūpamaṃ saṃnāhayogātmakaṃ hantuṃ kleśagaṇaṃ svato 'pi parataḥ prāptuṃ ca bodhiṃ parāṃ /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> practice incomparable vigor, consisting of armor-like [resolve] and [actual] engagement, to destroy the host of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) both in themselves and in others, and to attain supreme <s>bodhi</s>;

children.text: vīryeṇaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā vīryaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam // MSA_16.39 //
children.translated_text: and through that very vigor, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s>; and that vigor, embraced by knowledge, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.39

children.text: dhyānaṃ buddhasutaiḥ samādhibahulaṃ saṃpāditaṃ sarvathā śreṣṭhairdhyānasukhairvihṛtya kṛpayā hīnāpapattiḥ śritā /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> cultivate meditation rich in <s>samādhi</s> in every way; having dwelt in the supreme bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>, out of compassion they resort to rebirth in the lower [realms];

children.text: dhyānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā dhyānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam // MSA_16.40 //
children.translated_text: and through that very meditation, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s>; and that meditation, embraced by knowledge, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.40

children.text: jñātaṃ buddhasutaiḥ satatvamakhilaṃ jñeyaṃ ca yatsarvathā saktirnaiva ca nirvṛtau prajanitā buddhaiḥ[ddheḥ] kutaḥ saṃvṛtau /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> know all that exists, together with its beings, and all that is to be known, in every way; no attachment whatsoever is produced toward <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) — how much less toward <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional [reality]);

children.text: jñānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā jñānaṃ satvaparigraheṇa punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam // MSA_16.41 //
children.translated_text: and through that very knowledge, all beings are planted in the threefold <s>bodhi</s>; and that knowledge, embraced by the care of beings, is established imperishably in the world. MSA 16.41
Generosity, non-material nature, great purposefulness, and inexhaustibility —

children.text: dānādīnāṃ samastaṃ hi jñeyaṃ guṇacatuṣṭayam // MSA_16.42 //
children.translated_text: these should be known as the fourfold quality of giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the other [perfections]. MSA 16.42
A supplicant who has obtained what is desired abundantly experiences satisfaction at seeing [the donor];

children.text: abhibhavati sa tāṃ dātā kṛpālurādhikyayogena // MSA_16.43 //
children.translated_text: the compassionate giver surpasses even that dissatisfaction [of the supplicant] through his exceeding generosity. MSA 16.43
Out of compassion for beings, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] always delights abundantly in [giving away] life, enjoyments, and spouses to others;

children.text: āmodate nikāmaṃ tadviratiṃ pālayetra katham // MSA_16.44 //
children.translated_text: how then would he observe abstinence from that [giving]? MSA 16.44
Without regard [for self], equanimous, fearless, giving everything, for the sake of compassion —
how could a noble one speak falsehood for the purpose of harming others? MSA 16.45
With well-composed desires, compassionate, and extremely apprehensive about causing suffering to others,
skilled in the discipline of beings — he is far removed from the threefold fault of speech. MSA 16.46
Giving everything, compassionate, and well-skilled in the arising of <s>dharma</s> through dependent origination —
how could he allow mental <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of any kind? MSA 16.47
When the compassionate one, toward one who harms him, [maintains] the perception of benefit and joy, and the perception of [engaging in] the welfare of others amid suffering,

children.text: labhate yadā kṛpāluḥ kṣamitavyaṃ ..........[kiṃ kutasyasya] // MSA_16.48 //
children.translated_text: what then is there to be endured [for such a one]? MSA 16.48
Due to the abandonment of the perception of self and other, due to always having greater affection for others than for oneself,
and due to the practice of difficult austerities — for the compassionate one, vigor is not difficult. MSA 16.49

children.text: alpasukhaṃ hyātmasukhaṃ līnaṃ parihāṇikaṃ kṣayi samohaṃ /
children.translated_text: The meditation of the three [vehicles, excluding the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s] is considered to be of little happiness, withdrawn, subject to decline, perishable, and with delusion;
the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' [meditation] is the opposite of all these. MSA 16.50
Just as in darkness [things are illuminated] by theft-like lamps, so is the knowledge of the three [vehicles];
but the incomparable knowledge of the compassionate ones is like the rays of the sun. MSA 16.51
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetranniśrayācca paraṃ matam // MSA_16.52 //
children.translated_text: cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — giving (<s>dāna</s>) is considered supreme. MSA 16.52
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam // MSA_16.53 //
children.translated_text: cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — morality (<s>śīla</s>) is considered supreme. MSA 16.53
cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is considered supreme.
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam // MSA_16.54 //
children.translated_text: cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is considered supreme. MSA 16.54
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam // MSA_16.55 //
children.translated_text: cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is considered supreme. MSA 16.55
With respect to basis, substance, object, transference,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetranniśrayācca parā matā // MSA_16.56 //
children.translated_text: cause, knowledge, field, and reliance — wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is considered supreme. MSA 16.56
Giving that [brings about] the happiness of even a single being, [even if] it destroys many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
should be dear to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — how much more so [giving] that is the opposite of this [i.e., that benefits many]. MSA 16.57

children.text: yadarthamicchanti dhanāni dehinastadeva dhīrā visṛjanti dehiṣu /
children.translated_text: That for the sake of which embodied beings desire wealth — that very thing the courageous ones give away to embodied beings;

children.text: śarīrahetordhanamiṣyate janaistadeva dhīraiḥ śataśo visṛjyate // MSA_16.58 //
children.translated_text: wealth is desired by people for the sake of the body — that very [body] the courageous ones give away a hundredfold. MSA 16.58

children.text: śarīrāmevotsṛjato na duḥkhyate yadā manaḥ kā draviṇe 'vare kathā /
children.translated_text: When the mind does not suffer even while giving up the body itself — what need to speak of inferior wealth?

children.text: tadasya lokottaramiti yanmudaṃ sa tena tattasya taduttaraṃ punaḥ // MSA_16.59 //
children.translated_text: That joy of his is supramundane — and that [joy] is therefore greater than that [worldly joy]. MSA 16.59
A supplicant who has obtained desirable gifts to his heart's content does not attain as much satisfaction,

children.text: sarvāstidānena yatheha dhīmān tuṣṭiṃ vrajatyarthijanasya tuṣṭyā // MSA_16.60 //
children.translated_text: as the wise one here attains through giving everything — [he attains] satisfaction through the satisfaction of the needy. MSA 16.60
Even one who possesses complete enjoyments does not regard himself as wealthy to such an extent, nor does a supplicant [regard himself so];
as the wise one, even though without wealth through having given everything, regards himself as wealthy. MSA 16.61

children.text: suvipulamapi vittaṃ prāpya naivopakāraṃ vigaṇayati tathāthī dāyakāllābhahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Even having obtained very abundant wealth, the needy one does not consider the benefit from the donor [as great enough] for the sake of gain;

children.text: vidhivadiha sudānairarthinastarpayitvā mahadupakarasaṃjñāṃ teṣu dhīmānyathaiti // MSA_16.62 //
children.translated_text: but the wise one, having properly satisfied the supplicants with excellent giving, develops a great perception of gratitude toward them. MSA 16.62

children.text: svayamapagataśokā dehinaḥ svastharūpā vipulamapi gṛhītvā bhuñjate yasya vittaṃ /
children.translated_text: Embodied beings, free from sorrow, healthy in form, partake of his abundant wealth,

children.text: pathi paramaphalāḍhyādbhogavṛkṣādyathaiva pravisṛtiratibhogī bodhisattvānna so 'nyaḥ // MSA_16.63 //
children.translated_text: just as [travelers partake] from a wish-fulfilling tree on the path, rich with supreme fruits — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is no different from that most bountiful [tree]. MSA 16.63
Through distinctions of primacy, its cause, action, mode,
basis, and the fourfold remedy for the [four] bonds — vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is to be fully understood, thus it is declared. MSA 16.64

children.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ śuklagaṇasya madhye tanniśritastasya yato 'nulābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Vigor is supreme among the host of virtues; relying on it, there is attainment of all [other virtues];

children.text: vīryeṇa sadyaḥ susukho vihāro lokottarā lokagatāṃ ca siddhiḥ // MSA_16.65 //
children.translated_text: through vigor, there is immediately a very blissful abiding, and the accomplishment of both supramundane and worldly [goals]. MSA 16.65
Through vigor, the desired enjoyments of existence are obtained; through vigor, [beings] attain powerful purification;

children.text: vīryeṇa satkāyamatītya muktā vīryeṇa bodhiṃ paramāṃ vibuddhāḥ // MSA_16.66 //
children.translated_text: through vigor, having transcended the compounded [personality], they are liberated; through vigor, they are awakened to supreme <s>bodhi</s>. MSA 16.66
Furthermore, vigor [is classified as] that of decline and growth, that governing liberation, that pertaining to sides and their opposites,

children.text: tattve praviṣṭaṃ parivartakaṃ ca vīryaṃ mahārthaṃ ca niruktamanyat // MSA_16.67 //
children.translated_text: that which has entered reality, and that which transforms — and another [kind] of vigor is declared to be of great purpose. MSA 16.67
First, armor-like vigor (<s>saṃnāhavīrya</s>), then engagement vigor (<s>prayogavīrya</s>), properly dispatched,
unwavering, unshakeable, and vigor of dissatisfaction [with achievements] — all these kinds the <s>Buddhas</s> proclaim. MSA 16.68
Another [classification]: inferior, middling, and superior vigor, based on the persons suited to the three vehicles;
through the conjunction of withdrawn, exceedingly noble disposition and intelligence, vigor is held to be of small purpose and of great purpose. MSA 16.69
One who has vigor is not defeated by [attachment to] enjoyments; one who has vigor is not defeated by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: na vīryavān khedaparājito 'sti no vīryavān prāptiparājito 'sti // MSA_16.70 //
children.translated_text: one who has vigor is not defeated by weariness; one who has vigor is not defeated [in the quest for] attainment. MSA 16.70
Through mutual inclusion, through classification, through <s>dharma</s>-[characteristic], and through object,

children.text: ṣaṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ viniścayaḥ sarvathā jñeyaḥ // MSA_16.71 //
children.translated_text: the determination of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) should be known in every way. MSA 16.71
Giving corresponds to equal sharing; pleasant speech corresponds to [the teaching of] meaning;
beneficial activity corresponds to purposeful action; and [joining in] the same purpose is held [to be accomplished] through one's own exemplary conduct. MSA 16.72
A means of assistance, a gatherer, an instigator,
and a follower — these should be known as the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). MSA 16.73
By the first, there is the making of a vessel; by the second, [there is] conviction;
by the third, practice; and by the fourth, purification. MSA 16.74
The four means of attraction are held [to operate] through two kinds of gathering:
through material [means] and through <s>dharma</s>, and through <s>dharma</s> based on [its] support. MSA 16.75
The gathering is inferior, middling, and superior, and for the most part fruitless and fruitful;

children.text: abandhyaḥ sarvathā caiva jñeyo hyākārabhedataḥ // MSA_16.76 //
children.translated_text: and universally fruitful — these should be known through the distinction of modes. MSA 16.76
This method, employed through the attraction of assemblies,
is praised as the easy means for the accomplishment of all purposes for all [beings]. MSA 16.77
Those who have been gathered, those who will be gathered, and those who are being gathered now —

children.text: sarve ta evaṃ tasmācca vartma tatsatvapācane // MSA_16.78 //
children.translated_text: all of them [are encompassed] thus; and therefore this is the path for the maturation of beings. MSA 16.78
Thus, with a mind constantly unattached to enjoyments, having gone beyond to the far shore of effort in pacification,

children.text: bhavaviṣayanimittanirvikalpo bhavati sa satvagaṇasya saṃgṛhītā // MSA_16.79 //
children.translated_text: free from conceptual construction regarding the objects of existence — he becomes the gatherer of the host of beings. MSA 16.79
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixteenth chapter on the <s>pāramitās</s> is completed.
Seventeenth chapter.
Seven verses on the analysis of <s>Buddha</s>-worship.
Worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, face-to-face and in their absence, with robes and the like,
for one whose mind is deeply devoted — [this is] for the fulfillment of the twofold accumulation. MSA 17.1
For one who has [made] vows, for the sake of attaining fruitful <s>Buddha</s>-birth;
and through the non-apprehension of the three [i.e., giver, gift, and recipient] — <s>Buddha</s>-worship is perfected. MSA 17.2
Another [kind of worship is] for the maturation of immeasurable beings;
and another [arises] from material offerings and from the mind, and from faith through [their] treasure [of merit]. MSA 17.3
And another [arises] from compassion and patience, and from good conduct;
and from the realization of the object, the engagement, the awakening, and the nature of liberation. MSA 17.4
Worship [is demonstrated] with respect to basis, substance, object, transference,
cause, knowledge, field, and reliance. MSA 17.5
With respect to cause and fruit, both by oneself and by others,
and with respect to gain and honor, and practice — it [worship] is twofold. MSA 17.6

children.text: parīttā mahatī pūjā samānāmānikā ca sā /
children.translated_text: Worship is small and great, and of equal or different [measure];
it is held to be [distinguished] by application, by [spiritual] attainment, and by aspiration. MSA 17.7

children.text: buddheṣu pūjā paramā svacittāt dharmādhimuktyāśayato vibhutvāt /
children.translated_text: Supreme worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> [arises] from one's own mind, from devotion to <s>dharma</s>, from [noble] intention, from sovereign power,
through the embrace of non-conceptual means, and from being established in the single purpose of all [beings]. MSA 17.8
Service [to the teacher is demonstrated] with respect to basis, substance, object, transference,
cause, knowledge, field, and reliance. MSA 17.9
One should rely on a spiritual friend (<s>mitra</s>) who is self-controlled, tranquil, and thoroughly pacified, who excels in virtues, who has vigor, who is rich in scriptural learning,

children.text: prabuddhatatvaṃ vacasābhyupetaṃ kṛpātmakaṃ khedavivarjitaṃ ca // MSA_17.10 //
children.translated_text: who has realized reality, who is endowed with [eloquent] speech, who is compassionate in nature, and who is free from weariness. MSA 17.10

children.text: satkāralābhaiḥ paricaryayā ca seveta mitraṃ pratipattitaśca /
children.translated_text: One should serve the spiritual friend through honors and gains, through attendance, and through practice;

children.text: dharme tathājñāśaya eva dhīmān mitraṃ pragacchetsamaye nataśca // MSA_17.11 //
children.translated_text: and the wise one, with obedient intention toward the <s>dharma</s>, should approach the friend at the proper time with reverence. MSA 17.11
Free from desire for gains and honors, one should dedicate them for refuge,
and by practicing as instructed, the wise one should please the mind of that [teacher]. // MSA 17.12 //

children.text: yānatraye kauśalametya buddhyā svasyaiva yānasya yateta siddhau /
children.translated_text: Having gained skill in the three vehicles through wisdom, one should strive for the accomplishment of one's own vehicle.
Thus, knowledge from skill in the three modes of pride [is explained].

children.text: satvānameyānparipācanāya kṣetrasya śuddhasya ca sādhanāya // MSA_17.13 //
children.translated_text: For the maturation of immeasurable beings and for the purification of the [Buddha-]field. // MSA 17.13 //

children.text: dharmeṣu dāyādaguṇena yukto naivāmiṣeṇa pravesatsa mitram /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the quality of being an heir to the <s>Dharma</s>, not with material [goods], one should approach a spiritual friend;

children.text: hetoḥ phalāddharmamukhānuyānātseveta mitraṃ bahitaśca dhīmān // MSA_17.14 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should serve a spiritual friend from the cause, from the fruit, from following the doors of the <s>Dharma</s>, and from outside. // MSA 17.14 //
Through hearing and listening, through yoga of the mind, and through the pursuit of equal magical creation of mind,

children.text: gatiprayogapraṇidhānataśca kalyāṇamitraṃ hi bhajet dhīmān // MSA_17.15 //
children.translated_text: and through the course, practice, and aspiration — the wise one should attend upon a spiritual friend. // MSA 17.15 //
The supreme service of a good spiritual friend is from one's own mind, from aspiration to the <s>Dharma</s>, from intention, from powers,
from embracing the means of non-conceptualization, and from the commitment to achieving one single purpose in all things. // MSA 17.16 //
The <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) — free from adversaries, proceeding through non-conceptual knowledge,
operating on three kinds of objects — mature beings, [proceeding] in the wise ones. // MSA 17.17 //

children.text: saukhyārthini duḥkhārte sukhite kliṣṭe ca te pravartante /
children.translated_text: They operate toward those who seek happiness, who are afflicted with suffering, who are happy, who are defiled,

children.text: taddeśite ca dharme tattathatāyāṃ ca dhīrāṇām // MSA_17.18 //
children.translated_text: and also toward the <s>Dharma</s> taught by that [<s>Buddha</s>], and toward the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the wise ones. // MSA 17.18 //
Because of [compassion] having <s>tathatā</s> as its purpose, from the attainment of patience, from purification,
from twofold action, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is without object, and also from the exhaustion of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // MSA 17.19 //

children.text: te niścalāśca calāśca kṛpaṇairāsvāditā na ca jñeyāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are both unmoved and moved, tasted by the wretched but not to be known [by them];
the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established in those [brahmavihāras] that are immovable and free from attachment. // MSA 17.20 //
Those that are of an unconcentrated nature, mild and middling, belonging to a lower stage,

children.text: hīnāśayāḥ samānā hīnāste hyanyathā tvadhikāḥ // MSA_17.21 //
children.translated_text: and those of inferior aspiration that are equal — these are inferior; but otherwise they are superior. // MSA 17.21 //
When the wise one dwells with the abode of the <s>brahmavihāras</s> in the desire realm,
thereby one fulfills the accumulations and matures beings. // MSA 17.22 //
Everywhere one is inseparable from the <s>brahmavihāras</s> and free from their adversaries,

children.text: tatpratyayairapi bhṛśairna yāti vikṛtiṃ pramatto 'pi // MSA_17.23 //
children.translated_text: and even through intense conditions [of adversity], one does not undergo transformation, even when heedless. // MSA 17.23 //
Indeed, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is involved with ill-will, harmfulness, displeasure, ill-will, and sensual desire

children.text: yukto hi bodhisattvo bahuvidhamādīnavaṃ spṛśati // MSA_17.24 //
children.translated_text: incurs manifold disadvantages. // MSA 17.24 //
One harms oneself through <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), harms beings, impairs one's moral conduct,
and being deficient in gain with remorse, is also deficient in protection — thus [says] the teacher. // MSA 17.25 //
Having an offense, possessing [negative] intentions, one is reborn in unfortunate states in the next life,
and being deprived of attained and unattained [virtues], one experiences great suffering in mind. // MSA 17.26 //

children.text: ete sarve doṣā maitryādiṣu susthitasya na bhavanti /
children.translated_text: All these faults do not arise for one who is well-established in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the like;

children.text: akliṣṭaḥ saṃsāraṃ satvārthaṃ no ca saṃtyajati // MSA_17.27 //
children.translated_text: unafflicted, one does not abandon <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings. // MSA 17.27 //
Not even toward their only children, however virtuous, do all beings
have such a mental intention of <s>maitrī</s> and the like toward beings as the children of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) do. // MSA 17.28 //
Those who are ablaze, in the power of enemies, afflicted by suffering, enveloped in darkness,
who have ascended a difficult path, bound in great bondage, // MSA 17.29 //
overcome by the great poison of food, wavering, having lost the path,
beings who have set out on wrong paths, who are weak — toward them one has compassion. // MSA 17.30 //
Removing suffering, [and being] the seed of supreme awakening, bringing happiness, the cause of desired protection,

children.text: svabhāvadaṃ dharmamupāśritasya bodhirna dūre jinātmajasya // MSA_17.31 //
children.translated_text: giving the <s>Dharma</s> by nature — for the child of the <s>Jina</s> who has resorted [to this], awakening is not far. // MSA 17.31 //

children.text: vijñāya saṃsāragataṃ samagraṃ duḥkhātmakaṃ caiva nirātmakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having understood that all of <s>saṃsāra</s> is of the nature of suffering and without self,

children.text: nodvegamāyāti na cāpi doṣaiḥ prabādhyate kāruṇiko 'grabuddhiḥ // MSA_17.32 //
children.translated_text: the compassionate one of foremost wisdom neither becomes alarmed nor is afflicted by faults. // MSA 17.32 //

children.text: duḥkhātmakaṃ lokamavekṣamāṇo duḥkhāyate vetti ca tadyathāvat /
children.translated_text: Observing the world as made of suffering, one suffers and understands it as it truly is;

children.text: tasyābhyupāyaṃ parivarjane ca na khedamāyatyapi vā kṛpāluḥ // MSA_17.33 //
children.translated_text: and regarding the means of its removal — the compassionate one does not become weary. // MSA 17.33 //

children.text: kṛpā prakṛtyā pratisaṃkhyayā ca pūrvaṃ tadabhyāsavidhānayogāt /
children.translated_text: Compassion is fourfold for the compassionate ones: by nature, by deliberation,

children.text: vipakṣahīnā ca viśuddhilābhāt caturvidheyaṃ karūṇātmakānāṃ // MSA_17.34 //
children.translated_text: first by the method of repeated practice, and free from adversaries through the attainment of purification. // MSA 17.34 //

children.text: na sā kṛpā yā na samā sadā vā nādhyāśayādvā pratipattito vā /
children.translated_text: That is not compassion which is not equal, not constant, not from superior intention, not from practice,

children.text: vairāgyato nānupalambhato vā na bodhisattvo hyakṛpastathā yaḥ // MSA_17.35 //
children.translated_text: not from dispassion, nor from non-apprehension — and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is such is not without compassion. // MSA 17.35 //
Compassion, patience, reflection, aspiration, birth, and maturation of beings —
this great tree of compassion has these as root and the rest; its flowers, leaves, and fruit are the last [of these]. // MSA 17.36 //

children.text: mūlaṃ karuṇā na bhaved duṣkaracaryāsahiṣṇutā na bhavet /
children.translated_text: If compassion were not the root, there would be no endurance of difficult practices;
and the wise one who cannot bear suffering would never reflect on the welfare of beings. // MSA 17.37 //
One whose understanding is devoid of reflection would not make aspirations for pure births;
and one who does not follow auspicious births would never mature beings. // MSA 17.38 //
The sprinkling of compassion, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) — the abundant nourishment from happiness regarding their suffering —
the clear growth of branches should be known from proper mental attention. // MSA 17.39 //
From the casting and receiving of leaves — the unbroken continuity of aspirations —
from the accomplishment of twofold conditions, the flower is unfailing and the fruit [comes] from this. // MSA 17.40 //

children.text: kaḥ kurvīta na karuṇāṃ satveṣu mahākṛpāguṇakareṣu /
children.translated_text: Who would not practice compassion toward beings, who produce the virtue of great compassion?

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi saukhyamatulaṃ bhavati yadeṣāṃ kṛpājanitaṃ // MSA_17.41 //
children.translated_text: For even in suffering, incomparable happiness arises for them, born from compassion. // MSA 17.41 //

children.text: aviṣṭānāṃ kṛpayā na tiṣṭhati manaḥ śame kṛpālūnāṃ /
children.translated_text: For those not pervaded by compassion, the mind does not rest in peace; for the compassionate,

children.text: kuta eva lokasaukhye svajīvite vā bhavetsnehaḥ // MSA_17.42 //
children.translated_text: how could there be attachment to worldly happiness or to one's own life? // MSA 17.42 //

children.text: sneho na vidyate 'sau yo 'niravadyo na laukiko yaśca /
children.translated_text: That attachment which is not blameless and which is worldly does not exist [in them];
the attachment of compassion in the wise is blameless and transcends the world. // MSA 17.43 //
The world, situated in the great flood of suffering and ignorance and in great darkness —

children.text: uddhartuṃ ya upāyaḥ kathamiva na syātsa niravadyaḥ // MSA_17.44 //
children.translated_text: how could the means to rescue it not be blameless? // MSA 17.44 //
Such attachment does not exist in the world for <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
