children.text: prāgeva tadanyeṣāṃ kathamiva lokottaro na syāt // MSA_17.45 //
children.translated_text: let alone for others — how could it not be supramundane? // MSA 17.45 //
The suffering that arises from compassion for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the absence of [their own] suffering —

children.text: saṃtrāsayati tadādau spṛṣṭaṃ tvabhinandayati gāḍhaṃ // MSA_17.46 //
children.translated_text: at first it frightens, but when deeply experienced, it delights. // MSA 17.46 //

children.text: kimataḥ paramāścaryaṃ yad duḥkhaṃ saukhyamabhibhavati sarva /
children.translated_text: What greater wonder than this — that suffering overcomes all worldly happiness,

children.text: kṛpayā janitaṃ laukyaṃ yena vimukto api kṛtārthaḥ // MSA_17.47 //
children.translated_text: born from compassion, by which one is liberated and fulfilled even in the world? // MSA 17.47 //

children.text: kṛpayā sahitaṃ dānaṃ yaddānasukhaṃ karoti dhīrāṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: The happiness of giving accompanied by compassion that arises for the wise in giving —
the happiness of enjoyments in the three realms does not touch even a fraction of that happiness. // MSA 17.48 //

children.text: duḥkhamayaṃ saṃsāraṃ yatkṛpayā na tyajati satvārthaṃ /
children.translated_text: That one does not, through compassion, abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is full of suffering, for the sake of beings —
what suffering has not been endured by the compassionate for the benefit of others? // MSA 17.49 //
Compassion, giving, and enjoyments constantly increase for the compassionate one;
and from this, happiness born of affection and grace, produced by that capacity. // MSA 17.50 //

children.text: vardhe ca vardhayāmi ca dāne paripācayāmi sukhayāmi /
children.translated_text: 'I increase and I cause to increase; in giving, I mature and make happy;

children.text: ākarṣāmi nayāmi ca karuṇā sannānpravadatīva // MSA_17.51 //
children.translated_text: I attract and I lead' — compassion speaks, as it were, to those endowed [with it]. // MSA 17.51 //

children.text: duḥkhe duḥkhī kṛpayā sukhānyanādhāya kena sukhitaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Suffering in the suffering [of others] through compassion — without resorting [to other happiness], how could one be happy?
Therefore, the compassionate one makes oneself happy by resorting to the happiness of others. // MSA 17.52 //

children.text: svaṃ dānaṃ kārūṇikaḥ śāstīva sadaiva niḥsvasukhakāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: The compassionate one constantly instructs one's own giving, as it were, desiring the happiness of the destitute:

children.text: bhogaiḥ sukhaya paraṃ vā māmapyayutasaukhyam // MSA_17.53 //
children.translated_text: 'Make the other happy with enjoyments, or make me [happy] with ten thousand happinesses.' // MSA 17.53 //

children.text: saphalaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ tanme satveṣu tatsukhasukhena /
children.translated_text: 'The giving that has been given has borne fruit — that [happiness] is my happiness in the happiness of beings;

children.text: phala teṣveva nikāmaṃ yadi me kartavyatā te 'sti // MSA_17.54 //
children.translated_text: bear fruit abundantly in them, if I have any obligation [to do].' // MSA 17.54 //
For the giver who is averse to enjoyments, enjoyments approach abundantly and beautifully;

children.text: na hi tatsukhaṃ mataṃ me dāne pāraṃparo 'smi yataḥ // MSA_17.55 //
children.translated_text: 'for that happiness is not desired by me in giving, since I am beyond [self-interest] in the giving lineage.' // MSA 17.55 //
'In the complete renunciation of all, that you constantly look upon me with compassion —

children.text: nanu te tena jñeyaṃ na matphalenārthitā 'syeti // MSA_17.56 //
children.translated_text: surely by that you should know: I have no desire for my own fruit.' // MSA 17.56 //

children.text: dānābhirato na syāṃ prāptaṃ cettatphalaṃ na visṛjeyaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'I would not be delighted in giving if I were to obtain that fruit; I would not relinquish it;

children.text: kṣaṇamapi dānena vinā dānābhirato bhavati naiva // MSA_17.57 //
children.translated_text: the one delighted in giving is never even for a moment without giving.' // MSA 17.57 //

children.text: akṛtaṃ na phalasi yasmātpratikārāpekṣayā na me tulyaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Since what is not done does not bear fruit, and with regard to reciprocity — nothing equals me;

children.text: pratikāranirvyapekṣaḥ paratra phalado 'sya kāmaṃ te // MSA_17.58 //
children.translated_text: free from expectation of reciprocity, bearing fruit in the next world — let this be as you wish.' // MSA 17.58 //

children.text: niravadyaṃ śuddhapadaṃ hitāvahaṃ caiva sānurakṣaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Blameless, pure in goal, bringing benefit, and accompanied by protection,
requiring nothing in return, free from attachment — such is the compassionate giving of the children of the <s>Jina</s>. // MSA 17.59 //

children.text: sakalaṃ vipulaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ satataṃ muditaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ śuddhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Complete, vast, supreme, constant, joyful, without material [attachment], pure,
inclined toward awakening, inclined toward virtue — such is the compassionate giving of the children of the <s>Jina</s>. // MSA 17.60 //

children.text: na tathopabhogatuṣṭiṃ labhate bhogī yathā parityāgāt /
children.translated_text: The enjoyer does not obtain such satisfaction from enjoyment as the compassionate one obtains from renunciation,
with a mind nourished by threefold happiness. // MSA 17.61 //
Compassion for the wretched, compassion for the cruel, compassion for the disturbed, compassion for the heedless,
compassion for those enslaved to sense objects, and compassion for those attached to wrong views — // MSA 17.62 //
the compassion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [arises] from happiness, from suffering, from the sequence of that,
from the cause, from a spiritual friend, and from its own nature. // MSA 17.63 //
The compassion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be known as equal, from that intention,
from practice, from dispassion, from non-apprehension, and from purification. // MSA 17.64 //
The supreme cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> and the like — from one's own mind, from the <s>Dharma</s>, from aspiration,
also from intention, from powers, from non-conceptualization, and from unity. // MSA 17.65 //
Thus, one who has gained deep faith in the Blessed One, who worships with constant service to the firm great relics,
who constantly serves a spiritual friend of many virtues and benefits — the compassionate one for the world attains all accomplishments. // MSA 17.66 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the seventeenth chapter on worship, service, and the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) is complete.
The eighteenth chapter.
In the section on moral conscience (<s>lajjā</s>), sixteen verses:

children.text: lajjā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena /
children.translated_text: Moral conscience (<s>lajjā</s>) — free from adversaries, proceeding through non-conceptual knowledge,
having inferior and blameless objects — matures beings among the wise. // MSA 18.1 //
Moral conscience arises from laziness in cultivating the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
and also from applying oneself to practices favorable to the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) among the wise. // MSA 18.2 //
Moral conscience that is of an unconcentrated nature, mild and middling, belonging to a lower stage,

children.text: hīnāśayā samānā hīnā hi tadanyathā tvadhikā // MSA_18.3 //
children.translated_text: of inferior aspiration, and equal — this is inferior; but otherwise it is superior. // MSA 18.3 //
The wise one devoid of moral conscience tolerates the <s>kleśas</s> improperly;
with anger, indifference, and pride, one harms beings and [impairs] moral conduct. // MSA 18.4 //
Through remorse, one becomes distressed and loses one's honor;
one is disregarded by faithful people, the <s>saṃgha</s>, and the teacher. // MSA 18.5 //
One is censured by fellow children of the <s>Jina</s> and obtains ill-repute from the world;

children.text: dṛṣṭe dharme 'nyatra kṣaṇarahito jāyate bhūyaḥ // MSA_18.6 //
children.translated_text: in this life and the next, one is reborn without [favorable] opportunities. // MSA 18.6 //
One incurs the loss of attained and unattained [virtues] through [the absence of] pure <s>dharmas</s>;
one lives in suffering and therefore experiences unease of mind. // MSA 18.7 //

children.text: ete sarve doṣā himatsu bhavanti no jinasuteṣu /
children.translated_text: All these faults arise for those who are shameless, not for the children of the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: deveṣu ca manujeṣu ca nityaṃ saṃjāyate ca budhaḥ // MSA_18.8 //
children.translated_text: and the wise one is constantly reborn among gods and humans. // MSA 18.8 //

children.text: saṃbhārāṃśca sa bodheḥ kṣipraṃ pūrayati lajjayā dhīmān /
children.translated_text: The wise one, through moral conscience, quickly fulfills the accumulations for awakening,

children.text: satvānāṃ pācanayā na khidyate caiva jinaputraḥ // MSA_18.9 //
children.translated_text: and the child of the <s>Jina</s> does not become weary in maturing beings. // MSA 18.9 //
One is constantly reborn free from adversaries yet not free from their antidotes;
the child of the <s>Jina</s> who possesses moral conscience attains these benefits. // MSA 18.10 //
For the foolish one, stained by faults, devoid of moral conscience — even though well-clothed and well-covered —
the child of the <s>Jina</s>, even unclothed, clothed in moral conscience, is freed from the stain of faults. // MSA 18.11 //

children.text: ākāśamiva na lipto hrīyuktaḥ jinasuto bhavati dharmaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Like space, the child of the <s>Jina</s> endowed with moral conscience is not stained by [worldly] <s>dharmas</s>.
adorned with modesty (<s>hrī</s>), one shines in the company of the children of the <s>Jina</s>. // MSA 18.12 //
The modesty of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward those to be trained is like a mother's tenderness toward her children;

children.text: ārakṣā cāpi hrīḥ saṃsaratāṃ sarvadoṣebhyaḥ // MSA_18.13 //
children.translated_text: and modesty is the protection of those in <s>saṃsāra</s> from all faults. // MSA 18.13 //
Non-tolerance toward all [faults], the engagement in tolerance toward all [beings],

children.text: sarveṣu ca pravṛttirhrīvihitaṃ hrīmato liṅgam // MSA_18.14 //
children.translated_text: and engagement in all [virtuous activities] — this is the sign of one endowed with modesty, established by modesty. // MSA 18.14 //
The cultivation of modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is foremost — from one's own mind, from the <s>Dharma</s>, and from faith (<s>adhimokṣa</s>),
from [pure] intention, from pervasiveness, from non-conceptualization, and from unity. // MSA 18.15 //
The fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by its characteristic and its divisions,
and by its firmness, is distinguished from all others. // MSA 18.16 //

children.text: vīryaṃ samādhiḥ prajñā ca satvaṃ dhairyaṃ dhṛtirmatā /
children.translated_text: Vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) [comprise] strength; courage and fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) are understood [together];
the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is indeed fearless, since one proceeds from the [first] three and so forth. // MSA 18.17 //
Fear arises from sloth, from agitation, and from delusion;

children.text: kṛtyeṣu tasmādvijñeyā dhṛtisaṃjñā nije traye // MSA_18.18 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in [all] tasks, the designation of fortitude should be understood as [relating to] one's own three [antidotes]. // MSA 18.18 //

children.text: prakṛtyā praṇidhāne ca nirapekṣatva eva ca /
children.translated_text: By nature, in vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), and in indifference [to self],
in the waywardness of beings, in hearing the profound and vast, // MSA 18.19 //
in the difficulty of training the intractable, in the inconceivable body and [qualities] of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: duṣkareṣu vicitreṣu saṃsārātyāga eva ca // MSA_18.20 //
children.translated_text: in various difficult tasks, and in the very abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s>, // MSA 18.20 //
and in [the state of] non-defilement even therein — fortitude arises in the steadfast one;

children.text: asamā ca tadanyebhyaḥ so 'gre dhṛtimatāṃ yataḥ[mataḥ] // MSA_18.21 //
children.translated_text: and it is unequaled compared to others, since one is considered foremost among those possessing fortitude. // MSA 18.21 //
The heroic one is not shaken by [contact with] bad friends, suffering, the hearing of the profound —
like <s>Sumeru</s> by moths, gusts of wind, and oceans. // MSA 18.22 //
The unweariness of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is unequaled in three things:
based on insatiability for learning, great vigor, and modesty-and-fortitude regarding suffering. // MSA 18.23 //
Intense aspiration for great awakening — this is understood as the unweariness of the wise;
it is [present in the] unaccomplished, the accomplished, and the fully accomplished — across the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). // MSA 18.24 //
It is distinguished by its object, its scope, and its activity;
by its characteristic, its inexhaustibility, and the arising of its result. // MSA 18.25 //
The scriptural knowledge (<s>śāstrajñatā</s>) of the steadfast ones — the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) that is the gateway to <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: gṛhītā satvapākāya saddharmasya ca dhāraṇe // MSA_18.26 //
children.translated_text: is taken up for the ripening of beings and for upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 18.26 //
Through body and speech, and through truthful knowledge — unequaled —

children.text: lokajñatā hi dhīrāṇāṃ tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate // MSA_18.27 //
children.translated_text: the worldly knowledge (<s>lokajñatā</s>) of the steadfast ones is distinguished from all others. // MSA 18.27 //
For what purpose again? — it is said: for beings' capacity [to receive];
for what aim is that capacity? — for the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 18.28 //
From the two truths, the arising of the world occurs repeatedly;
and from the two, its setting — therefore, one who knows that is called 'knower of the world.' // MSA 18.29 //

children.text: śamāya prāptaye teṣāṃ dhīmān satyeṣu yujyate /
children.translated_text: For the pacification and attainment of those [beings], the wise one applies oneself to the truths;

children.text: satyajñānadyato dhīmān lokajño hi nirucyate // MSA_18.30 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the wise one, [being] a knower of truth, is indeed called 'knower of the world.' // MSA 18.30 //
The teaching of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (<s>ārṣa</s>) is the <s>Dharma</s>; its meaning is intentional (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>);

children.text: prāmāṇikaśca nītārtho nirjalpā prāptirasya ca // MSA_18.31 //
children.translated_text: it is authoritative (<s>prāmāṇika</s>), of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>), and its attainment is free from verbal elaboration (<s>nirjalpa</s>). // MSA 18.31 //
Of one who rejects [the teaching], of one who [interprets it] as literally stated, and of one who misrepresents [it],

children.text: sābhilāṣa[pa]sya ca prāpteḥ pratiṣedho 'tra deśitaḥ // MSA_18.32 //
children.translated_text: and of one who has attachment [to it] — the prohibition of [their mode of] attainment is taught here. // MSA 18.32 //
From faith (<s>adhimukti</s>), from investigation, from hearing properly from others,

children.text: nirjalpādapi ca jñānādapraṇāśo hi dhīmatāṃ // MSA_18.33 //
children.translated_text: and from knowledge that is free from verbal elaboration — there is non-destruction for the wise. // MSA 18.33 //
The four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are unequaled;

children.text: paryāye lakṣaṇe vākye jñāne jñānācca tā matāḥ // MSA_18.34 //
children.translated_text: they pertain to the synonym (<s>paryāya</s>), the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), speech (<s>vākya</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) — and they arise from knowledge. // MSA 18.34 //

children.text: deśanāyāṃ prayuktasya yasya yena ca deśanā /
children.translated_text: Of one engaged in teaching — who teaches, and by what;
teaching is through speech regarding both <s>Dharma</s> and meaning, and indeed through knowledge. // MSA 18.35 //
From the topic (<s>uddeśa</s>) and exposition (<s>nirdeśa</s>) of the <s>Dharma</s>, from leading [beings] to both [Dharma and meaning] in every way,
and from the full comprehension of objections — the fourfold analytical knowledge. // MSA 18.36 //
Having personally attained equanimity (<s>samatā</s>), the communication to others thereafter,
for the destruction of all doubts — this is called analytical knowledge. // MSA 18.37 //
The accumulation (<s>saṃbhāra</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, consisting of merit and knowledge, is unequaled;
one is for prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the other for undefiled transmigration. // MSA 18.38 //

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ ca puṇyasya prajñā jñānasya saṃbhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Giving (<s>dāna</s>) and morality (<s>śīla</s>) are the accumulation of merit; wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the accumulation of knowledge;
the [remaining] three are for both; and all five are [also] the accumulation of knowledge. // MSA 18.39 //

children.text: saṃtatyā bhāvanāmetya bhūyo bhūyaḥ śubhasya hi /
children.translated_text: The nourishment that is the cultivation of the wholesome, repeatedly, in continuity —

children.text: āhāro yaḥ sa saṃbhāro vī[dhī]re sarvārthasādhakaḥ // MSA_18.40 //
children.translated_text: that is the accumulation for the steadfast, accomplishing all purposes. // MSA 18.40 //
The accumulation increases for the steadfast ones — for entering [the path], for [attaining] the signless,
for the effortless, for consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), and for the final [stage]. // MSA 18.41 //
The cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) [is done] through fourteen aspects;
because of its unequaledness, it is distinguished from all others for the wise. // MSA 18.42 //
From the support, from the antidote, from the entry, and likewise
from the object, mental engagement, and attainment — it is distinguished. // MSA 18.43 //
From conformity, from continuous practice, from full understanding, from another's arising,
by degree, by supremacy, and from the accomplishment of cultivation. // MSA 18.44 //
The right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) of the steadfast are unequaled among all embodied beings;
they are cultivated as the antidote to the faults of the foundations of mindfulness. // MSA 18.45 //
In the enjoyment of <s>saṃsāra</s>, in the abandonment of the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>),

children.text: manaskārasya ca tyāge praveśe caiva bhūmiṣu // MSA_18.46 //
children.translated_text: in the abandonment of mental engagement, and in the very entry into the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>); // MSA 18.46 //
in the signless abiding, in the attainment of the prediction [of <s>Buddhahood</s>],

children.text: satvānāṃ paripāke ca abhiṣeke ca dhīmatāṃ // MSA_18.47 //
children.translated_text: in the ripening of beings, and in the consecration of the wise — // MSA 18.47 //

children.text: kṣetrasya ca viśuddhyarthaṃ niṣṭhāgamana eva ca /
children.translated_text: and for the purpose of the purification of the [Buddha-]field, and in the very attainment of the final [stage] —
it is cultivated by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as antidote to the adversary. // MSA 18.48 //
Relying on aspiration, the cultivation of yoga is sign-based (<s>sanimittikā</s>);
in all the right exertions, this is declared as the antidote. // MSA 18.49 //
The four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) of the steadfast have supreme characteristics;

children.text: sarvārthasiddhau jāyante ātmanaśca parasya ca // MSA_18.50 //
children.translated_text: they arise for the accomplishment of all purposes, both for oneself and others. // MSA 18.50 //
From the support, the division, the means, and the accomplishment —
the arrangement of the bases of supernatural power is accepted in every way for the wise. // MSA 18.51 //
Relying on the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), the division is fourfold;
and the means and accomplishment are prescribed as sixfold. // MSA 18.52 //
The first is of the nature of resolution; the second is of the nature of benefiting [others];
the third is of the nature of binding; the fourth is of the nature of antidote. // MSA 18.53 //
The accomplishment of seeing, of admonition, of abiding-and-sport,
of aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), of mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>), and of attainment of the <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 18.54 //
Awakening, conduct, the best of learning (<s>śruta</s>), tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>), and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) —
the foundation of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the like should be known from the perspective of their purpose in accomplishment. // MSA 18.55 //
Those [qualities] such as faith, which are engaged in entry into the stages and in defilement —
through the weakness of the adversary, those very [qualities] are designated as powers (<s>balas</s>). // MSA 18.56 //
For one who has entered the stages, the arrangement of the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) is prescribed —
from the understanding of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and all beings. // MSA 18.57 //
Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) operates everywhere, for the conquest of what is unconquered in the knowable;
and its investigation (<s>vicaya</s>) is for the destruction of all conceptual signs. // MSA 18.58 //
Just as a jewel-elephant [destroys] adversaries,
vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) operates for the swift and complete awakening;

children.text: dharmālokavivṛddhyā ca prītyā āpūryate dhruvam // MSA_18.59 //
children.translated_text: and through the increase of the light of <s>Dharma</s>, one is certainly filled with joy (<s>prīti</s>). // MSA 18.59 //
From the release of all obscurations, through tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), one attains happiness;
and the fulfillment of contemplated purposes arises from concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). // MSA 18.60 //
Through equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), one abides everywhere as one wishes;
having attained the non-conceptual after [the conceptual], through [non-conceptual] abiding, one is always the supreme. // MSA 18.61 //
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with such qualities operates like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch),
constantly surrounded by the limbs of awakening, which are comparable to the seven jewels. // MSA 18.62 //
The first is the limb of support; the second is the limb of [intrinsic] nature; the third is the limb of deliverance;
the fourth is the limb of benefit; and the limb of non-affliction is threefold in nature. // MSA 18.63 //
The subsequent [practice] arises in accordance with awakening, and above that;
the arrangement in accordance with awakening, and the entry into [that] arrangement. // MSA 18.64 //
The purification of the three activities, and the cultivation of the antidote
to the obscuration of the knowable, and the path — and of the distinctive quality. // MSA 18.65 //
From the mind's abiding in the mind, and from the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>,
relying on right abiding — tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>). // MSA 18.66 //
All-pervading, and [operative] in both the learning and the beyond-learning [stages];

children.text: prativedhe ca niryāṇe animitte hyasaṃskṛte // MSA_18.67 //
children.translated_text: in penetration and deliverance, in the signless, and in the unconditioned. // MSA 18.67 //
In purification and in [complete] purity — tranquility and insight;

children.text: sarvabhūmigatā dhīre sa yogaḥ sarvasādhakaḥ // MSA_18.68 //
children.translated_text: pervading all stages for the steadfast — that yoga accomplishes everything. // MSA 18.68 //
In fulfilling the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, in ripening sentient beings,

children.text: kṣipraprāptau kriyāśuddhau vartmācchede ca kauśalaṃ // MSA_18.69 //
children.translated_text: in swift attainment, in purity of action, and in cutting off the path [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] — skillfulness. // MSA 18.69 //
The skillfulness of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in means (<s>upāya</s>) is unequaled across all stages;
relying on that skillfulness, they accomplish all purposes. // MSA 18.70 //
Through maturation, through practice of learning, through <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and through <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: parīttā mahatī sā ca mahatī trividhā punaḥ // MSA_18.71 //
children.translated_text: it is small and great; and the great is again threefold. // MSA 18.71 //
For the wise who have not entered and who have entered [the stages] — gentle and middling;
for those on the impure stages — great; and for those on the pure stages [— the greatest]. // MSA 18.72 //
Relying on that <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), <s>Bodhisattvas</s> again and again

children.text: prakāśayanti saddharmaṃ nityaṃ saṃdhārayanti ca // MSA_18.73 //
children.translated_text: illuminate the true <s>Dharma</s> and constantly uphold it. // MSA 18.73 //

children.text: cetanā chandasahitā jñānena preritā ca tat /
children.translated_text: Intention accompanied by aspiration, and impelled by knowledge — that
is the aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) of the steadfast, unequaled across all stages. // MSA 18.74 //

children.text: hetubhūtaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ cittātsadyaḥ phalaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: It should be known as being a cause, and as producing an immediate result from the mind;
for the accomplishment of purposes in the future, through the fulfillment from mind alone. // MSA 18.75 //
Variegated, great, and pure — in the progressively higher stages,
until awakening — accomplishing the purposes of self and others for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // MSA 18.76 //
Twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) is to be known, and the basis of self-grasping (<s>ātmagrāha</s>);
and its pacification is always in the domain of the threefold <s>samādhi</s>. // MSA 18.77 //
The threefold <s>samādhi</s> should be known from the [cessation of] grasped and grasper;
the non-conceptual [samādhi] too is always turned away [from defilements] and endowed with delight. // MSA 18.78 //
For full understanding, for abandonment, and again for direct realization —
the threefold purpose of the <s>samādhis</s> of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the like is proclaimed. // MSA 18.79 //
Through <s>samādhi</s> as a prerequisite, the fourfold summary of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmoddāna</s>)
has been taught to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> out of the desire to benefit sentient beings. // MSA 18.80 //
The meaning of non-existence, the meaning of non-conceptualization, the meaning of mere imagination,
and the meaning of the pacification of conceptualization — that is the fourfold [summary] for the wise. // MSA 18.81 //
From the impossibility [of arising], from cause, from origination, from contradiction, from non-establishment by itself,
from non-existence, from the certainty of characteristics, from continuity, and from cessation; // MSA 18.82 //
from transformation and apprehension, from being its cause and its result,
from being taken up, from sovereignty, and from the continuity of pure beings; // MSA 18.83 //
from the first and the lowest, from accumulation, and from being a basis,
from modification and maturation, and likewise from being inferior and superior; // MSA 18.84 //
from being luminous and non-luminous, from going to another place,
from having a seed and being seedless, and from the reflection — [these are] the points. // MSA 18.85 //
In the fourteen kinds of arising, from the distinction of what possesses a cause,
from [the impossibility of] accumulation, from purpose, from impossibility, and from being a basis — the impossibility [is shown]; // MSA 18.86 //
from the impossibility of what is established [ceasing] at the end, from the unchangeability of the first,
and likewise in [the states of] inferior and superior, and in the luminous and non-luminous. // MSA 18.87 //
Because of the absence of going, the impossibility of remaining, and the impossibility of being the last [moment],
and because of the continuity of consciousness — all conditioned things are momentary. // MSA 18.88 //
The momentariness of beings is established in six kinds of objects:

children.text: śoṣavṛddheḥ prakṛtyā ca calatvād vṛddhihānitaḥ // MSA_18.89 //
children.translated_text: from drying and growth, from nature, from instability, and from increase and decline. // MSA 18.89 //
And from the arising of that, and from the four transformations of earth,
and from the equality of color, smell, taste, and touch — likewise that [is established]. // MSA 18.90 //
From being dependent on fuel for its functioning, from the observation of gradation,
from the continuity of mind, and from inquiry — the external is also momentary. // MSA 18.91 //

children.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu /
children.translated_text: The person (<s>pudgala</s>) is to be spoken of as existing by designation, not as a substance.
Because of non-apprehension, because of inversion, because of affliction, and because of being a cause of affliction. // MSA 18.92 //
He is to be spoken of as neither identical with nor different [from the aggregates] — therefore, from the twofold fault;
and because of the unwanted consequence of being identical with the aggregates, and the unwanted consequence of being a substance. // MSA 18.93 //
If he existed as a substance yet were inexpressible — the purpose of such a statement must be stated.
Being inexpressible as either identical or different is not justified and is purposeless. // MSA 18.94 //
From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and from scripture too, it is not justified.
For the inexpressibility of fuel and fire [as identical or different] is [established] through the perception of both. // MSA 18.95 //

children.text: dvaye sati ca vijñānasaṃbhavātpratyayo na saḥ /
children.translated_text: And since, when both [subject and object] exist, consciousness arises dependent on them — he is not a condition;

children.text: nairarthakyādato draṣṭā yāvanmoktā na yujyate // MSA_18.96 //
children.translated_text: from being purposeless — therefore, a seer up to a liberator is not justified. // MSA 18.96 //
And if there were ownership, the impermanent and undesirable would not arise.

children.text: tatkarmalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyaṃ saṃbodho bādhyate tridhā // MSA_18.97 //
children.translated_text: That which has the characteristic of <s>karma</s> is to be proved; awakening is refuted in three ways. // MSA 18.97 //
And in seeing and the like, that effort — neither self-arisen nor from the three;
and the condition-nature of that effort, and the effortlessness of seeing and the like. // MSA 18.98 //
Because of non-agenthood, because of impermanence, and because of functioning sometimes and perpetually —

children.text: darśanādiṣu yatnasya svayaṃbhūtvaṃ na yujyate // MSA_18.99 //
children.translated_text: the self-arisen nature of effort in seeing and the like is not justified. // MSA 18.99 //
Likewise, because of the prior non-existence of what is established and what has perished, and because of impermanence,
and because of the absence of a third alternative — the condition-nature is not justified. // MSA 18.100 //
All phenomena are without self; in ultimate truth, [there is] emptiness.

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaśca deśito yata eva ca // MSA_18.101 //
children.translated_text: And the fault in apprehending a self has been taught — for that very reason. // MSA 18.101 //
In affliction and purification, distinguished by states and breaks,
the difference of functioning and continuum is indicated by [the concept of] 'person.' // MSA 18.102 //
The view of self is not to be newly produced [since it is]; the habitual tendency is beginningless.

children.text: ayatnamokṣaḥ sarveṣāṃ na mokṣaḥ pudgalo 'sti vā // MSA_18.103 //
children.translated_text: Effortless liberation for all [would follow]; or [there would be] no liberation — [if] the person exists. // MSA 18.103 //

children.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu /
children.translated_text: The person is to be spoken of as existing by designation, not as a substance.
He is to be spoken of as neither identical with nor different [from the aggregates] — therefore.
And because of the unwanted consequence of being identical with the aggregates, and the unwanted consequence of being a substance.
If he existed as a substance yet were inexpressible — the purpose of such a statement must be stated.
Being inexpressible as either identical or different is not justified and is purposeless.
From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and from scripture too, it is not justified.
For the inexpressibility of fuel and fire [as identical or different] is [established] through the perception of both.
Since, dependent on both, consciousness arises — he is not a condition.
And if there were ownership, the impermanent and undesirable would not arise. //
And the condition-nature of that effort, and the effortlessness of seeing and the like.
Because of non-agenthood, because of impermanence, and because of functioning once and perpetually —
the self-arisen nature of effort in seeing and the like is not justified. //
Likewise, because of the prior non-existence of what is established and what has perished, and because of impermanence,
and because of the absence of a third alternative — the condition-nature is not justified. //
All phenomena are without self; in ultimate truth, [there is] emptiness.

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaśca deśito yata eva ca //
children.translated_text: And the fault in apprehending a self has been taught — for that very reason. //
In affliction and purification, distinguished by states and breaks,
the difference of functioning and continuum is indicated by [the concept of] 'person.' //
The view of self is not to be newly produced, since it has already arisen. Nor is it for the purpose of habituating [the view of self], since the habitual tendency of the self-view
is beginningless.

children.text:
yadi cātmadarśanena mokṣa ityasau deśyeta /
evaṃ sati syāt
children.translated_text: And if it were taught that liberation comes through the view of self, then in that case there would be —
effortless liberation for all.
Thus, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are always endowed with these qualities;

children.text: ātmārthaṃ ca na riñcanti parārthaṃ sādhayanti ca // MSA_18.104 //
children.translated_text: they do not abandon their own welfare and they accomplish the welfare of others. // MSA 18.104 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eighteenth chapter on the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) is completed.
Nineteenth chapter:
Three verses in the section on the wonderful:
The abandonment of one's own body, and of possessions, in the conventional [sense],

children.text: durbaleṣu kṣamā kāye jīvite nirapekṣiṇaḥ // MSA_19.1 //
children.translated_text: patience toward the weak, without regard for body or life. // MSA 19.1 //

children.text: vīryārambho hyanāsvādo dhāneṣu sukha eva ca /
children.translated_text: The undertaking of effort without [seeking] pleasure, and happiness in meditation,

children.text: niṣkalpanā na prajñāyāmāścaryaṃ dhīmatāṃ ga[ma]taṃ // MSA_19.2 //
children.translated_text: and non-conceptualization in wisdom — these are considered the wonders of the wise. // MSA 19.2 //
Birth in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the attainment of prophecy,
and the attainment of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), and awakening — these are considered wonderful. // MSA 19.3 //
Dispassion and compassion and supreme meditation,

children.text: tathaiva samacittatvaṃ nāścaryaṃ tāsu yuktatā // MSA_19.4 //
children.translated_text: and likewise equanimity of mind — the engagement in these is not [merely] wonderful. // MSA 19.4 //
Not toward oneself, one's wife, one's sons, friends, or relatives

children.text: satvānāṃ pragataḥ sneho yathā satveṣu dhīmatāṃ // MSA_19.5 //
children.translated_text: do beings have such love as the wise have toward beings. // MSA 19.5 //
Impartiality toward supplicants, unbroken morality always,
patience everywhere for the sake of beings, and great undertaking of effort. // MSA 19.6 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ ca kuśalaṃ nityaṃ prajñā caivāvikalpikā /
children.translated_text: Wholesome meditation constantly, and non-conceptual wisdom —
the equanimity of mind of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in these very [practices] should be known. // MSA 19.7 //

children.text: sthāpanā bhājanatve ca śīleṣveva ca ropaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Establishing [beings] in receptivity, and planting in moral precepts,
forbearance of harm, and engagement in purposeful activity. // MSA 19.8 //
Attracting [beings] to this teaching, cutting through doubt,
and benefiting beings — this is desired of the wise. // MSA 19.9 //
Those who constantly sustain beings with equanimous intention,
generate [them] in the noble stage, and develop [them] with wholesome [qualities], // MSA 19.10 //
protect them from wrongdoing, and instruct them in what has been heard —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like mothers to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.11 //
Because of always implanting faith in all beings,
and because of engaging [them] in the training of higher morality and the like, and in liberation, // MSA 19.12 //
and because of requesting the <s>Buddhas</s>, and because of removing their obscurations —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like fathers to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.13 //

children.text: anarhadeśanāṃ ye ca satvānāṃ gūhayanti hi /
children.translated_text: Those who conceal from beings teachings that are not appropriate [for them],

children.text: śikṣāvipattiṃ nindanti śaṃsantyeva ca saṃpadam // MSA_19.14 //
children.translated_text: who censure failure in training and praise its success, // MSA 19.14 //
who give instruction and who reveal <s>Māra</s> —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like kinsmen to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.15 //
Regarding affliction and purification, they themselves are of unwearied understanding;

children.text: yacchanti laukikīṃ kṛtsnāṃ saṃpadaṃ cātilaukikīm // MSA_19.16 //
children.translated_text: they bestow the entire worldly prosperity and the supramundane as well. // MSA 19.16 //

children.text: sukhe hite cābhinnā[akheditvādabhinnā] ye sadā sukhahitaiṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are unbroken [in their pursuit of] happiness and benefit, always seeking happiness and benefit —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like friends to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.17 //
Those who always make effort in the ripening of beings,
who are speakers of the right way of going forth, who are patient with wrong practices, // MSA 19.18 //
who are bestowers of the twofold prosperity and skilled in its means —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like servants to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.19 //
Those who are considered to have attained the acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena,
who instruct in all [vehicles], who engage [beings] in accomplished practices, // MSA 19.20 //
who are kindly-faced in return, and who have no expectation of retribution —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like teachers to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.21 //
Those who, engaged in the activity for beings, fulfill the accumulations,
who quickly liberate those who have accumulated, and who cause the abandonment of the adversary, // MSA 19.22 //
and who join [beings] with diverse worldly and supramundane attainments —
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like preceptors (<s>upādhyāya</s>) to beings, through five activities. // MSA 19.23 //

children.text: asaktyā caiva bhogeṣu śīlasya ca na khaṇḍanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through non-attachment to enjoyments, through non-violation of morality,
through the application of gratitude, and through engagement in practice — // MSA 19.24 //
embodied beings who abide in the six <s>Pāramitās</s>
become, in turn, benefactors of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // MSA 19.25 //

children.text: vṛddhiṃ hāniṃ ca kāṅkṣanti satvānāṃ ca prapācanaṃ /
children.translated_text: They aspire for the growth and the ripening of beings,

children.text: viśeṣagamanaṃ bhūmau bodhiṃ cānuttarāṃ sadā // MSA_19.26 //
children.translated_text: for the attainment of distinction on the stages, and always for the unsurpassed awakening. // MSA 19.26 //
In removing fear, in generating [the wholesome], in cutting through doubt,
and in instructing in practice — the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are always unfailing. // MSA 19.27 //
Giving without expectation of return, without desire for further existence;

children.text: śīlaṃ kṣāntiśca sarvatra vīryaṃ sarvaśubhodaye // MSA_19.28 //
children.translated_text: morality and patience everywhere; effort in the arising of all that is wholesome; // MSA 19.28 //
meditation without [attachment to] the formless, and wisdom conjoined with skillful means —
this is the right practice of the steadfast in the six <s>Pāramitās</s>. // MSA 19.29 //
Attachment to enjoyments, breach [of morality], pride, indulgence in pleasure,
savoring, and conceptualization — these are the causes of decline for the steadfast. // MSA 19.30 //
For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the antidotes to these,
the qualities leading to distinction should be known — from the opposite of these. // MSA 19.31 //
Deceiving, displaying a pleasant face [for gain],

children.text: lobhatvena tatha vṛttiḥ śāntavākkāyatā tathā // MSA_19.32 //
children.translated_text: likewise, conduct motivated by greed, and likewise, calm in speech and body [only], // MSA 19.32 //
and excellence of fine speech devoid of practice —
these are taught as leading to inauthenticity for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;
their opposite, when practiced, is taught as leading to authenticity. // MSA 19.33 //
Through the aids of giving and the like, they discipline beings;

children.text: ṣaṭprakāraṃ vipakṣaṃ hi dhīmantaḥ sarvabhūmiṣu // MSA_19.34 //
children.translated_text: the wise, on all stages, [overcome] the sixfold adversary. // MSA 19.34 //
The prophecy of the wise is twofold, by the distinction of time and person;
and in the prophecy of awakening as well, what is great and other have been stated. // MSA 19.35 //
From the attainment of the acceptance of non-arising, from the absence of the practice of pride,
and because of arriving at oneness [with all] — by all the <s>Buddhas</s> and children of the <s>Jinas</s>. // MSA 19.36 //

children.text: kṣetreṇaṃ nāmnā kālena kalpanāmnā ca tatpunaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the [Buddha]-field, name, time, name of the <s>kalpa</s>,
retinue, succession, and the True <s>Dharma</s> — that is desired. // MSA 19.37 //
In attaining prosperity, in the certainty of arising, in the absence of weariness for the wise,
and in the continuity of meditation, and in the non-falling from <s>samādhi</s>,
and in the accomplishment of duties without effort, and in the attainment of acceptance in every way. // MSA 19.38 //
Worship, undertaking the training, compassion, cultivation of the wholesome,
diligence, [dwelling] in the forest, and insatiability for the meaning of what is heard —
these are the obligatory duties of the steadfast on all stages. // MSA 19.39 //
Knowledge of the dangers in sensual desires, examination of one's own lapses,

children.text: duḥkhādhivāsanā caiva kuśalasya ca bhāvanā // MSA_19.40 //
children.translated_text: endurance of suffering, and cultivation of the wholesome. // MSA 19.40 //
Non-savoring of happiness, and non-conceptualization of signs —
these are the constant duties of the wise on all stages. // MSA 19.41 //
The gift of <s>Dharma</s>, purity of morality, the acceptance of non-arising,
great effort in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the final abiding with compassion,

children.text: prajñā pāramitānāṃ ca pradhānaṃ dhīmatāṃ matam // MSA_19.42 //
children.translated_text: and the wisdom of the <s>Pāramitās</s> — these are considered the chief [virtues] of the wise. // MSA 19.42 //
Establishment in the fields of knowledge, according to the distinction of forms such as sūtras and the like —
this should be known as the establishment in <s>Dharma</s> of the wise on all stages. // MSA 19.43 //
Again, the establishment of beings [is described] in seven ways based on <s>tathatā</s>,

children.text: caturdhā ca tridhā caiva yuktiyānavyavasthitiḥ // MSA_19.44 //
children.translated_text: and in four ways and in three ways — the establishment of reasoning and vehicle. // MSA 19.44 //
Proper mental attention, right view endowed with result,
investigation through means of knowledge, and the inconceivable — the fourfold reasoning should be known. // MSA 19.45 //
From intention, from teaching, from practice, from accumulation,
and from the distinction of attainment — the vehicle is considered threefold. // MSA 19.46 //
The adventitious nature, the investigation — of name and thing, mutually —
the investigation here of the mere-that-ness of twofold designation. MSA 19.47
And through the non-apprehension of everything, fourfold true knowledge
arises for the courageous ones on all stages, for the accomplishment of all purposes. MSA 19.48
For the basis, engagement, and seed are indeed the cause of bondage;
and <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors), together with their basis, are bound here together with their seeds. MSA 19.49

children.text: purataḥ sthāpitaṃ yacca nimittaṃ yatsthitaṃ svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: That which is placed before [as object] and the sign that stands by itself —
the wise one, illuminating all of this, attains supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). MSA 19.50
Knowledge that takes <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as its object, free from the grasping of duality,
is held by the wise to be directly perceived as the body of afflictive tendencies (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), upon its destruction. MSA 19.51
Knowledge that takes <s>tathatā</s> as its object, cultivated without diverse appearances,
is said to be directly perceived with respect to existent and non-existent objects, and is the master of conceptual constructions. MSA 19.52
Concealing reality, unreality appears everywhere to the childish;

children.text: tattvaṃ tu bodhisatvānāṃ sarvataḥ khyātyapāsya tat // MSA_19.53 //
children.translated_text: but for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, reality appears everywhere, having cast that [unreality] aside. MSA 19.53
The non-appearance and appearance should be known respectively of unreal objects and real objects;
the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) is liberation — it [results in] freedom of movement. MSA 19.54
Objects of the same kind mutually appear as great everywhere;
since [such appearance] creates obstacles, having fully understood it, one should abandon it. MSA 19.55

children.text: paripācyaṃ viśodhyaṃ ca prāpyaṃ yogyaṃ ca pācane /
children.translated_text: What is to be matured, what is to be purified, what is to be attained, and what is fit for maturing,
and the object of correct teaching — these are immeasurable for the wise. MSA 19.56
And the arising of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s [mind], the non-arising patience (<s>anutpattikṣānti</s>),

children.text: cakṣuśca nirmalaṃ hīnamāśravakṣaya eva ca // MSA_19.57 //
children.translated_text: and the pure eye, and the inferior, and the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements). MSA 19.57
The long duration of the true <s>dharma</s>, accomplishment in interpretation, severance, and enjoyment —

children.text: deśanāyāḥ phalaṃ jñeyaṃ tatprayuktasya dhīmataḥ // MSA_19.58 //
children.translated_text: these should be known as the fruit of teaching for the wise one who is engaged in it. MSA 19.58
The greatness of the object and of practice in both [aspects],

children.text: jñānasya vīryārambhasya upāye kauśalasya ca // MSA_19.59 //
children.translated_text: and of knowledge, the undertaking of vigor, and skill in means; MSA 19.59
and the greatness of attainment and the greatness of <s>Buddha</s>-activity —
it is because of this conjunction of greatness that it is called <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). MSA 19.60
The spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), devotion to <s>dharma</s>, and likewise the generation of the [awakening] mind,
the practice of giving and the like, and the entry into the correct [path]; MSA 19.61
the maturation of beings and the purification of the [Buddha-]field,

children.text: apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ bodhiḥ śreṣṭhā ca darśanāt[darśanā] // MSA_19.62 //
children.translated_text: non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), and the supreme <s>bodhi</s> — through seeing [these]. MSA 19.62
One [type] based on aspiration (<s>adhimokṣika</s>) and another based on pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayika</s>);
and [those at the stage of] signs and signlessness, and the noble ones [at the stage] of the unconditioned —

children.text: bodhisatvā hi vijñeyāḥ pañcaite sarvabhūmiṣu // MSA_19.63 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be known as these five [types] on all stages. MSA 19.63
Unattached to sense-pleasures, with threefold pure conduct, overcoming the ground of anger, devoted to virtues,
steadfast in <s>dharma</s>, with a view profound as to reality, and aspiring to awakening — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.64
Wishing to help, seeing non-harm, and forbearing in the face of others' offenses,

children.text: dhīro 'pramattaśca bahuśrutaśca parārthayuktaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.65 //
children.translated_text: courageous, vigilant, learned, and devoted to others' welfare — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.65
Knowing the faults in one's own possessions, unattached to enjoyments, without concealed enmity,

children.text: yogī nimitte kuśalo 'kudṛṣṭiradhyātmasaṃsthaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.66 //
children.translated_text: a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, skilled in signs, free from wrong views, established within — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.66
Endowed with compassion, possessed of the quality of modesty, unattached to personal comforts through forbearance of suffering,

children.text: smṛtipradhānaḥ susamāhitātmā yānāvikāryaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.67 //
children.translated_text: with mindfulness as the chief [quality], well-concentrated in mind, unwavering from the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.67

children.text: duḥkhāpaho duḥkhakaro na caiva duḥkhādhivāso na ca duḥkhabhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: A remover of suffering, yet not a creator of suffering; forbearing of suffering, yet not afraid of suffering;

children.text: duḥkhādvimukto na ca duḥkhakalpo duḥkhābhyupetaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.68 //
children.translated_text: freed from suffering, yet not [merely] imagining [the absence of] suffering; having taken on suffering — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.68
Delighting in <s>dharma</s>, not delighting in <s>adharma</s> by nature; disgusted with [false] <s>dharma</s>, devoted to [true] <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: dharme vaśī dharmanirandhakāro dharmapradhānaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.69 //
children.translated_text: master of <s>dharma</s>, without darkness regarding <s>dharma</s>, with <s>dharma</s> as the chief [concern] — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.69
Vigilant regarding enjoyments, vigilant regarding discipline, vigilant regarding protection, vigilant regarding virtue,

children.text: sukhāpramatto dharamāpramatto yānāpramatto khalu bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.70 //
children.translated_text: vigilant regarding happiness, vigilant regarding <s>dharma</s>, vigilant regarding the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.70
Modest about [others'] contempt, modest about [one's own] minor faults, modest about [expressions of] resentment, modest about decline,
modest about [showing] vastness, modest about [narrow] views, modest about other vehicles — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.71
Both here and hereafter, through equanimity, through the application of [mental] formations, through attainments of sovereign power,

children.text: śamopa[samaupa]deśena mahāphalena anugrahe vartati bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.72 //
children.translated_text: and through the great fruit of teaching pacification — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engages in benefiting [beings]. MSA 19.72
<s>Bodhisattva</s>, great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), wise one (<s>dhīmān</s>), of supreme splendor,
son of the <s>Jinas</s>, support of the <s>Jinas</s>, conqueror, and sprout of the <s>Jinas</s>; MSA 19.73
heroic, supremely wonderful, caravan-leader, of great fame,
compassionate, of great merit, sovereign, and righteous. MSA 19.74
Through awakenings of true nature, awakenings of great purpose, awakenings of all purposes, and awakenings that are perpetual,

children.text: upāyabodhaiśca viśeṣaṇena tenocyate hetuna bodhisatvaḥ // MSA_19.75 //
children.translated_text: and through awakenings of skillful means as distinguishing [factor] — for this reason he is called <s>Bodhisattva</s> (awakening-being). MSA 19.75
Through awakening to the self, through awakening to subtle views, and through awakening to varied representations (<s>vijñapti</s>),
and through awakening to the unreal conceptualization of everything — for this reason he is called <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.76
Through awakening to non-awakening, through awakening to subsequent awakening, through awakening to non-existence, through subsequent awakening to origination,
and through counter-awakening to non-awakening — for this reason he is called <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.77
Through awakening to non-purpose, through awakening to supreme purpose, through awakening to all purposes, through awakening to complete purpose,
and through awakening to the basis of what is to be awakened — for this reason he is called <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.78
Through awakening to the perfected, through awakening to the [proper] stage, and through subsequent awakening to the embryo [of the <s>Tathāgata</s>], through seeing the sequence,

children.text: bodhādbhṛśaṃ saṃśayahānibodhāt tenocyate hetuna bodhisattvaḥ // MSA_19.79 //
children.translated_text: and through intense awakening to the elimination of doubt — for this reason he is called <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 19.79
A gainer yet a non-gainer, established in wisdom, one who awakens and causes others to awaken, and a confessor,
of speech free from verbal elaboration, free from pride and conceit, and of understanding both unripened and ripened — such is the wise one. MSA 19.80
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the chapter on qualities [nineteenth] is completed.
Twentieth and twenty-first chapters.
Two verses on the analysis of signs (<s>liṅga</s>).
Compassion, pleasant speech, courage, open-handedness,
and release of profound [textual] connections — these are the signs of the wise. MSA 20.1
In [the sphere of] embracing, in conviction and attainment, in indefatigability, in the gathering of both [merit and knowledge],
and from intention and from application — the fivefold sign should be known. MSA 20.2
The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, always being [like] universal monarchs (<s>cakravartins</s>),

children.text: prakurvanti hi satvārthaṃ gṛhiṇaḥ sarvajanmasu // MSA_20.3 //
children.translated_text: perform the welfare of beings as householders in all births. MSA 20.3
Renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>) obtained through acceptance, that which is superior through conformity with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nidarśikā ca pravrajayā dhīmatāṃ sarvabhūmiṣu // MSA_20.4 //
children.translated_text: and renunciation that is exemplary — [these belong to] the wise on all stages. MSA 20.4
The side of the renunciant is endowed with immeasurable virtues;
therefore the ascetic is superior to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is a householder. MSA 20.5
The desire for desired fruits in the next [life], and virtuous conduct in this very [life],
and the desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s> — these are held as the intention toward beings among the courageous;
impure, pure, and very pure — on all stages. MSA 20.6
Through aspiration, from an even mind, through sovereignty — [this is] the embrace
and the attraction of assemblies — of the wise on all stages. MSA 20.7
And another [kind of] birth for the wise is held [to arise] through the sovereignty of action,
through aspiration, through <s>samādhi</s>, and through [the attainment of] sovereign powers. MSA 20.8
Through characteristic, person, the accomplishment of the training-aggregates, through sign,

children.text: nirukteḥ prāptitaścaiva vihāro bhūmireva ca // MSA_20.9 //
children.translated_text: through etymology, and through attainment — the abode is indeed the stage (<s>bhūmi</s>). MSA 20.9
Emptiness of the supreme self; stability in the non-destruction of <s>karma</s>;

children.text: vihṛtya sasukhairdhyānairjanma kāme tataḥ param // MSA_20.10 //
children.translated_text: having dwelt with blissful <s>dhyānas</s>, birth in the desire-realm — and then beyond. MSA 20.10
And then, the dedication of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: vinā ca cittasaṃkleśaṃ satvānāṃ paripācanā // MSA_20.11 //
children.translated_text: and the maturation of beings without the defilement of the mind. MSA 20.11
And in [the process of] birth, having accumulated, the guarding against defilement;
attached to the single path, the path that is exclusively signless. MSA 20.12
Even in signlessness, non-engagement; and the purification of the [Buddha-]field;

children.text: satvapākasya niṣpattirjāyate ca tataḥ param // MSA_20.13 //
children.translated_text: and the accomplishment of the maturation of beings arises thereafter. MSA 20.13
And the purity of <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentive powers) and of awakening itself —
from this arrangement, the characteristic of the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) should be known. MSA 20.14
With purified vision, with supremely purified morality, concentrated, [and] with splendid <s>dharma</s>-powers;
in the distinction between the defilement and purification of the [mental] continuum; in emanation; with intelligence attained in a single instant. MSA 20.15
Equanimous, purifier of the [Buddha-]field, skilled in the maturation of beings, of great supernatural power,

children.text: saṃpūrṇakāyaśca nidarśane ca śakto 'bhiṣiktaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ // MSA_20.16 //
children.translated_text: with a perfected body, and capable of demonstration — such indeed is the consecrated <s>Bodhisattva</s>. MSA 20.16
Having penetrated the nature of <s>dharma</s>, in the training in superior morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>),
and in superior mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and superior wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>) — but wisdom pertains to [both] domains. MSA 20.17
The reality of <s>dharma</s>, the ignorance of that [reality] and the knowledge [of it], and their [respective] modes of operation —
that is the domain of wisdom; therefore its establishment is on two stages. MSA 20.18
The fruit of the cultivation of the trainings is fourfold, and another [set];
the abode with signs and [mental] formations is the first fruit. MSA 20.19
That very [abode] without [mental] formations is held to be the second fruit;
and purification of the field and the accomplishment of the maturation of beings. MSA 20.20
And the accomplishment of <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīs</s> is the supreme fruit;
this fourfold fruit is based on the four [sets of] stages. MSA 20.21
Having penetrated the nature of <s>dharma</s>, the purification of the morality-aggregate;
and then the purification of the <s>samādhi</s>-aggregate and wisdom-aggregate above that. MSA 20.22
The purification of liberation, liberated-knowledge — [this purification occurs] on the other [stages];
from the fourfold obstruction, including the covering of [mental] resistance. MSA 20.23
All the stages should be known as both unaccomplished and accomplished;
even the accomplished are [in a sense] unaccomplished, and [yet] they are again held to be accomplished. MSA 20.24
Accomplishment should be known through mental attention according to [proper] arrangement;
and through non-conceptualization by [means of] the knowledge of that very conceptualization. MSA 20.25
Cultivation too and accomplishment on all stages are inconceivable,
because they are to be personally experienced, and because they belong to the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. MSA 20.26
Faith, together with vision, is held to be the sign on every [stage];
non-withdrawal, non-dejection, and non-dependence on others. MSA 20.27
And penetration everywhere, equanimity everywhere,
the knowledge of means for guiding and attracting, and birth in the [divine] assembly. MSA 20.28

children.text: nācchando na ca lubdhahrasvahṛdayo na krodhano nālaso nāmaitrīkarūṇāśayo na kumatiḥ kalpairvikalpairhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Not without aspiration, not greedy or small-hearted, not angry, not lazy, not without the intention of loving-kindness and compassion, not of poor intellect or struck by conceptual elaborations,

children.text: no vikṣiptamatiḥ sukhairna ca hato duḥkhairna vā [vyā]vartate satyaṃ mitramupāśritaḥ śrutaparaḥ pūjāparaḥ śāstari // MSA_20.29 //
children.translated_text: not of distracted mind, not overcome by pleasures, not turning away from sufferings — relying on a true friend, devoted to learning, devoted to the worship of the Teacher. MSA 20.29

children.text: sarvaṃ puṇyasamuccayaṃ suvipulaṃ kṛtvānyasādhāraṇaṃ saṃbodhau pariṇāmayatyaharaharyo hyuttamopāyavit /
children.translated_text: Having accumulated all merit, vast and extraordinary, day after day dedicating it to awakening — he who indeed knows the supreme means;

children.text: jātaḥ svāyatane sadā śubhakaraḥ krīḍatyabhijñāguṇaiḥ sarveṣāmuparisthito guṇanidhirjñeyaḥ sa buddhātmanaḥ // MSA_20.30 //
children.translated_text: born in his own domain, always a doer of good, he sports with the qualities of superknowledge — standing above all, a treasury of virtues — he should be known as one of <s>Buddha</s>-nature. MSA 20.30
In <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), the benefit [is held to be] fivefold for each,
for the wise, in every way, on all stages. MSA 20.31
For those who see <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) as near and the accomplishment of beings' welfare,

children.text: tīvra utpadyate modo muditā tena kathyate // MSA_20.32 //
children.translated_text: intense joy arises — therefore it is called <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). MSA 20.32
Because of the purity of freedom from immorality, [the second stage] is called <s>Vimalā</s> (the Stainless);
and because of producing the great radiance of <s>Dharma</s>, [the third is called] <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Luminous). // MSA 20.33 //
Since the <s>dharmas</s> that are the aids to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) become like flames that burn [the afflictions],
[the fourth] is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Radiant), by virtue of that connection, [which burns] the duality. // MSA 20.34 //
The maturation of beings and the protection of one's own mind —

children.text: dhīmadbhirjīyate duḥkhaṃ durjayā tena kathyate // MSA_20.35 //
children.translated_text: by the wise, [this] suffering is conquered [with difficulty]; hence [the fifth] is called <s>Durjayā</s> (the Hard to Conquer). // MSA 20.35 //
Because of being face-to-face with both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
[the sixth] is called <s>Abhimukhī</s> (the Manifest), because of its reliance on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom). // MSA 20.36 //
Because of connection with the single path, [the seventh] stage is considered <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (the Far-Going);
and because of being unshakable from the notion of duality, [the eighth] is called <s>Acalā</s> (the Immovable). // MSA 20.37 //
Because of the excellence of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), [the ninth] stage is considered <s>Sādhumatī</s> (the Good Intelligence);
<s>Dharmameghā</s> (the Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>), because of pervading the duality [of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa], like a cloud in the sky of <s>Dharma</s>. // MSA 20.38 //
In the various excellent accomplishments, because of always dwelling with delight,
the stages of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are considered abodes of dwelling everywhere. // MSA 20.39 //
Again and again, in those immeasurable [stages], through the practice of ascending upward,

children.text: bhūtāmitābhayārthāya ta eveṣṭā hi bhūmayaḥ // MSA_20.40 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of being immeasurable and fearless — those very stages are desired. // MSA 20.40 //
Through attaining the stages, through aspiration,
through engagement in the practices, through penetration, and through the accomplishment of the stages — [the practice] is fourfold. // MSA 20.41 //
For those who have faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and for those beings in the <s>Hīnayāna</s>,
for the purpose of attracting and disciplining both,
the four practices of the resolute [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>] have been taught, in accordance with the <s>sūtras</s>. // MSA 20.42 //
O compassionate one toward beings, [with] the intention of union and separation,
with the intention of non-separation, with the intention of happiness and benefit — homage to you! // MSA 20.43 //
O one freed from all obstructions, O <s>Muni</s> who overcomes all worlds,

children.text: jñānena jñeyaṃ vyāptaṃ te muktacitta namo 'stute // MSA_20.44 //
children.translated_text: the knowable is pervaded by your knowledge, O liberated-minded one — homage to you! // MSA 20.44 //
O destroyer of all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of all beings without remainder,
O striker of afflictions who has compassion for the afflicted — homage to you! // MSA 20.45 //
O one who acts without effort (<s>anābhoga</s>), without attachment, without obstruction, concentrated,

children.text: sadaiva sarvapraśnānāṃ visarjaka namo 'stu te // MSA_20.46 //
children.translated_text: always the resolver of all questions — homage to you! // MSA 20.46 //

children.text: āśraye 'thāśrite deśye vākye jñāne ca deśike /
children.translated_text: In the basis, in the object taught, in the teachings, in the words, in the knowledge, and in the teacher —
O one of unobstructed understanding, always excellent teacher — homage to you! // MSA 20.47 //
Having approached with [appropriate] words, O knower of their conduct, in their coming and going,

children.text: niḥ sāre caiva satvānāṃ svavavāda namo 'stu te // MSA_20.48 //
children.translated_text: and indeed in the essencelessness of beings, O one of excellent counsel — homage to you! // MSA 20.48 //
All embodied beings resort to true manhood upon seeing you;
O one who produces faith from the mere sight [of you] — homage to you! // MSA 20.49 //
In grasping, abiding, relinquishing, transformation, and change,
O one who has attained mastery over <s>samādhi</s> and knowledge — homage to you! // MSA 20.50 //
In skillful means, in refuge, in purity, in the dispute of beings,

children.text: mahāyāne ca niryāṇe mārabhañja namo 'stu te // MSA_20.51 //
children.translated_text: and in the departure through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, O destroyer of <s>Māra</s> — homage to you! // MSA 20.51 //
O teacher of the obstacles to knowledge, abandonment, and departure,
O one invincible to other <s>tīrthyas</s> (sectarians) in one's own and others' benefit — homage to you! // MSA 20.52 //
O one who speaks reprovingly in assemblies, free from the two defilements,

children.text: nirārakṣa asaṃmoṣa gaṇakarṣa namo 'stu te // MSA_20.53 //
children.translated_text: without need of protection, unfailing in memory, O one who attracts assemblies — homage to you! // MSA 20.53 //
In conduct and dwelling, everywhere, there is no action of yours that is not omniscient;

children.text: sarvadā tava sarvajña bhūtārthika namo 'stu te // MSA_20.54 //
children.translated_text: always, O omniscient one, O one who speaks what is true — homage to you! // MSA 20.54 //
In all deeds for the benefit of all beings, you never let the [right] time pass;
O one whose deeds are never fruitless, constantly unfailing — homage to you! // MSA 20.55 //
Six times [daily] you survey the great day-and-night of all worlds;

children.text: mahākaruṇayā yukta hitāśaya namo 'stu te // MSA_20.56 //
children.translated_text: O one endowed with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), of benevolent intention — homage to you! // MSA 20.56 //
In conduct, in attainment, in knowledge, and in action,
O one supreme over all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — homage to you! // MSA 20.57 //
Through the three bodies (<s>kāyas</s>), having attained the great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) of all aspects,

children.text: sarvatra sarvasatvānāṃ kāṅkṣāchida namo 'stu te // MSA_20.58 //
children.translated_text: O one who cuts the doubts of all beings everywhere — homage to you! // MSA 20.58 //
O one without obstruction, without fault, free from impurity, not fixed [in one state],

children.text: āniṅkṣya sarvadharmeṣu niṣprapañca namo 'stu te // MSA_20.59 //
children.translated_text: O one who is beyond conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>) with regard to all <s>dharmas</s> — homage to you! // MSA 20.59 //
You have accomplished the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>), you have emerged from all stages;
having attained the foremost position among all beings, you are the liberator of all beings. // MSA 20.60 //
Endowed with inexhaustible and incomparable qualities, you are seen in the worlds;
yet invisible even in [the divine] circles, in all respects, to gods and humans. // MSA 20.61 //
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, spoken by the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the purified assembly, the twentieth-first chapter on the establishment of practice (<s>caryāpratiṣṭhā</s>).
The <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> is complete.
